title: Printcrime
text:
The coppers smashed my father’s printer when I was eight. I remember the hot, cling-film-in-a-microwave smell of it, and Da’s look of ferocious concentration as he filled it with fresh goop, and the warm, fresh-baked feel of the objects that came out of it.

The coppers came through the door with truncheons swinging, one of them reciting the terms of the warrant through a bullhorn. One of Da’s customers had shopped him. The ipolice paid in high-grade pharmaceuticals—performance enhancers, memory supplements, metabolic boosters. The kind of thing that cost a fortune over the counter; the kind of thing you could print at home, if you didn’t mind the risk of having your kitchen filled with a sudden crush of big, beefy bodies, hard truncheons whistling through the air, smashing anyone and anything that got in the way.

They destroyed grandma’s trunk, the one she’d brought from the old country. They smashed our little refrigerator and the purifier unit over the window. My tweetybird escaped death by hiding in a corner of his cage as a big, booted foot crushed most of it into a sad tangle of printer-wire.

Da. What they did to him. When he was done, he looked like he’d been brawling with an entire rugby side. They brought him out the door and let the newsies get a good look at him as they tossed him in the car, while a spokesman told the world that my Da’s organized-crime bootlegging operation had been responsible for at least twenty million in contraband, and that my Da, the desperate villain, had resisted arrest.

I saw it all from my phone, in the remains of the sitting room, watching it on the screen and wondering how, just how anyone could look at our little flat and our terrible, manky estate and mistake it for the home of an organized crime kingpin. They took the printer away, of course, and displayed it like a trophy for the newsies. Its little shrine in the kitchenette seemed horribly empty. When I roused myself and picked up the flat and rescued my peeping poor tweetybird, I put a blender there. It was made out of printed parts, so it would only last a month before I’d need to print new bearings and other moving parts. Back then, I could take apart and reassemble anything that could be printed.

title: Anda’s Game
text:
Anda didn’t really start to play the game until she got herself a girl-shaped avatar. She was 12, and up until then, she’d played a boy-elf, because her parents had sternly warned her that if you played a girl you were an instant perv-magnet. None of the girls at Ada Lovelace Comprehensive would have been caught dead playing a girl character. In fact, the only girls she’d ever seen in-game were being played by boys. You could tell, cos they were shaped like a boy’s idea of what a girl looked like: hooge buzwabs and long legs all barely contained in tiny, pointless leather bikini-armor. Bintware, she called it.

But when Anda was 12, she met Liza the Organiza, whose avatar was female, but had sensible tits and sensible armor and a bloody great sword that she was clearly very good with. Liza came to school after PE, when Anda was sitting and massaging her abused podge and hating her entire life from stupid sunrise to rotten sunset. Her PE kit was at the bottom of her school-bag and her face was that stupid red color that she hated and now it was stinking maths which was hardly better than PE but at least she didn’t have to sweat.

But instead of maths, all the girls were called to assembly, and Liza the Organiza stood on the stage in front of Miss Cruickshanks the principal and Mrs Danzig, the useless counsellor.

title: الفستان
text: The dress was finished and ready for delivery. Widad stretched out on the floor, allowing her back and neck to rest against a hard surface, hoping to ease the aches in her spine and muscles. No one was home. Her three children were at school, her husband was at work, and her sister-in-law and her husband, with whom she shared the rented apartment, had gone on a family visit. Widad gazed at the dress; it was beautiful, elegant, and distinctive. She felt immense pride and a strong desire to wear it, even though her thin frame would be hidden within the dress, which was tailored to the size of a plump woman in her sixties. She glanced at the clock; there was still some time before someone returned home. She stood before the fitting mirror, removed her clothes, and pulled the dress over her body through the neckline. She inserted a fabric insert in place of her surgically removed breasts. She looked at herself. Her complexion was pale, her body thin, her cheeks sunken, and wrinkles were beginning to etch themselves across her forty-year-old face. She let down her auburn hair and puffed out her cheeks. Then she grasped the hem of her long skirt and began to dance alone in the house without music. She twirled and twirled as if in a mystical trance, and with each spin she remembered a fragment of the past.

title: البحث عن السعادة
text:
In 2013, Umm Alaa began cooking at home and selling her meals on a small scale to cover her rent and her own needs, as well as those of her son, a soldier who was still alive at the time. She continued working alone until 2015, when her landlord decided to raise the rent, completely disregarding the immense grief she was experiencing after the deaths of her two sons. Amidst all this hardship, her neighbor, a first lieutenant in the Political Security Directorate from Jroud, was living a silent love affair with her as its protagonist.

Abu Mudhar, also in his fifties, was divorced and lived alone in a house in Damar al-Balad. His house happened to be directly opposite Umm Alaa's. He would wait for her every morning as she left her house to buy groceries, watching her quietly. It took him a long time before he offered to help her carry her purchases on her way home. Umm Alaa was in her fifties, with a full figure. Despite all she had endured, her face was barely wrinkled. Her kind, shy smile and her well wishes for his success would lift his spirits for days, especially for the single man who had no one to keep him company in his loneliness.

Umm Alaa, for her part, was preoccupied with her own life and absorbed in dealing with loss and pain, so she didn't notice his attention. In truth, she felt a mix of emotions towards him, her gratitude tinged with caution and fear, given that he was, after all, a security officer, even though he seemed a kind and honorable man. This didn't stop her from occasionally bringing him a meal she had cooked.

But their relationship deepened when she faced the problem of a rent increase. Umm Alaa was at her lowest point, and it was then that the man intervened, using persuasion and a touch of intimidation, to reach an acceptable settlement with the landlord, who raised the rent only nominally and allowed Umm Alaa to remain as his tenant.

Umm Alaa hosted her neighbor, Al-Rida, for lunch, defying all her previous convictions about bringing a strange man into her home, and challenging her neighbors, whose disapproval she sensed in their glances. According to custom and law, she was still married, and as a grieving mother, she had no reason to put herself in a position that would make her the subject of gossip.

Umm Alaa laughed as she instructed one of the women rolling grape leaves: "Don't make them too thick, they don't like them that way... Anyway... God is great, it's all destiny. Neither Abu Mudhar nor I cared. We were comfortable and happy. He was a good, simple, and solitary man. We would sit and eat and talk, and we wouldn't even notice the time. Then one day he asked me, 'Will you marry me, Umm Alaa?' And I said yes. Honestly, I didn't marry my husband for love. May God grant him ease if he's alive, and have mercy on him if he's passed away. But I'm alive, and I have the right to relax and enjoy the rest of my life."

Since the personal status law in Syria allows a wife to be divorced and marry another man if her husband is absent for more than a year without her knowing anything about him, the couple had the option to get married. They got married in 2016 and live together in Umm Alaa’s house, after Abu Mudhar moved out and changed the lease to his name and handed over his house.

title: SCP-CN-100
text:
CN-100-1 is a high-energy substance, possibly a three-dimensional projection from a higher-dimensional space. Observations with the naked eye and ordinary optical sensors show that condensed CN-100-1 is a pure black spherical substance, resembling drinking water in a weightless state. Individual humans carry varying amounts of non-condensed CN-100-1, but it is generally inseparable from the body. Specific behaviors of individual humans can cause varying numbers of channels to appear at the quark level, inputting or outputting a certain amount of non-condensed CN-100-1 into or out of the body. Research on the location of these channels is ongoing.

The human body absorbs and carries CN-100-1 without significant negative effects, but collecting condensed CN-100-1 through the human body is not recommended. It is best to use the strong energy field generated by the Symmetra device to collect and move condensed CN-100-1.

When condensed CN-100-1 is "ignited" by the project, the project emits extremely weak gravitational waves, and the gravitational distortion of the surrounding space by the project is slightly enhanced. Although all optical measurements indicate that the project's volume has not increased, its mass will still increase slightly.

Unlike ordinary flames that tend to move towards areas rich in oxidizer, CN-100 will spontaneously move towards areas rich in non-condensed CN-100-1 within a certain range. If a qualified Class D person is placed within 60 meters of the project, the project will slowly move towards that person (at a minimum speed of micrometers), and no obstruction will hinder this movement. If a qualified Class D person is placed in the opposite direction, the project will remain in its original position. If the number of ordinary humans gathered within the [data redacted] range of the project reaches ███ or more, it will have the same effect on the project. It is speculated that when the gathering reaches this scale, the amount of non-condensed CN-100-1 carried by the crowd is equivalent to that of a qualified Class D person.

Any human individual who comes into physical contact with CN-100 will lose complex cognitive abilities, retaining only basic physiological functions. According to information provided by the Kuiyang faction, any biological individual's contact with CN-100 carries an extremely high risk.

title: SCP-CN-173
text:
SCP-CN-173 is a humanoid entity composed of pure black lines. The object is 2 meters tall, with lines 2 centimeters wide. Its head is a circle composed of lines, approximately 20 centimeters in diameter. Two appendages, functioning as arms, connect to the head at the junction of the head and body, with a joint dividing each appendage into two equal-length segments. Similarly, two appendages, functioning as legs, connect to the tail, also with a joint dividing them into two equal-length segments. The body is 80 centimeters long, and the appendages are 100 centimeters long.

Regardless of the viewing direction, SCP-CN-173 always faces the observer in a flat plane. The object exhibits no apparent thickness and does not possess the ability to interfere with conventional physical phenomena. This means that the object cannot physically affect any object and cannot resist any form of force. Nevertheless, no injuries or pain have been observed. Visual analysis of the object's movement indicates that it is still subject to gravity, and its mass is 100 kg.

SCP-CN-173 exhibits certain deductive characteristics and possesses intelligence equivalent to that of a normal human. The object has the ability to speak and is fluent in Chinese, locating the source of sound as below its head. The object is aware of its anomalous nature and is willing to cooperate with containment and experimental procedures; most of its behavior is positive and proactive, but SCP-CN-173 is eager to retrieve SCP-CN-173-1. The object possesses sensory abilities, but the mechanism of these abilities is unknown.

SCP-CN-173-1, as described by SCP-CN-173, is a canvas of unidentified material produced by Dr. Wondertainment. SCP-CN-173-1 possesses the ability to manipulate SCP-CN-173's current form, to which SCP-CN-173 responds that both text and images are effective, suggesting it possesses entirely metaphysical characteristics and a clear deductive nature. After the Foundation expressed a clear commitment to searching for SCP-CN-173-1, SCP-CN-173 expressed a willingness to trust the Foundation, and its attitude improved. If SCP-CN-173-1 is found, it should be handed over to the Foundation's Theory Department for analysis and to develop containment procedures. Due to the possibility of compressing the theory subject and guidance into the same metaspace or creating an illegal loop, SCP-CN-173 should not be allowed to come into contact with SCP-CN-173-1.

title: Jan, Wächter der Koll Sicherheit
text:
Hot coffee in a cup slowly cools. Thick fingers twitch at the cup. Fifteen eyes rest on the other hand. The trigger trembles under the index finger as the barrel is aimed at the first observer. Beads of sweat form on his forehead and catch in his bushy black eyebrows. His eyes widen.

"I almost had him, but he ran into Alex's territory!" The trigger grinds. "I didn't think anyone had gotten him!" The pressure on the trigger slowly eases. Another speaks up. "You had him right in your sights, you could have stopped him." The first one clenches his teeth. Another among the fifteen speaks. "The shot would have been risky. It could have killed him." Slowly, the barrel drops, and the first one takes a deep breath.

title: Schnödder und Höckel
text:
Schnödder: Well, I am concerned about the job security regulations. After all, the new rules could be abused. But in a crisis, such considerations mustn't deter us. We must do everything we can to pull our country out of this crisis.

Höckel: Exactly. And in times like these, businesses must finally be freed from their constraints so they can restore the German economy to its former strength. And they are certainly on the right track. Only without restrictive collective bargaining agreements can we prevent foreign competition from driving out our established companies. Only by adjusting wages to market rates can we retain our employees. I congratulate them on their steadfastness in the face of pressure from the German Trade Union Confederation (DGB). As long as they reduce non-wage labor costs, our economy will fare better, no matter what the doomsayers in the unions try to tell them.

Schnödder: That is our stated goal. We did consider reintroducing the wealth tax, but in the current crisis, that might deter potential investors.

title: कुत्ते के अंडे
text:
A lapwing laid four eggs.

She sat on them every day, incubating them for hours.

She would leave only to eat.

Many days passed like this. Now she was waiting for the chicks to hatch.

She felt very hungry. She covered the eggs with straw. Then she went in search of food.

She returned after some time.

But, what was this!

A dog was lying on the eggs. She waited for the dog to leave.

Morning turned to afternoon. Afternoon turned to evening. But the dog remained lying there.

title: टप-टप-टपक
text:
There was a forest. It was very dense. One day it rained heavily.

The next day the sun came out. All the animals came out. Then came the sound - drip-drip-drip. Everyone got scared.

The lion thought. The leopard thought. The elephant thought. The bear thought.

What kind of sound was that?

The bear got scared. He hid in the bushes. The deer started trembling. He ran away.

The leopard didn't stop there either. The lion said, "I'm not afraid."

But he too slipped away. The big animals ran away with their tails between their legs.

Magione emerged first to the ring, accompanied by the handler wearing the blue and gold colors of the stable. He began to circle, shaking his neck, as if to release the tension. A four-year-old fawn thoroughbred, with a thin, sharp muzzle, he had had a good season in 1953, numerous placings and two victories. Behind him, the handlers introduced the other horses, proud, six feet at the withers, their breath fading in the crisp afternoon air. Giuseppe Marano stroked the neck of his Ninfa, the clear favorite, even though he knew he was the more nervous of the two. He cast a questioning glance at the spectators, then completed the lap, checking the trim for the umpteenth time. The mare snorted a few steps from Lario: she didn't like males. Then Verdi, Augusta, and Redipuglia, also very good, but names good at most for a placing, except that Augusta, on heavy ground, could do well. Until the previous day, before the clear skies of that wintry Sunday, it had rained in Naples and the track was still loose. Monte Allegro, the most nervous of the group, arrived huffing and puffing, ignoring the trainer's voice, who seemed to be whispering something to calm him. Nothing new: Monte Allegro was one of those beasts that were difficult to control, that devour the first thousand meters and collapse at the finish.

In the stands, Salvatore Lucania lit a cigarette and watched the wind carry away the first puff of smoke. He had had to take off his gloves and now almost regretted it: the cold was intense. He turned to Cavalier De Dominicis and said: "But wasn't this the city of the sun? Damn, it's so cold it feels like New York!"

title: Altai
text:
I descended the stairs, skipping the steps. The building's front door had come off its hinges, but was blocked by a pile of rubble. I found a gap and pushed it open. In the street, stunned faces questioned one another, shrouded in frightened silence. The boldest whispered the names of Earthquake and Apocalypse. Entire families abandoned their homes, some leaping from the balconies as if from the sides of a sinking ship.

The second explosion scattered the flock in a cloud of ash and screams. I leaped to the center of the street to avoid an avalanche of tiles, looked up, and saw them. Two gondolas were flying in the Venetian sky. They had wings of flame and uncertain parabolas, like wounded birds. One crashed into the bell tower, which was incessantly ringing the fire alarm. The other disappeared from sight, beyond the curtain of the roofs.

title: 私と煌めく魚
text:
For some reason, many people can't resist throwing coins into any water source within a sacred area, and it's common to find large piles of one-yen and five-yen coins covering the bottom of ponds within the grounds of temples and shrines.

The three small ponds in a corner of the shrine I frequently visit were no exception; a dull shimmer of gold, silver, and copper flickered beneath the surface.

Even if they see divinity in the water, surely sinking so much metal will worsen the water quality. I think it would be much easier for the shrine if they just threw them into the offering box, but deeply ingrained customs rarely change, so there's nothing that can be done.

I often think about these things as I stroll around the shrine grounds, but one day I encountered an unexpected anomaly.

The pile of coins that had been submerged in one of the ponds had vanished. I had stopped by the shrine yesterday as well, and as usual, I peered into the pond as I passed by. At that time, nothing had changed from before. In other words, the bottom of the pond had become clean overnight.

I considered whether it was simply a cleaning, but the coins in the two neighboring ponds were still glittering in the sunlight. Each pond was quite small, small enough to be cleaned all at once in a day. It seemed a little unnatural to dredge the bottom of only this one while leaving the others untouched.

Although it seemed unnatural, it wasn't impossible. But I was drawn to the strange feeling and peered into the pond where the coins had vanished.

Suddenly, I saw something glittering move in the shadow of a rock sticking out in the middle of the pond.

title: 清算の持越し
text:
Even late at night, the bustling downtown area was filled with people and lights, and the woman walked with long strides, her face a frown that seemed out of place amidst the slightly frivolous hustle and bustle.

She glanced around discreetly, occasionally checking her company-issued smartphone. The date and time displayed on the screen was December 31st, 11:06 PM. The seconds continued to tick even as she watched.

"Ah, ah, the new year's almost here,"

She muttered bitterly to herself, slowing her pace.

Even if she could find her target at this very moment, calling for backup from other agents, continuing to tail the target without being noticed until they arrived, and then cornering them in a location where concealment and other post-operative procedures would be less troublesome—it seemed highly unlikely that it could be done within an hour.

(I can't exactly tell you that the New Year won't come for you.)

Putting her device in her coat pocket, the female agent finally stopped beside a street tree.

(Anyway, it's all wishful thinking. I haven't even gotten a single clue.)

Muttering self-deprecatingly, she took off her felt hat and fanned herself. Since the end of the year had arrived, she had been pushing herself too hard, driven by impatience. The fact that she hadn't been able to capture that "doctor" this year, and that she was letting the anomalous objects continue to be produced, was incredibly frustrating and infuriating.

She clicked her tongue and put her hat back on. Should she persevere for another hour, even after the New Year? Or, with her tired legs and eyes, would she even be able to spot anything abnormal? As she hesitated, a yawn welled up inside her. She stifled it, covering her mouth, but wondered if today was a bust.

As she remained undecided, she heard a familiar voice calling out to her from nearby.

title: Радио «Правда»
text:
SCP-1002 is a radio signal of unknown origin detected in and around the city of ██████. Attempts to locate the source have been unsuccessful, and power outages throughout the ██████████ region have also failed.

SCP-1002's broadcast frequency changes randomly, typically within ██ known frequencies. No pattern has been observed in the frequency changes or the duration of its broadcasts.

SCP-1002 transmits information classified as "Top Secret" from various countries, including Foundation materials, trade secrets, and the like. The broadcast language is most often Russian, English, or Chinese, although some dialects have not been identified. The text is read in a monotone, low-pitched male voice. Broadcasts are often sped up tenfold.

The information transmitted by SCP-1002 can be both current and outdated. No instances of it transmitting information about future events have been observed. Between readings of various documents, SCP-1002's "slogan" can sometimes be heard: "Radio Pravda. Everyone should know this!"

title: Денежная стиральная машинка
text:
SCP-1005 appears to be an old wooden washing machine with an electric motor. One of its legs is stamped "Made by Lefty."

This object's unique property is the ability to launder, or legalize, money through a completely unknown and inexplicable means. This effect only applies to bills, coins, and foreign objects (including GPS transmitters) left in the machine. A table is included that specifies, down to the second, how long the machine should be run for each unit of currency. For larger or smaller quantities, the time is proportional. In addition to the money, a slip of paper with the account number of the bank to which the money will be deposited is also included. A list of banks the object works with is also included. Failure to comply with the time limit or an incorrect account will result in either partial or complete loss of the amount, or a smaller amount being transferred to the account.

The stamp "Made by Lefty" on the leg also raises questions. Who this Lefty is and how he created this object is currently unknown.

The procedure for laundering the money is specified in the instructions.

title: La ratonera
text:
It was around seven in the evening when I parked the car in front of her house and got out to open the door for her. Nuria gave me a smile mixed with a kiss, smoothed down her patterned dress, and got out. After opening the gate, she tossed her hair and narrowed her eyes. I inhaled a wave of Eternity.

"Would you like to come in?" she said, somewhere between inviting and challenging.

I felt a few tiny electric shocks in my forearms; then, a remote and fleeting dizziness struck me. I admired her apple-like face, which didn't even betray her mid-twenties, and I felt more married than ever.

"Are your parents home?" I asked.

"No, silly! Nobody's home!" she replied, and burst out laughing.

We entered a small, open patio. On the other side, I could see some windows. We walked arm in arm and went into the living room. It was too big for the furniture; it only had four blue armchairs and a wooden table in front of them.

title: Violetas para Luisa
text:
On my study desk, the page remains blank. The pipe has infused each book with maple, the Martell is almost empty, and I still don't know if I should write you this letter. It's not your new relationship that stops me, but your emotional fragility.

Thirty years into our life together, your illness began, and now this. You'll understand it's too much. Even for me, a fisherman in the river of personal stories.

A few months before you turned sixty, you started forgetting trivial things, like my cell phone number, or the number of suits sent to the dry cleaners.

Now my skin crawls when I think about how we laughed at those lapses… until you omitted some notes while giving your concert at the Japanese embassy. Your tears flowed all night. Morning found you lying on the white sofa, in your purple dress, your eyes blurred with mascara. When you woke up, my hand was caressing yours.

You gave me a look full of melancholy and, smiling, you said as you have so many times: "Life is a novel, you have to live it with passion."

title: Viatu vyangu vya kwanza
text:
I had never worn shoes. When I saw children wearing shoes, I looked at them with longing.

My mother comforted me by saying, “You will have many pairs later, just wait and see!” Sometimes I didn’t believe her. “When will it be later?” I asked her one day.

Then it was Christmas time. Everyone was busy going to the market and returning with new things. “Shall we go to the market, Mom?” I asked her.

The day before Christmas, my mother woke me up earlier than usual. She told me to take the big basket that she usually used to go to the market.

There were many parents at the market with their children. They bought new clothes and a large stock of food.

We went straight to the shoe section. I was surprised to see row after row of neatly arranged shoes.

title: Kalabushe, chiriku
text:
Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Kalabushe. Kalabushe was a chiriku. She was warned by her mother not to talk too much, but she did not listen.

One day, Kalabushe’s aunt, who lived on the other side of Kalabushe’s village, fell ill.

Kalabushe’s mother was very busy that day. When Kalabushe was given food to take to her aunt, it was already evening.

On the way, Kalabushe met a hyena named Sinsou. Sinsaou had turned into a man.

Sinsou asked her what she was carrying. Kalabushe replied, “I am carrying meat, eggs and milk.” Kalabushe had been warned not to say what she was carrying.

Kalabushe also told Sinsou that her aunt was sick and that she was bringing her food. Sinsou drooled when he thought about the meat Kalabushe had brought.

Quickly, Sinsou ran ahead. He went to Kalabushe’s aunt’s house and waited.

He swallowed Kalabushe's aunt and then covered himself with his blanket.

title: NASA's Three-Billion-Mile Journey to Pluto Reaches Historic Encounter
text:
NASA’s New Horizons spacecraft is at Pluto.

After a decade-long journey through our solar system, New Horizons made its closest approach to Pluto Tuesday, about 7,750 miles above the surface — roughly the same distance from New York to Mumbai, India – making it the first-ever space mission to explore a world so far from Earth.

“I’m delighted at this latest accomplishment by NASA, another first that demonstrates once again how the United States leads the world in space,” said John Holdren, assistant to the President for Science and Technology and director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy. “New Horizons is the latest in a long line of scientific accomplishments at NASA, including multiple missions orbiting and exploring the surface of Mars in advance of human visits still to come; the remarkable Kepler mission to identify Earth-like planets around stars other than our own; and the DSCOVR satellite that soon will be beaming back images of the whole Earth in near real-time from a vantage point a million miles away. As New Horizons completes its flyby of Pluto and continues deeper into the Kuiper Belt, NASA’s multifaceted journey of discovery continues.”

“The exploration of Pluto and its moons by New Horizons represents the capstone event to 50 years of planetary exploration by NASA and the United States,” said NASA Administrator Charles Bolden. “Once again we have achieved a historic first. The United States is the first nation to reach Pluto, and with this mission has completed the initial survey of our solar system, a remarkable accomplishment that no other nation can match.”

Per the plan, the spacecraft currently is in data-gathering mode and not in contact with flight controllers at the Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory (APL) in Laurel, Maryland. Scientists are waiting to find out whether New Horizons “phones home,” transmitting to Earth a series of status updates that indicate the spacecraft survived the flyby and is in good health. The “call” is expected shortly after 9 p.m. EDT tonight.

title: NASA Confirms Evidence That Liquid Water Flows on Today's Mars
text:
New findings from NASA’s Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) provide the strongest evidence yet that liquid water flows intermittently on present-day Mars.

Using an imaging spectrometer on MRO, researchers detected signatures of hydrated minerals on slopes where mysterious streaks are seen on the Red Planet. These darkish streaks appear to ebb and flow over time. They darken and appear to flow down steep slopes during warm seasons, and then fade in cooler seasons. They appear in several locations on Mars when temperatures are above minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (minus 23 Celsius), and disappear at colder times.

“Our quest on Mars has been to ‘follow the water,’ in our search for life in the universe, and now we have convincing science that validates what we’ve long suspected,” said John Grunsfeld, astronaut and associate administrator of NASA’s Science Mission Directorate in Washington. “This is a significant development, as it appears to confirm that water — albeit briny — is flowing today on the surface of Mars.”

These downhill flows, known as recurring slope lineae (RSL), often have been described as possibly related to liquid water. The new findings of hydrated salts on the slopes point to what that relationship may be to these dark features. The hydrated salts would lower the freezing point of a liquid brine, just as salt on roads here on Earth causes ice and snow to melt more rapidly. Scientists say it’s likely a shallow subsurface flow, with enough water wicking to the surface to explain the darkening.

title: رغم الثورة.. لا حياة سياسية في إدلب
text:
The question remains: Where are the other leftist and nationalist movements in Syria today? And what about the supporters of the Ba'ath Party? Where have they disappeared to? Or did the end of tyranny also expose the falsehood and hypocrisy of Ba'athist affiliation?

These are questions answered by journalist and political activist Manhal Barish (37 years old), a former member of the opposition People's Democratic Party (formerly the Communist Party - Political Bureau). He tells the story of "What Hasn't Been Told": "Basically, there weren't any movements in the true political sense. They were simply individuals and small groups who couldn't create a broad base of support in Syria. We're talking about political opponents, not an opposition. It was the situation of hundreds and thousands of people who couldn't find a unified front, with the exception of the Damascus Declaration Front (which included nationalists and leftists), which the regime also eliminated by arresting and disposing of its members, thus paralyzing the coalition."

In short, amidst an armed conflict combining sectarian strife, a regime's war against its own people, and regional and international conflicts, Barish believes there is no chance for a leftist movement to be effective, at least in the foreseeable future. Political activity, even within the confines of a democratic system, suffers repression and persecution in areas liberated from the regime to the same degree as in regime-held areas.

As for the Ba'ath Party supporters of today, who once held sway over every aspect of the country, they have either disappeared from public view or retreated into seclusion. "Joining the Ba'ath Party used to provide members with preferential treatment in all kinds of government positions, both civilian and military. They had considerable influence within state institutions," says Muhammad al-Bayoush (50 years old), a former police officer and active Ba'ath Party member who now resides in Kafranbel after his retirement. He has withdrawn from society, trying to distance himself from current events and declaring no support for either the revolution or Assad and his regime.

Manhal Barish points out that a segment of the party's members turned against it, describing it as essentially "a party of self-interest and opportunism. Most of the beneficiaries and mercenaries transformed into regime thugs, reflecting that it wasn't a party in the political sense, but rather that joining was motivated by fear of the authorities." Therefore, Barish argues, it's natural that the revolution exposed the falsity of Ba'ath Party membership, and that the claim of three or four million members is laughable.

This is echoed by revolutionary activist and member of the Union of Revolutionary Offices in Kafranbel, Ahmad Jalal (38 years old), who tells the story of "What Hasn't Been Told": "There are no true Ba'athists, meaning no believers in the Ba'ath Party. They have all disavowed Ba'athism, even those who supported the regime, whose loyalty has now shifted to Bashar al-Assad, not the Ba'ath Party. With the outbreak of the revolution, the Ba'ath Party ceased to exist."

Given the absence of political parties in Idlib, despite the absence of Assad's forces there today, Al-Jalal explains that political parties emerge as a result of the rotation of power, and power in the liberated areas is managed by fighting factions in a manner similar to the emergency system due to the ongoing war in the region. It is an environment that is "unsuitable for the emergence of any political parties, not to mention the factional polarization that has affected most segments. Between supporters and opponents of the faction, a kind of political current is formed that are in conflict over power, sometimes with weapons."

title: تصاعد الجريمة في الساحل السوري
text:
(Latakia) “I was on my balcony at noon making a phone call when I saw a young man I knew on a neighbor’s balcony pull out a Russian rifle and shoot his fiancée and her sister. They fell to the ground instantly. Without stopping, the young man pointed the rifle at his own head and fired, falling dead himself in a pool of blood. When I arrived at their house, the fiancée (whose name was Rana) and the young man who killed her were already dead, while her sister, Hana, was fighting for her life. I carried her and rushed her to the National Hospital. Thank God, she miraculously survived, but the bullet had torn through her internal organs and severed an artery in her leg. She is still in the hospital today.”

This is what engineer Ayman (47 years old), a neighbor of the victim Rana (23 years old), told the story of. Rana never imagined that June 8th, the day the daytime curfew was lifted in Syria due to the coronavirus, would be the last day of her life, and that she would die at the hands of her fiancé.

The reason for the crime was Rana's refusal to return her gold jewelry to her fiancé, with the support of her sister, after she decided to break off their engagement. According to information from the victim's neighbors, he came to the house and asked her sister to leave the kitchen. Then, angrily, he addressed Rana with a single sentence: "Is this your final word?" When Rana replied in a frightened voice, "Yes," the young man responded, "Then return the rings and bracelet to me." The young woman took a breath and told him, "This is my right, and I will not return anything to you." This marked the sixth officially recorded murder on the Syrian coast in a single month.

A few days earlier, a fifteen-year-old boy living in the Saqoubin neighborhood (northern Latakia) shot and killed his father. Another crime occurred in the village of Bdeira (Tartous countryside), where a father, an engineer working at the port, slaughtered his wife and children before attempting suicide. The country was also rocked by a murder and rape in Dreikish (Tartous countryside) committed by two minors. This was followed by a murder in Tartous, where the perpetrator then committed suicide. Meanwhile, the murder of university professor Ahmed Subh, from Tartous and a teacher at Aleppo University, was revealed at the end of May to have been perpetrated by his two sons.

During July, August, and September, three more murders occurred, and there may be other unreported or covered-up murders for various reasons. This is no longer unlikely given the widespread security and social breakdown plaguing the country today.

These incidents have been occurring with increasing frequency for years, with reports circulating of murders on the Syrian coast outside the context of the country's bloody conflict. While this might not seem surprising given the wartime circumstances, a closer examination of the frequency, numbers, spread, and nature of these crimes indicates a significant rise in the rate of murders committed in ways that are gruesome and unusual for these communities. This investigation aims to uncover the types of crimes, their prevalence, and their underlying and immediate causes.

title: 2009年諾貝爾物理獎介紹-光纖與CCD 感光元件
text:
Thanks to modern technological civilization, our lifestyles are constantly transforming, moving towards a new era of considerable convenience and comfort. This year, the 2009 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to three masters in the field of optoelectronic science who spearheaded this new lifestyle movement: American scientist of Chinese descent, Charles K. Kao; American scientist Willard S. Boyle; and Canadian scientist George E. Smith. They all converted light into electronic signals, thus profoundly transforming industry and human life.

Charles K. Kao (born in Shanghai, China in 1933, the father of fiber optics, and former president of the Chinese University of Hong Kong) spearheaded the use of glass optical fibers as the medium for light wave transmission, significantly extending the transmission distance of optical signals. The achievements of fiber optic communication have enabled the ubiquitous reach of the internet today; fiber optics have shrunk the world into a village. Without fiber optic communication, there would be no internet age. Nobel laureate in Physics Charles K. Kao: "The Father of Fiber Optics" has brought the world closer together. The internal structure of fiber optics can be divided into a core of high-refractive-index glass and a surface layer coated with a low-refractive-index material. The principle is that light propagates in the core, utilizing the fact that the refractive index of the glass is greater than that of the surface layer, allowing light to propagate through total internal reflection. Normally, light attenuates within the glass due to absorption and scattering by impurities. However, in 1966, Kao Kuen confirmed the correlation between impurity concentration and light attenuation. Scientists then continuously produced high-purity glass, improving signal attenuation and successfully reducing signal transmission attenuation to 0.15 decibels per kilometer, enabling light signals to travel over 100 kilometers. Besides its applications in communications, optical fibers are also used in medical endoscopes and as signal lines for instruments.

In 1969, Willard S. Boyle and George E. Smith jointly invented the Charge-Coupled Device (CCD), an integrated circuit that can convert optical images into electronic digital signals in a short time, facilitating modern photography and telemetry technologies. The development of CCDs replaced the function of traditional film, storing optical images as digital information, leading to the development of modern digital cameras. Charge-coupled devices (CCDs) utilize photoelectric coupling technology, where light is converted into electronic signals through the photoelectric effect. Originally invented as memory devices, they utilize the photoelectrons generated by semiconductors exposed to light to charge CCDs, thus creating digital images. These images are stored using CCDs, captured electronically, replacing the function of traditional film and storing images as digital signals. CCDs have led to the widespread use of digital cameras today, changing people's lifestyles. CCDs have revolutionized photography, making digital image processing and transmission more convenient. These photosensitive elements are used in optical scanners and cameras, and are also widely used in medical and astronomical instruments.

title: 2008年台北国际听障运动邀请赛 地主展现成果 泰国笑到最后
text:
Yesterday (September 10th) was the final day of the 2008 Taipei International Deaflympics Invitational Tournament. Besides table tennis and martial arts (judo, karate, and taekwondo), football was the last event to determine the rankings.

In the martial arts events, which concluded earlier on the third day (September 8th), European and Asian powerhouses demonstrated their strength. Even in judo, a knockout in six seconds caught the attention of spectators. Ultimately, the Chinese Taipei team performed best in taekwondo and karate; South Korea, in judo, repeatedly used technical points and knockouts to outmaneuver European and Japanese powerhouses.

In the final football match, Thailand and Japan faced off in a high-level championship game. In the 20th minute, Shifang Hengxian capitalized on a positioning error by the opposing goalkeeper, Theerawat Hansamer, taking a free kick from behind the halfway line and scoring to give Japan a 1-0 lead. However, before halftime, Somsak Thongdee capitalized on a lapse in defense to equalize at 1-1.

In the second half, Thailand's captain, Anothai Sathiyamat, transferred the lead to Thailand in the 60th minute, putting them ahead 2-1. Although Japan intensified their counter-attacks, it was too late, and Thailand secured the gold medal in football.

In the bronze medal match, Iran, leveraging their superior overall strength, easily won 8-0 thanks to goals from Mostafa Heydaribondarabadi, Hosseinali Mohammadi Firouzjaei, Mazaher Shirzad Sibani, and Hamid Reza Khazaei.

At the closing ceremony, the event's president and Taipei Mayor Hau Lung-bin stated, "This competition has showcased the results of the Deaflympics' preparations, including the performance of participating countries and the administrative efforts of the organizing committee. Although some countries participated as a training exercise, we hope that all countries will deliver their best performance in next year's official Deaflympics."

Following the event, Chen Chih-ho, President of the Asia-Pacific Federation of Deaf Sports, presented a medal of appreciation to the Taipei City Government, encouraging the city's organizing team to demonstrate the highest quality of service at next year's Deaflympics.

title: Augsburg: Pressekonferenz zum Polizistenmord
text:
Augsburg (Germany), November 30, 2011 – A press conference regarding the murder of two police officers in Augsburg's Siebentischwald forest was held on Friday at the Swabia North Police Headquarters. Police and prosecutors believe the two brothers, aged 56 and 58, were planning a robbery when they were stopped by the two police officers for questioning. The 56-year-old brother had previously murdered an Augsburg police officer in 1975. To avoid prosecution, they allegedly opened fire on the 30-year-old female police officer and the 41-year-old male police officer with two weapons.

The press conference began with speeches by Bavarian Justice Minister Beate Merk (CSU), followed by Bavarian Interior Minister Joachim Herrmann (CSU). Merk stated that the state must take a stand, which is why she and Minister Herrmann were present: "The government will not abandon the police." She added that she had long campaigned for an increase in the maximum penalty for resisting arrest, which had ultimately been achieved, but that some issues still needed to be addressed. She thanked the investigators and said, "There is strong evidence that the two cowardly murderers have been caught."

Minister Herrmann praised the work of the special task force "Soko Spickel," noting that up to 53 officers had been working on the case simultaneously at times. He expressed his hope that if the suspicion against the 56-year-old perpetrator is confirmed, he will remain behind bars for life. The suspect has already served an 18-year sentence for the murder of a police officer, a crime committed in 1975.

title: Europaweite Protestaktionen gegen ACTA
text:
Berlin (Germany), February 11, 2012 – Internet users are taking to the streets today in many cities across Germany and Europe. In Germany, protests against the ACTA agreement are taking place in 60 cities.

The Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement (ACTA) is an international trade agreement. The participating nations aim to establish international standards in the fight against product piracy and copyright infringement through ACTA.

Germany has announced that it will not sign the agreement for the time being, joining the ranks of countries that have expressed concerns. However, no final decision has yet been made. The Green Party, the Left Party, and the Pirate Party see the postponement as a victory. These parties are staunch opponents of the agreement and fear significant restrictions on civil liberties. In France, a monitoring authority has already been established. It is called the High Authority for the Diffusion of Works and the Protection of Rights on the Internet (Hadopi). It can block people from using the internet for up to a year. Providers and rights holders cooperate directly with each other there. The United Kingdom is planning something similar.

title: जलाधिकार सत्याग्रह
text: The Jal Satyagraha began today at Rajghat, and then a group of social activists, women's groups, water panchayats, farmers' groups, and water friends, all supporting the Satyagraha, joined the march to Jantar Mantar. At Jantar Mantar, the march swelled into a mass of several thousand people, including representatives of various voices from 13 drought-affected states. Manish, from the Chambal region, joined the march. Manish has contributed to the villagers' work in Palera village, Tikamgarh, to build a stop dam to conserve rainwater. According to Magsaysay Award recipient Rajendra Singh, water-rich land must be preserved for water. We are snatching away water-rich land and depleting the earth's stomach. As long as the earth's stomach remains empty, water cannot be recharged. Rivers and sewers must be separated. Rainwater must be separated from drain flows. The politics of mixing drain water and drinking water is, in fact, the same dirty politics. Funds can be obtained from the World Bank to clean the sewage. I've seen this misuse with my own eyes. I've seen thirty sewage treatment plants built, costing millions of rupees, yet they're not working today.

title: फरक्का हटाओ, बिहार बचाओ
text:
The Farakka Barrage has filled the Ganga's belly with silt, causing Bihar to suffer the devastation of floods every year. In reality, the Ganga's disease lies within its belly, and the treatment is occurring along its banks. Without dismantling the Farakka Barrage, neither can Bihar be saved from floods nor can the Ganga's uninterrupted flow be maintained.

Bihar Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has scheduled a meeting at the end of this month with national and international experts to discuss the Ganga floods and the Farakka Barrage. Nitish Kumar says the Indian government should close Farakka or implement a system to contain the silt, preventing the Ganga's flow from being disrupted. Chief Minister Nitish Kumar told Yathavat that he has spoken to Prime Minister Narendra Modi twice about Farakka. The uninterrupted flow of the Ganga has been disrupted at Farakka. Because of Farakka, the Ganga's belly is filled with silt. Bihar faces the terror of floods every year. To avoid this, Farakka Dam will have to be demolished.

title: In tutta Italia il V-Day contro i parlamentari condannati
text:
Other political figures, such as Walter Veltroni, mayor of Rome, have openly supported the initiative. Grillo also conducted a survey of 209 MPs, finding 122 politicians in favor of reinstating direct preference (abolished with the electoral law reform promoted by the center-right during the previous legislature), 109 in favor of ineligibility for convicted candidates, and 82 in favor of limiting them to two terms in office.

The center of the demonstration was Bologna, where Beppe Grillo was present, along with other figures who criticize or mock the political world, such as Alessandro Bergonzoni, Sabina Guzzanti, Peter Gomez, and Marco Travaglio, as well as singers such as Gianna Nannini, Luciano Ligabue, who submitted a video testimony, and Biagio Antonacci. Musicians, comedians, and witnesses, such as the Calabrian youth of the "Ammazzateci Tutti" movement and the parents of Federico Aldrovandi, took turns on the stage. By early afternoon, despite the heat, twenty thousand people had gathered in Piazza Maggiore, completely occupying it and clogging many surrounding streets. Long lines could be seen at the signature collection points. The stage was set up with its back to the city hall, and the absence of any political symbols was noticeable, testifying to the demonstration's total apolitical nature. Only three banners were present in the square: one read "Fuck you" in marker, while the second read "Class action." The third read "Clementina Forleo, we are with you." Forleo is the Milan judge who submitted a request to Parliament to use the wiretaps that sparked the Bancopoli scandal in investigations into the summer 2005 takeovers. Indeed, the use of wiretaps of MPs requires Parliamentary authorization.

Three stands were set up in Milan: in Piazza Cordusio near Sottovia Mercanti, in Piazza San Babila, and on Viale Papiniano. Also in Milan, Infrastructure Minister Antonio Di Pietro signed the bill, stating that "those convicted with a final criminal sentence cannot be candidates. Criminals should be sent home, not to Parliament." The minister also said that similar bills have been proposed in the past, but Parliament "doesn't want to listen."

Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, present today in Bari for the inauguration of the Fiera del Levante, took a different view. When asked by volunteers to sign the bill as they exited, the prime minister refused to respond and instead drove to the airport.

The Green Party Federation also provided concrete support for Grillo's initiative: a stand was set up at the Festa dei Verdi in Rome to collect signatures, while the party's television station was made available to promote the initiative.

title: In Valle di Susa i manifestanti impediscono i sondaggi per la costruzione della ferrovia TAV
text:
Residents of the Susa Valley demonstrated today against the surveys for the construction of the high-speed railway. The deployment of law enforcement to protect the geologists was incredible: around 11 a.m., approximately 1,200 police officers, Carabinieri, and Guardia di Finanza (Italian Fire Brigade) were deployed. All this was to allow access to the three sites in the Mompantero mountains above Susa (Piedmont) and begin the surveys, which effectively represent the beginning of the project.

They were stopped by the valley residents, led by administrators, always at the forefront, wearing tricolor sashes, to avoid the most violent charges. The entire mountain was patrolled by more or less large groups, able to move according to the reports of police sightings, communicated via cell phones. Already during the night, many protesters had settled on the mountain, blocking the road at several points, erecting barricades, and knocking down rocks and trees to stop the armored vehicles. The key point of the day was a small bridge at the beginning of the road, where protesters and police officers jostled all day, with mayors at the forefront. The risk of falling from the five-meter-wide, ten-meter-high, and, most importantly, unguarded bridge, and the interposition of the mayors, courageously squeezed between the two opposing crowds, prevented the widespread use of smoke bombs and truncheons.

The confrontation then moved to the survey sites, which many protesters reached by bypassing the police roadblocks and skillfully exploiting the ancient mule tracks that were the scene of partisan battles 60 years ago. 500 protesters managed to push back the Carabinieri from the valley, just 20 meters from their destination. After several futile attempts to charge, the Carabinieri defused the tension by partially removing their helmets and accepting sweets and candy from the protesters.

Other police officers were blocked on an access road to the site by a large barricade of logs and brambles, manned by a handful of mayors wearing tricolor sashes. Meanwhile, the entire municipal area of Mompantero was blocked to prevent other Val di Susa residents from accessing and assisting. All factories in the valley were blocked in solidarity, and the railway line was interrupted by other protesters for several hours, while the municipalities of Carrara and Ferrara were occupied in solidarity with the Val di Susa residents.

Around 5:00 PM, police officers on both sides withdrew, followed by protesters about an hour later. The day's toll included several injuries and four arrests.

For today, the protesters have won a battle that has been going on for about a decade, to defend the territory from a project considered unnecessary by residents, as well as dangerous and damaging to the image and economy of the valley's towns. However, it is reported that experts managed to take possession of the sites overnight and begin surveys.

title: スマートフォンアプリ「Pokémon GO」日本でも公開開始 - 政府が注意喚起も
text:
In Indonesia, the use of smartphones by government and other public institution employees at work has been prohibited due to security and confidentiality concerns. Furthermore, the manager of Manchester United FC (England) has instructed players to refrain from using smartphones for 48 hours before matches.

Following incidents and accidents in the United States and other countries, Japan's National Cyber Security Center also issued warnings before the release of its content, urging people to "avoid using smartphones while walking," "avoid playing in dangerous places," "pay attention to the weather," and "be careful of heatstroke." Chief Cabinet Secretary Yoshihide Suga stated that "it is gratifying that Japanese content is widely enjoyed around the world," but added that "we hope people will follow the precautions for safe smartphone use." Additionally, JR West President Tatsuo Kijima stated at a press conference that "we need to consider how to raise awareness to prevent accidents on trains and platforms," indicating that they will consider measures to prevent accidents. Osaka Mayor Hirofumi Yoshimura has also indicated his intention to strengthen warnings against using smartphones while walking on subways and buses. Following the incident in the United States where a boy trespassed onto the grounds of a nuclear power plant, the Nuclear Regulation Authority has also called on Japanese power companies to strengthen security. Izumo Taisha Shrine (Izumo City, Shimane Prefecture) and Kotohira-gu Shrine (Kotohira Town, Kagawa Prefecture) have posted notices on their websites and elsewhere advising people not to play on their grounds, while Tomioka Silk Mill (Tomioka City, Gunma Prefecture) has installed signs that read, "Please be careful of restricted areas and accidents, and be considerate of your surroundings." Keta Taisha Shrine (Hakui City, Ishikawa Prefecture) has also prohibited the use of the game on its grounds and has asked the operating company to remove it from its list of points of interest. Deputy Chief Priest Mitsui Takahide said, "There are stairs at the shrine, and I think it is dangerous to play 'Pokémon GO' there," adding, "We will continue to take care to prevent injuries." The operating company has also issued a warning that accounts are being bought and sold on internet auctions. In an interview with NHK, the operating company stated, "The buying and selling of accounts, which is prohibited by the terms of service, is illegal, and if discovered, we may delete the accounts or take legal action. We want people to enjoy the game while following the rules."

title: 香川県さぬき市で2014年の「あばれみこし」が行われ、衆議院議員の玉木雄一郎氏も池へ落とされる
text:
According to the Shikoku Shimbun, on October 12, 2014, a "bizarre festival" called the "Abare Mikoshi" ritual was held at Tsukahara Inari Shrine in Nagao-nishi, Sanuki City, Kagawa Prefecture. This ritual is designated as an "Intangible Folk Cultural Property" by Sanuki City.

According to the Shikoku Shimbun, this festival is the autumn festival of Tsukahara Inari Shrine, held to pray for good health and a bountiful harvest, and boasts a tradition of over 100 years. Young people with heavy makeup carried simple portable shrines made of wood and bamboo, running back and forth. Finally, they jumped into a pond. Some young people were thrown into the pond along with spectators, and their wild antics drew loud cheers.

Yuichiro Tamaki, a member of the House of Representatives from the Democratic Party, also participated in the festival and, like the other spectators, was mercilessly thrown into the pond. In an interview with a Wikinews reporter, Representative Tamaki said, "I've been thrown into the pond every year for the past seven or eight years. This year I was thrown in five or six times," and "The water in the pond was colder this year compared to last year."

title: В 2019 году на «Алые Паруса» собралось более 33 тысяч выпускников
text:
On the night of June 23-24, the Scarlet Sails festival took place in St. Petersburg. According to organizers, more than 33,000 graduates participated, and the event was attended by over 1.4 million people.

In addition to the main concert, which began on Palace Square at 10:00 PM, a "youth program" featuring performances by lesser-known artists and groups was prepared for the graduates. This program performed before the main show, as the graduates gradually gathered on the square, and again later that night, after the fireworks.

This year's concert headliners were Sergey Lazarev and Polina Gagarina.

Also performing for the graduates were Marcus Riva, the band #2Mashi, Zara, Kravts, #Lera, Vladimir Presnyakov, Burito, Yulia Parshuta, Alekseev, and the band Marsel.

At the beginning of the concert, Acting Governor of St. Petersburg Alexander Beglov addressed the graduates with parting words.

Ivan Urgant and Dasha Alexandrova hosted the concert.

The show concluded with the appearance of a ship with scarlet sails on the Neva. This year, it was the brig "Rossiya." It replaced the Swedish vessel "Tre Kronor af Stockholm," which had been the symbol of the festival for the past nine years. The brig was based on the hull of a former Dutch fishing seiner, built in 1958. It was originally named "ORA ET LABORA" ("Pray and Work"). In 2005, the ship was completely refitted, becoming a sailing vessel named "Mercedes." In May of this year, it was purchased by a Russian company and given its current name.

title: В Подмосковье вместо закрытия незаконной свалки фабрикуют дела на активистов
text:
The Russian Ministry of Defense has issued a written demand for immediate measures to close the Aleksinskaya landfill in the city of Klin in the Moscow Region. The closure is attributed to swarms of birds attracted by the 30-hectare waste pile, which is paralyzing operations at the strategic Klin-5 airfield of the Russian Aerospace Forces (military unit 45095-A), located 3 km away. Until the landfill is closed and reclaimed, the birds could cause aviation tragedies, which would compromise flight safety and the safety of the city's residents. Current legislation prohibits the placement of landfills and waste disposal sites within the 15-kilometer approach zone of airfields. There have already been incidents of aircraft crashing into high-rise buildings and private residential buildings in Klin.

Instead of closing the landfill, municipal authorities have allowed direct transit of road trains carrying waste across an unfinished highway, which is expected to be completed in 2020. The volume of waste disposed of ranges from 300 to 800 20-ton garbage trucks per day. Currently, this "road" is a clearing in the forest with slabs laid down. More than 30 hectares of protective forest were cleared in 2018 to construct it, which leads solely to the landfill.

The authorities are thus making it clear that they have no intention of closing the illegal landfill. Instead, they plan to expand it and construct a waste processing plant in a densely populated area, in violation of environmental regulations. Furthermore, there is no valid state environmental assessment, and the federal register of waste disposal facilities (GRORO) and the regional Territorial Waste Management Scheme contain false information about the landfill's area, capacity, and actual load. This, coupled with the proximity of an active airfield, clearly indicates that the continued operation of the landfill, much less its expansion, is illegal. Due to multiple exceedances of limits, violations of disposal technology, lack of waste refilling, and other deviations from design specifications, the recorded airborne concentration of harmful substances in Klin exceeds the maximum permissible concentration by 80 times with an easterly wind; with other wind directions, residents of nearby villages and towns suffer. Residential buildings are located 400 meters from the landfill, and the Yedunov Secondary School and the Oduvanchik Kindergarten are less than a kilometer away.

title: López Obrador asume la presidencia de México
text:
This Saturday (December 1st), the six-year term of President Enrique Peña Nieto, of the Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), came to an end, and he was succeeded by Andrés Manuel López Obrador, of Morena, with a ceremony at the San Lázaro Legislative Palace during a joint session of Congress. According to El País, he is the first left-wing president in Mexico in recent years.

The joint session of Congress began after 9:00 a.m. local time, with 448 members of the Chamber of Deputies and 110 senators present. The resolutions of the Solemn Proclamation, issued by the Chamber of Deputies on September 6th, were read aloud, followed by the appointment of committees of legislators tasked with escorting the newly inaugurated presidents to and from the Legislative Palace.

Subsequently, legislators representing the various parliamentary groups in Congress spoke for up to ten minutes each. Raúl Bolaños Cacho Cué, of the Green Party of Mexico, stated that "It is time to act in unity for the benefit of the country. [...] It is in our hands to consolidate this fourth transformation," referring to the fourth transformation promised by López Obrador, a profound change for the country following the Revolution, the Reform War, and Independence.

Miguel Ángel Mancera, former Head of Government of Mexico City, assured that the party he represents, the Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), "will not be an obstacle to the change that has been proposed for our nation," adding that they hope the new president "will fulfill each and every one of his campaign promises." Following this, Geovanna del Carmen Bañuelos de la Torre, of the Labor Party (PT), stated that they are "proud to have nominated López Obrador [as a presidential candidate] three times," as their party supported the leftist in all three of his presidential bids.

"We reiterate our call to leave behind division and build true national unity," stated Fernando Luis Manzanilla of the Social Encounter Party, while Clemente Castañeda Hoeflich, representing the Citizens' Movement, affirmed their "commitment to the citizens [...] we welcome the President of the Republic to this parliamentary chamber." On behalf of the PRI, René Juárez Cisneros asserted that "we will never be on our knees" and reiterated his recognition of former President Peña Nieto.

title: Miles piden paz y justicia en la Ciudad de México
text:
Thousands of citizens participated in the National March for Justice and Peace, also known as the March of Silence, in Mexico City, led by poet Javier Sicilia. The group departed last Thursday from Cuernavaca, located 90 kilometers from the Mexican capital, and arrived Sunday afternoon at the country's main square, the Zócalo. The protesters demanded justice and peace in the face of the insecurity plaguing many parts of Mexico and the "war" declared by President Felipe Calderón against criminal organizations, which has left an estimated 40,000 victims and 10,000 missing persons. Sicilia concluded the event, after three days of walking, by calling for justice from the authorities and the resignation of Genaro García Luna, Mexico's Secretary of Public Security.

Wikinews consulted police and civil protection authorities, who confirmed that some 150,000 people arrived at the Zócalo, the site where Javier Sicilia delivered a speech demanding decisive action from the political class and proposing an electoral boycott in 2012, since, he accused, political parties of having members who negotiate with criminals.

"If we have walked and arrived like this, in silence, it is because our pain is so great and so deep, and the horror from which it stems so immense, that we no longer have words to express it. It is also because through this silence we tell ourselves, and we tell those responsible for the security of this country, that we do not want one more death because of this growing confusion that only seeks to suffocate us, as it suffocated the breath and life of my son Juan Francisco, of Luis Antonio, of Julio César, of Gabo, of María del Socorro, of Commander Jaime, and of so many thousands of men, women, children, and elderly people murdered with a contempt and vileness that belong to worlds that are not and never will be ours," the poet said in his message.

Before concluding and asking for five minutes of silence for all the victims, Sicilia announced the upcoming signing in Ciudad Juárez of the pact "For a Peaceful, Just, and Secure Mexico," which contains six points. Among these points is a demand that authorities resolve, within three months, six of the most emblematic cases of Felipe Calderón's presidency: the execution of Juan Francisco's son, Sicilia's own son; the execution of 14 young people and two adults in Villas de Salvárcar, who were later determined to have been mistaken for drug cartel members; the murder of Rubí Fraire and her mother, Marisela Escobedo, which occurred in front of the Chihuahua State Government Palace; the murder of Benjamín LeBarón for denouncing kidnapping activities; and the 49 children who died in the ABC Daycare fire.

“If we have marched and arrived like this, in silence, it is because our pain is so great and so deep, and the horror from which it stems so immense, that we no longer have words to express it.”

“The pact we are calling for, after gathering many proposals from civil society, and which Olga Reyes, who has suffered the murder of six family members, will read in a few moments, is a pact that contains six fundamental points that will allow civil society to closely monitor its implementation and, in the event of any betrayal, to hold those responsible accountable,” the poet said.

The President of the Republic expressed respect for the march and its participants on Saturday, to which the opposition parties to Felipe Calderón responded with criticism. Sicilia accused the political class itself of creating “the mess,” urging them to listen to the citizens’ demands in silence.

title: Tanzania: Ulimwengu wa Blogu Wachambua Kampeni za Uchaguzi Mkuu 2010
text:
On October 31, 2010, more than 19.6 million Tanzanians will make a crucial decision about the future of their country. They will do so through the fourth general election under a multi-party system. With just days left before the election, the Tanzanian blogosphere is also closely following the developments in the various parties’ campaigns.

Among the exciting features of this year’s campaign is the fact that many university students appear unlikely to be able to vote. Senior journalist Ndimara Tegambwage, who runs a blog called Uhuru Hauna Kikomo, explains the matter:

…Thousands of students from government universities registered to vote at their campuses. The ministry knew this. The Electoral Commission knew this and planned accordingly. The students knew they would be at the campuses (usually the campuses open in late September or early October, but this year the government has decided that the campuses will open in November). The government generally knew this …

He describes the experience in other countries:

.. In some countries around the world, there are systems to ensure that their citizens living abroad participate in the election process in their home country. The government ensures that every vote is counted.

title: Tanzania: Kufungiwa ‘Mwanahalisi’, uhuru wa habari mashakani?
text:
The Tanzanian media community has been shocked by the closure of the weekly newspaper ‘MwanaHalisi‘. A Government statement published on the Wavuti blog briefly stated that

The Government has decided to indefinitely suspend the publication of the newspaper MwanaHalisi, in accordance with the Newspapers Act of 1976, Section No. (25) (i), with effect from 30 July 2012, in accordance with Government Notice No. 258 published in the Government Gazette and issued in Dar es Salaam on 27 July 2012.

The statement added:

The Government calls on owners, editors and journalists to adhere to the law, patriotism, professionalism and ethics of the journalism profession in carrying out their duty to inform, educate and entertain the public.

Through its statement, the Government gives the reason for closing the newspaper as ‘writing news and articles of incitement, hostility and fabrication with the intention of causing the citizens to lose faith in state institutions, a situation that could endanger the peace and solidarity that exists in the country’.

Professor Joseph Mbele, who owns a blog called Hapa Kwere, wrote his opinion on the news of the closure of the MwanaHalisi newspaper, saying:

The government would have been wise, it would have seriously considered these issues of Dr Ulimboka as reported by MwanaHalisi. Banning this newspaper, I feel, will reinforce the widespread notion in society that the government is involved in the attack against Dr Ulimboka. It is possible that the government is not involved, but these actions could be detrimental to the government itself.

He concludes by writing:

Let me conclude by saying that I am offended by the actions that undermine my right to read what I want to read. I am an adult and I have my own mind. I can analyze whatever I read. When the government bans a newspaper or bans a book, I see it as an insult to the citizens, that they do not have the mind to read and analyze things.

title: Fight Off Food Poisoning
text:
Several types of bacteria can also cause food poisoning. Some foods you buy—such as raw meat or fruits and vegetables—may already contain bacteria that you need to wash off or cook to destroy. Bacteria can also thrive in certain foods if not stored properly.

Bacteria like Staph and Bacillus cereus can make you sick quickly, within 1 to 7 hours. These bacteria produce fast-acting toxins in foods (such as meat or dairy for Staph, and starchy foods like rice for B. cereus). Keeping such foods refrigerated at 40 °F or colder helps slow or stop the growth of these bacteria.

Other bacteria, such as Salmonella and Campylobacter, don’t make you sick until they get in your body and multiply. With these microbes, it can take 12 hours or a few days for you to feel ill. “Symptoms can include fever, cramps, and sometimes bloody diarrhea,” says O’Brien.

When you have a foodborne illness, you usually need to drink plenty of fluids. “But see a doctor if you have blood in your stool,” O’Brien advises. “And if a child seems to have food poisoning, you should have the child seen by a doctor.”

title: Better Nutrition Every Day
text:
“Healthier diets don’t have to cost more, provided that you have the right attitude, make the right food choices, and try to cook at home,” says Dr. Adam Drewnowski, a nutrition expert at the University of Washington in Seattle. With some planning, he says, you can prepare meals that are tasty, affordable, and nutrient rich.

Get the whole family to help slice, dice, and chop. NIH has developed several resources to help you learn how to cut unhealthy fats and calories (see the Web Links box). You might be surprised how easy healthy cooking and snacking can be.

Unfortunately, these days much of our food isn’t eaten at home. It’s eaten on the go. One easy way to eat more nutritiously is to pack healthy lunches—both for yourself and your kids.

“You can work with your child to make a lunch using whole-grain bread, wraps, or pita pockets filled with lean meats or cheese, vegetables, and nut butters or spreads, such as hummus,” de Jesus says. “Pack vegetables such as carrots, snap peas and cucumbers, or any fresh fruit that’s currently in season. Teens can learn to pack their own lunches with a healthy variety of foods.”

title: رائحة كعك العيد تطغى على رائحة البارود في إدلب
text:
Making Eid cakes is one of the most important and enduring traditions of the Eid holidays in Idlib city and its surrounding countryside. It sees a surge in popularity with the arrival of the holidays, as almost every home has these sweets, which are considered a staple in the hospitality offered to those celebrating.

Yellow cakes and cakes made with oil are the most popular in large areas of northern Syria. Over the years, they have remained a staple, although some of their ingredients have changed due to economic circumstances. However, they have maintained their quality and taste.

Mrs. Fatima Al-Naeem (37 years old) tells the story of how these sweets are prepared: "Making cakes at home requires special skill and experience in preparing the dough. The type and quantity of spices added to the flour are the key to the deliciousness of the cakes."

She adds, "The dough for these cookies is made with flour, ghee, and oil, along with a wide variety of spices, including mahlab, sesame seeds, fennel, nigella seeds, and nutmeg, as well as ginger, cinnamon, and anise. The dough is then shaped into long ropes, rolled into a circular shape, and baked in the oven. We can't imagine Eid without these ingredients because they remind us so much of our childhood and the family gatherings of the past. We also make these cookies to bring joy to our children, whose lives have been worn down by the harshness of war."

Idlib and its surrounding countryside are famous for their long list of ready-made sweets and pastries, prepared for the holidays. Some shops specialize in these treats, known for their delicious taste and rich variety of nuts, such as baklava, barazek, warbat, and qatayef. However, these shops are closed to the poor, who cannot afford them due to their high prices, and sales are limited to those who are well-off.

"It pains me to see my children eagerly awaiting Eid, and I am unable to bring them happiness and joy." This is what Umm Mohsen (39 years old), displaced from the northern Hama countryside, told us, tears welling in her eyes. She explained that after her husband's death, they could no longer afford to buy Eid sweets because there was no one to provide for them.

Khaled al-Mansour (44 years old), owner of a shop in Kafranbel, noted that business was slow this year for several reasons, most notably the systematic bombing of markets and crowded areas. He added that a large number of people had been displaced due to the intense shelling of their towns and villages, and some families lacked the money to buy sweets and new clothes for Eid. He pointed out that last year, around this time, the markets were bustling with people buying sweets and other necessities, even though prices this year were similar to last year.

Despite the bombing, displacement, and forced migration, the people of Idlib and its surrounding countryside still celebrated Eid. The aroma of sweets wafted from their windows, overpowering the smell of fire and gunpowder.

title: أغلى من الذهب.. يا موز
text:
Most Syrian homes at that time were quite similar: the same blankets, cups and mugs, spoons and plates, matchboxes, tissue boxes, baby wipes, and tea biscuits if available. The source was also the same: government-subsidized consumer cooperatives, established to address the severe shortages of food and essential goods.

The missing items were also the same: tomatoes sometimes, lemons sometimes, but bananas were an unattainable dream for all Syrians, from the middle class to the poor. Only the lucky ones could afford bananas once or twice a year, as they were only available through smuggling and were prohibitively expensive for government employees. Government salaries at the time did not exceed 2,000 Syrian pounds (approximately $400), while a kilogram of bananas could cost up to 150 Syrian pounds (approximately $15), depending on their scarcity and origin. However, Ammar's father, a government employee at the General Organization for Social Insurance and Pensions, always tried to find a way to get a kilo of bananas for his children, Ammar, Hania, and Hassan. Sometimes Ammar would even share his portion with his siblings, as he wasn't particularly fond of bananas. He couldn't understand why they were harder to obtain than potatoes, which he loved in all their forms—fried, boiled, or roasted—and why eating them was so expensive. Even cucumbers were more refreshing and enjoyable for him than bananas.
