The family had to eat bananas secretly on rare occasions so as not to tempt the neighbors and their children and surprise them with an unexpected visit, as had happened once when Hassan was peeling a banana on the windowsill. A neighbor spotted him, and his wife and four children went to Ammar's mother's house for a cup of coffee. The children disappeared, only to be discovered on the kitchen floor having devoured all the bananas. That day, Ammar saw his father looking dejected, tears frozen in his eyes, as if he had lost a mountain of gold. Perhaps Ammar's relationship with bananas was fraught because he couldn't distinguish between the fruit itself and the humiliating and stressful circumstances surrounding the rituals of buying and eating it, which were enough to kill any sense of enjoyment or satisfaction.

Furthermore, due to his lack of experience with eating bananas, the family often ate unripe, hard bananas. The taste of the unripe banana in the mouth made the experience even more disappointing and unpleasant. However, his mother always extolled the high nutritional value of bananas, emphasizing that eating them was beneficial in many ways, not just for satisfying cravings.

Ammar also remembers his mother talking to her neighbors about bananas being a fruit of Paradise, and the heated debate that ensued because there was no religious evidence for this. His mother insisted that if there were no bananas in Paradise, it would be lacking. One of the neighbors then offered an explanation, asserting that bananas were available in Paradise because believers craved them, and Paradise contains whatever believers desire!

The days passed, the children grew up, and Ammar's father retired. The country's economic situation changed, and bananas became readily available to everyone, in various types—Lebanese, Somali, and with labels bearing unusual names—suiting all budgets. They could be bought for as little as 25 or even 30 Syrian pounds. Syrians, including Ammar's family, rushed to buy bananas, to the point that banana peels littered the streets, bags, and garbage bins. But Ammar still found them difficult to eat, except perhaps with the smoothies and milkshakes he drank before going to the gym.

title: 國產好米選購指南
text: With hundreds of domestically produced packaged rice brands on the market, how should one choose? Rice can be categorized by its milling process into brown rice (husk removed), germ rice (brown rice with some bran removed), and white rice (germinated rice with the germ removed and fully whitened). Brown rice has the highest nutritional value, while white rice offers the best taste. If you prioritize nutritional value, it's recommended to choose brown rice or germ rice that retains the bran or germ nutrients. If you value taste, choose white rice. Consumers can choose different milling levels based on their personal preferences and needs. The quality of white rice can be discerned from the appearance of the grains inside the bag. Old rice grains will be yellowed, powdery, less transparent, and lack luster, often with an off-odor. As a result, cooked rice will be harder, less sticky, less elastic, and less fragrant. Furthermore, if the rice grains contain too many green rice grains, signs of insect infestation, or broken grains, the quality is poor, affecting the appearance and taste of the cooked rice. If consumers find self-inspection too complicated and time-consuming, it is recommended to choose rice marked with "CAS" (Certified Excellent Agricultural Product). This means the rice is grown in suitable areas according to government-recommended varieties and produced in well-managed processing plants. Its quality meets or exceeds the Republic of China National Standard (CNS) Grade 1 standard and is subject to regular safety inspections, ensuring quality. You can also refer to brands from factories with government guidance and good quality control. Remember, "you get what you pay for," and don't be tempted by unreasonably low prices. Furthermore, rice deteriorates gradually after being exposed to air after milling. It's best to buy a month's worth at a time, store it in a dry, cool place after opening, and refrigerate it if it cannot be consumed in a short period. Those who have eaten Thai rice often remember it as lacking stickiness and having a loose texture, while domestically produced rice is sweet, soft, and chewy, clearly demonstrating that variety and origin determine the quality of rice.

title: 首選健康食用油─茶油
text: In recent years, food safety issues have caused public anxiety about food safety. Cooking oil is one of the seven necessities of life (firewood, rice, oil, salt, soy sauce, vinegar, and tea), making the selection of healthy, safe, and high-quality cooking oil a major concern for housewives. However, the perfect cooking oil to maintain the health of the whole family is right at hand – camellia oil. Camellia oil, along with oil palm, olive, and coconut, is known as one of the world's four major woody oilseed plants. As early as 2300 years ago, our ancestors regarded it as a "miracle oil," and the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations has listed it as a key healthy cooking oil for promotion. However, consumers are generally unfamiliar with camellia oil and even less aware of how to choose the right one to ensure their families' peace of mind. This article provides a brief introduction to camellia oil to help consumers choose the right oil and consume healthy oil. Currently, there are three main types of camellia oil on the Taiwanese market, divided into two categories based on tree height and tree species. All three belong to the order Theales, family Theaceae, and genus Camellia. The first type of camellia tree, with a relatively tall stature, is commonly known as "true camellia oil." There are two types. One is the short-column camellia, scientifically known as *Camellia brevistyla* (Hayata) Coh.-Stuart or *Camellia tenuifolia*, which produces white flowers or flowers with golden-yellow buds. Its fruits are relatively small, commonly called "small-fruited camellia," "golden-flowered small fruit," or "tall tree with small fruit," and it has a low yield and high price. The other type is the camellia tree, scientifically known as *Camellia oleifera* Abel, which produces white flowers or bright red flowers with buds. Its fruits are large seeds, commonly called "large-fruited camellia," or "red-flowered large fruit," and it has a higher yield and is therefore cheaper. The camellia oil produced from these two types of trees is generally called "bitter camellia oil" or "camellia seed oil." In mainland China, it is called (wild) camellia oil; in Japan, it is called camellia oil; and in Europe and America, it is called camellia seed oil. The second type of camellia tree, with a shorter stature, is scientifically named *Camellia sinensis* (L.) O. Kuntze. Its leaves are generally used to produce various types of tea (oolong tea, black tea, green tea, etc.) for drinking. The oil made from the seeds of this tree is called "tea oil" or "tea seed oil," commonly known as tea seed oil. The three types of tea oil have different flavors. Comparing their edible texture and aroma intensity, tea seed oil is more mellow and smooth, superior to the two bitter tea oils.

title: Kochbuch/ Nudeln richtig gekocht
text:
IMPORTANT: The pot must be made of stainless steel (either 18/10 or AMC), as this method only works with stainless steel. All other pots are unsuitable and cannot be used. A set of stainless steel pots is available from around €20, and you'll save water, electricity or gas, and salt. You'll need 300 ml of water for every 100 g of pasta. For four people, you'll need approximately 500 g of pasta, which equates to 1.5 liters of water. The pot should be large enough to hold everything, and the water shouldn't boil over when stirring.

Place the pot filled with water on the stovetop (you can set it to the highest setting) and wait until the water boils vigorously. It's essential to add the salt now (10-15 g per liter of water). Adding it at the end will irreversibly leach the salt from the pasta. Therefore, adding salt afterward is pointless. Now add the pasta to the salted water and stir to prevent it from sticking to the bottom. Stir a few more times to ensure all the pasta is cooked. (If you want to do something else at the same time, it's recommended to use the traditional method of 1 liter of water per 100g of pasta in any pot; this eliminates the need for stirring.) The cooking time is indicated on the packaging, and after cooking, the pasta should be approximately al dente, meaning it should have a slightly firm, perceptible center when biting into it. The center may be just barely visible (lighter than the rest of the pasta) or not at all – depending on your definition of "al dente." In Italy, you can sometimes find pasta that is very, very firm. In any case, when the pasta is approximately al dente, all the water should have been absorbed. If not, it's better to drain off the excess water than to let the pasta become too soft.

title: Kochbuch/ Grundausstattung
text: An Arabic proverb says, "Whoever has sugar also has ants." Pests are one of the worst things you can have in the kitchen. Flour moths can infest almost all dry foods made from flour. And once you have them in your house, you have to throw away almost all open dry food. To prevent this, all food should be stored in airtight containers. Square coffee canisters have proven effective for sugar, flour, coffee, rice, muesli, and pasta. You can tightly and airtightly seal an entire package of flour or sugar in a coffee canister. Airtight plastic boxes are available in almost every size at hardware stores. These allow you to safely store dry foods, protecting them from mice and other pests. Furthermore, such boxes are a great help in keeping the kitchen organized.

title: बरमान घाट पर नर्मदा
text: Here, my sister and nephew have set up a stove made of cow dung cakes (cow dung cakes) and put eggplants, potatoes, and tomatoes in it to make bharta. The eggplants from Barman are large, so we bought those. We also bought radishes and carrots for salad. The flour rotis have been made and placed on the embers. They have to be constantly turned over, otherwise they burn. It's said that if you turn a roti fifty-two times, it's completely cooked. Meanwhile, my nephew has brought back roasted potatoes, bhatte, and tomatoes in a plate, washed them in the Narmada River. A brick stove is being built and the tempering is being done. The rotis are now cooked. My sister is applying ghee. Everyone has bathed. The use of polythene has decreased. People don't even use soap while bathing. I was very touched to see the awareness about preventing pollution in the Narmada.

title: ‘मन की बात 2.0’ की तीसरी कड़ी में प्रधानमंत्री का सम्बोधन
text: We've even transformed the knowledge of food into a science. A balanced and nutritious diet is essential for all of us, especially for women and newborns, as it forms the foundation of our society's future. Under the "Poshan Abhiyaan," nutrition is being transformed into a mass movement across the country using modern scientific methods. People are fighting malnutrition in new and interesting ways. A topic was once brought to my attention: "A handful of grain" has become a major movement in Nashik. During harvest season, Anganwadi workers collect a handful of grain from people. This grain is used to prepare hot meals for children and women. The person donating becomes a conscious citizen social worker. They then dedicate themselves to this cause, becoming a soldier of that movement.

title: Libro di cucina/Tecniche di cottura/Cottura della pasta
text:
Boiling water involves raising the temperature of a certain volume of water from room temperature (assuming it's 25°C) to boiling point (100°C).

The water used for this process must meet the "potable" water specifications. It can be drawn from the mains, a water supply, or purchased bottled. If the water is drawn from the mains, special care must be taken to ensure that its potability is not compromised by deterioration (e.g., corrosion) or fouling of the household pipes.

To contain the boiling water, a steel pot (which is an excellent heat conductor) is used, the bottom of which is typically heated by a burner fueled by a combustible gas (methane or a propane-butane mixture). An alternative to a gas cooktop is an induction cooktop, which is safer because it does not contain open flames (which can cause burns) or combustible gases (which, if used incorrectly or if the connection pipe is damaged, can lead to unconsciousness and a fire or explosion).

The amount of water to use for cooking depends on the desired amount of pasta (generally, no less than 1 liter is needed for every 100 grams of pasta). Once the amount of pasta has been determined, it is possible to estimate the amount of water needed and therefore the diameter of the pot used for this purpose. This should be determined by considering that the water should not completely fill the pot, but should be a few centimeters below the rim (or about 2/3 full), so as to limit foaming, which intensifies during the actual cooking phase (i.e., after mixing the pasta and table salt into the cooking water).

The arrival of boiling point is indicated by the formation of bubbles within the liquid mass, which occurs at the bottom of the pan (where the temperature is highest). After the formation of the first (smaller) bubbles, bubbles with gradually increasing diameters form.

title: Vini nel tempo. Intervista ad Helmuth Köcher, fondatore del Merano WineFestival
text:
W@H Interaction with the scientific and academic world is essential for improving quality and control methods in production chains. Will this aspect be included in future events surrounding the festival?

Köcher: Congratulations on your suggestion. For several years, I've been closely following the role of the scientific and academic world, and I believe this should be increasingly integrated into events like the Merano WineFestival. Every producer needs to better understand many aspects, such as wine sustainability.

W@H If we look at the map of major Italian food and wine events, Southern Italy is absent. Reading the local Italian press, however, one sees great enthusiasm for local producers from Southern Italy to be able to participate in Merano. Does the MWF plan to organize some events south of the capital in the coming years, for example along the lines of the Food and Wine Festivals in Milan and Rome?

Köcher: I've been planning to organize an event in Southern Italy for years. A few years ago, I was heavily invested in Naples or Trapani. Most likely, the timing wasn't right. Today, I believe the best region to host an event like the Merano WineFestival is Puglia, as in recent years the quality of its wine has begun to gain recognition, making itself felt on international markets as well.

title: 日本橋ゆかり 野永喜三夫さんに聞く「だし」と「うま味」
text:
It's important to remember that the umami in dashi (Japanese broth) is enhanced by the synergistic effect of glutamic acid and inosinic acid, as seen in kelp and bonito flakes, and guanylic acid in dried shiitake mushrooms. This applies to other ingredients and seasonings as well; for example, the tomato and miso sauce I call "Tomomiso," and Parmesan cheese in miso soup, both go very well together. Japanese cuisine needs to evolve with the times, too (laughs). Also, remember that the umami in each ingredient increases as it matures.

However, and this may sound contradictory, dashi-infused miso and dashi packets are certainly suitable for times when cooking time is limited. Even granulated dashi is fine. Adding a little chicken stock powder to it will deepen the flavor. The important thing is to use slightly less than the recipe calls for. The ingredients themselves release umami, so there's plenty of flavor.


Making dashi by simply soaking kombu seaweed in water the night before is also a good option. Even at room temperature, the kombu will slowly open up over time, releasing its umami flavor slowly, resulting in a mild taste. You can then bring it to a boil in the morning and use it to make miso soup. You don't need to make dashi every day; it's convenient to make enough for about three days at once and store it in the refrigerator or freezer for later use.

title: 平成22年度文部科学白書：栄養教諭と学校給食
text: To address the changing environment surrounding children's eating habits in recent years, it is crucial to establish a guidance system in schools and to provide systematic and continuous guidance on food within the overall school educational activities. For this reason, the placement of nutrition teachers began in each prefecture in April 2005, and as of April 2011, a total of 3,853 nutrition teachers have been assigned to all prefectures. Additionally, 66 nutrition teachers are assigned to affiliated schools of national universities. The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) has included "promotion of food education in schools" in the general provisions of the new curriculum guidelines, which will be fully implemented in elementary schools from April 2011 and in junior high schools from April 2012, and has also enhanced the descriptions from a food education perspective in related subjects. Furthermore, the curriculum guidelines for high schools and kindergartens have also been enhanced with descriptions from a food education perspective. In June 2008, the School Lunch Act was amended, clearly defining "promoting food education in schools" as one of the law's objectives. It also stipulated that nutrition teachers should provide practical guidance on food using school lunches, and that school principals should create an overall plan for food education. Based on these changes, in March 2010, the "Guidelines for Food Education" were revised to outline the necessity of food education in schools, the goals of food education, the overall plan for food education to be created primarily by nutrition teachers, and the basic concepts and methods of food education in subjects and during lunchtime. Furthermore, since 2009, the "Food Education Promotion Project Centered on Nutrition Teachers" has been implemented, supporting initiatives in each region to address challenges in promoting food education by having nutrition teachers at the core, in cooperation with families, producers, PTAs, and other local organizations, under the guidance of the board of education. Furthermore, in fiscal year 2009, we produced educational materials (DVDs) to deepen parents' and others' understanding of the importance of promoting food education in schools and school lunches. Since fiscal year 2010, we have also been implementing a program to dispatch experienced retired nutrition teachers and school nutrition staff to less experienced nutrition teachers. School lunches not only aim to maintain and improve children's health by providing them with nutritionally balanced and nutritious meals, but they also have great educational significance as they can be used as "living teaching materials" not only during lunchtime but also in various subjects, special activities, and integrated learning time to effectively promote guidance on food. As of May 2009, 21,713 elementary schools (99.2 percent of all elementary schools) and 9,235 junior high schools (85.5 percent of all junior high schools) were implementing school lunches, for a total of approximately 32,400 schools. In recent years, schools have been working to diversify their school lunches. For example, they are using locally produced ingredients in school lunches and incorporating local regional dishes and traditional cuisine into their menus.

title: В "Роскачестве" рассказали, какими должны быть идеальные пельмени и как их есть, чтобы не растолстеть
text:
Roskachestvo will host a tasting of pelmeni sold in Russian stores and, as is its tradition, rank the best brands. Meanwhile, experts have shared tips on choosing the popular convenience food, storing it, and eating it properly without harming your figure. Recommendations are published on the organization's website.

According to experts, ideal pelmeni should contain only seven ingredients: ground meat, onions, salt, pepper, flour, water, and eggs. However, the wording for "spices" in the ingredients is very vague, and flavor enhancers and flavorings may be added under the guise of "spices."

Experts recommend choosing a product whose labeling clearly lists all the spices used. Experts also recommend that neither the ground meat nor the dough should contain fiber or starch, otherwise it's a form of consumer deception. Pelmeni should also be crumbly in the package, as sticky products may indicate improper storage. The maximum shelf life of pelmeni should be six months, stored at a temperature no higher than -10 degrees Celsius.

"For those watching their weight, a serving of pelmeni should not exceed 10 pieces—150 grams, or approximately 300 kilocalories," noted Roskachestvo. Additives such as mayonnaise, butter, and heavy cream should be avoided. If the pelmeni significantly increase in size during cooking, this may indicate soy in the recipe.

Roskachestvo intends to check the quality of pelmeni produced in Moscow, the Novgorod, Chelyabinsk, Tver, Leningrad, and Samara regions, the Krasnodar Territory, St. Petersburg, the Vladimir, Belgorod, and Oryol regions, the Republic of Mordovia, the Nizhny Novgorod, Novosibirsk, and Tomsk regions, the Republic of Bashkortostan, the Krasnoyarsk, Altai, and Perm territories, as well as the Saratov and Ryazan regions. Experts will examine the meat filling, check the dough for flaky texture, evaluate the taste of the dumplings, and determine if they contain antibiotics, colorings, or flavorings. About 50 packs will be purchased, including "children's" varieties and the popular "bulmeni" dumplings. The products will be tested for over 50 quality and safety parameters.

title: Роскачество к лету перечислило признаки идеального мороженого и добавки в его составе, которых можно не бояться
text:
With summer approaching, Roskachestvo (the Federal Agency for Quality Assurance) has issued a reminder on how to choose the right ice cream and whether stabilizers and E-additives should be a concern. Expert recommendations are published on the agency's website.

According to GOST, ice cream is made from milk or cream, natural flavors and stabilizers, butter, and eggs. The milk content in such products must be over 40%. If palm oil is listed as an ingredient, it is considered a milk-containing product and should be priced lower than ice cream.

Fat content affects the appearance of ice cream: in milk ice cream, it is no more than 7.5%, making it a treat even for those watching their weight. Cream ice cream has 8 to 11.5% fat, while plombir ice cream has 12 to 20%. Ideally, ice cream should be uniform in color. Inconsistency indicates that the mixture was not properly mixed with the natural additive or coloring during production. The higher the fat content, the yellower the treat.

If the ice cream is misshapen, it's either improperly stored or nearing its expiration date. A white coating on the chocolate coating also indicates improper storage or an ambiguous composition. The coating itself should be evenly distributed and not fall off. Ice crystals on the surface indicate that the ice cream has been re-frozen, meaning its flavor has already been spoiled. However, if the ice cream is chipping, it's a good sign: hardened frozen mass always has a dense consistency.

title: Es salsa mahonesa o quizás mayonesa
text:
The spell checker accepts both spellings, although the Royal Spanish Academy (RAE) and this writer prefer to spell it with an "h". Making mayonnaise is simple: garlic clove + egg + vinegar + a pinch of salt. Whisk, gradually adding sunflower oil. Some might add, "Start praying it doesn't curdle," but simply don't move the whisk until it begins to thicken.

It's related to other sauces like aioli, but mayonnaise is prohibited in food establishments, as it's made with raw egg. The mayonnaise found in many restaurants is either jarred or made with pasteurized eggs; with the latter, curdling is virtually impossible.

Its origins, though disputed, begin on April 18, 1756, when Marshal Richelieu attacked Fort San Felipe in Mahón and invaded the island. The troops then tasted the sauce known as "all-i-oli." They copied the recipe and took it to France to share it with their French friends.

It was in France that they changed the original olive oil for a milder one, omitted the garlic, and named the resulting sauce 'Sauce Mahonnaise' (after Mahon). Louis François Armand du Plessis's cook claimed to have created it to celebrate Duke Richelieu's victory over the British at the port of Mahón, in Menorca, and that it was named in honor of that town.

The debate surrounding its origin centers on whether the sauce the French took with them predated this version or if it was a cook's improvisation during battle. A poem by a Frenchman named Lancelot, written in 1625, long before the Battle of Mahón, appeared in France as a recipe for mayonnaise.

title: La Estrella Tortilla de patata
text:
It is believed that the potato omelet began to spread, and most theories revolve around the Carlist Wars.

It is said that a housewife living in one of the many houses in the Navarrese mountains invented it and offered it to General Tomás de Zumalacárregui (the military leader of the Carlist army). He asked her for something to eat. She went to the kitchen and saw that she only had a few potatoes and onions and a couple of eggs. Not wanting to disappoint him, she fried the chopped potatoes and onions, and when they were cooked, she mixed them with beaten eggs.

She put the mixture in a pan and let it simmer. The general liked the dish and used the recipe to feed his troops.

The CSIC (Spanish National Research Council) contributes its research on the origin of this dish in Europe. Researchers refer to Joseph de Tena Godoy y Malfeyto, Marquis of Robledo, who was searching for a nutritious and inexpensive food to combat the famines that plagued late 18th-century Europe. It appears they invented a type of pancake that wasn't baked but rather cooked in a pan.

The study places the origin of the Spanish omelet in the Extremaduran town of Villanueva de la Serena.

It may also have origins in Seville, as the hospital run by the Brotherhood of Charity in Seville was experiencing financial difficulties. On the advice of some of the repatriated emigrants from the Americas, the brothers used potatoes grown in some fields to feed the patients, and they were well-received. This all occurred in 1575.

title: MIVARF Yachochea Tanzania ya Viwanda
text:
The Government through the Marketing, Value Addition and Rural Financial Services (MIVARF) Program has been able to improve the lives of rural people in Meru and Mbulu Districts in Arusha Region by adding value to milk and garlic farming.

Speaking to experts from MIVARF, The Grand Demam Dairy Factory Manager Deo Temba said, we used to process 300 liters of milk per day which was a small amount of milk according to the needs of the people, but now we can process 2500 liters of milk per day after receiving assistance from MIVARF by building a Cold Room for us.

“Since the construction of the cold room, we have been able to increase milk products through 15 groups where in those groups there are 120-150 people which reaches the number of people who bring milk to the factory”, Temba noted.

The Grand Demam.co.Ltd factory has been able to connect farmers with the factory as the factory provides them with education on how to milk milk productively so that they can get a lot of quality milk along with good husbandry by having few livestock and producing a lot of milk and providing them with medical services for their livestock.

A farmer from Meru District Hilda Mroso explained that, previously, she used to milk a lot of milk but sent 300 liters of milk to The Grand Demam Factory due to lack of storage space, currently she is able to send 800 liters of milk to the Factory due to increasing the storage space for the milk.

In addition, the MIVARF Program has also enabled the Bashay Vegetable Processing Factory in Meru District by providing them with an onion drying machine where previously they were drying onions using the sun or Solar Drier which used to take them one to six weeks to dry the onions.

Onion farmer Boniface John explained that before the MIVARF program was implemented, the Bashay Onion Processing Factory was processing with great difficulty and for a long time and processed very few onions.

“The availability of this onion drying machine has enabled our factory to improve processing services as the machine is capable of drying one to two tons of garlic in eight hours, equivalent to 20 sacks, so we can dry it quickly, and it has helped us increase customers as we are completing our orders on time. This is a great development in our Bashay Village, said the farmer. ”

The factory is now able to sell value-added products by selling crushed garlic, namely garlic powder and garlic paste, which has helped them sell easily and increase their income.

MIVARF; is a Rural Markets and Financial Services Infrastructure Programme developed by the Government of Tanzania in collaboration with the International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) and the African Development Bank (ADB). The main objective of this Programme is to achieve the Government's objective of reducing poverty and accelerating sustainable economic growth by enabling rural households to increase their income and food security.

title: TADB Yaipa ‘Sapoti’ Kampeni ya Kitaifa ya Unywaji wa Maziwa
text:
In ensuring that many Tanzanians increase their enthusiasm for drinking milk, the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank (TADB) has supported the efforts of the Government and the Tanzania Dairy Board (TDB) in the country by providing equipment to be used in the National Milk Drinking Campaign expected to be held nationwide in Kagera region from May 28 - June 1 this year.

Speaking during the handover of the equipment held at the TADB Offices in Dar es Salaam, the Acting Managing Director of TADB, Mr. Francis Assenga said that the Agricultural Development Bank has supported the Campaign by recognizing the importance of promoting milk drinking in the country as recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO).

“Recognizing the importance of this Campaign, TADB in collaboration with TDB and many stakeholders are determined to promote milk drinking to reach international standards of milk consumption which is estimated to reach at least 200 liters per year from the current 47,” he said.

He added that recognizing the importance of dairy farming, TADB included the value chain of beef and dairy farming as one of the first chains to receive loans for livestock value addition in the country.

He stressed that his Bank is committed to developing the value addition of Beef and Dairy Farming to support various Government efforts in the development of the dairy sector in the country.

“The Bank provides loans and supports investments for the construction, purchase of machinery and installation of cattle handling equipment including dips and watering ponds as well as milk processing to add value to milk,” said Mr. Assenga.

For his part, the Acting Registrar of TDB, Dr. Mayasa Simba said that the national campaign with the theme ‘Save the Ship, Build Health, Build the Economy through Milk’ aims to shape the Dairy Board’s commitment to managing, coordinating and providing quality advisory services to stakeholders to promote and develop a sustainable and competitive dairy industry in the country.

“The aim of this campaign is to promote milk consumption to ensure that more Tanzanians reach international standards and also to achieve the Board’s goal of ensuring a well-managed and coordinated, competitive dairy sector with the aim of improving the lives of Tanzanians and increasing the contribution of the dairy sector to the national economy,” he said.

The Dairy Board was established by the Dairy Sector Act, Chapter (262) which is under the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries with the responsibility to manage, coordinate and develop the sector. The Board has the responsibility to encourage and empower stakeholders in the activities of production, milk collection, processing, improving marketing and consumption of milk and its products.

title: Feeling Stressed?
text:
It’s not clear why some people can sidestep or recover more quickly from stress than others. These resilient people seem to “bounce back” more easily after stressful situations. Recent studies of animals suggest that resiliency may depend at least in part on our genes. But learning healthy ways to cope with stress can also boost your resilience.

“There are many different ways to cope with stress. We know from a lot of different studies that having close personal relationships—people with whom you can talk, with whom you can share your feelings—can be helpful,” says Kiecolt-Glaser. “So spending time with family and friends in order to maintain those relationships is perhaps one of the most crucial things you can do as a stress reducer.”

Unfortunately, Kiecolt-Glaser adds, “when we’re stressed, we tend to do the worst things that are not at all helpful to our health.”

For instance, stressed out people may tend to isolate themselves and not seek social support. “Exercise is a great stress reducer. But when people are stressed, exercise becomes less common and less appealing,” Kiecolt-Glaser says. “Instead of maintaining a healthy diet—also important to reducing stress—some people who are stressed tend to eat more donuts than vegetables.”

You may think that the agitation brought on by stress might help to burn calories. But evidence hints that the opposite is more likely. Kiecolt-Glaser and colleagues found that, compared to nonstressed people, those who were stressed burned fewer calories after high-fat meals and they produced more of the hormone insulin, which enhances fat storage. “So stress may contribute to weight gain and obesity through these biological routes,” Kiecolt-Glaser adds.

title: Struggling to Sleep?
text:
Most people who have sleep apnea don’t realize it. That’s because this disorder only occurs during sleep.

Sleep apnea is when you have pauses in breathing while you’re asleep. These pauses can last from seconds to minutes. You may have difficulty breathing a few times or dozens of times an hour.

These breathing pauses can be dangerous if they cause the oxygen level in your body to drop or disturb your sleep. When oxygen drops, your brain does whatever it can to get you to resume breathing. And then you may snore, gasp, snort loudly, or make a choking sound. A family member or bed partner might be the first to notice these disruptions in your sleep.

Sleep apnea is a common disorder. Anyone can develop it. “Sleep apnea can occur in both genders, in all races and ethnicities, and in people of all sizes and shapes,” says Dr. Michael Twery, a sleep expert at NIH.

title: تعليق المبادرة المصرية للحقوق الشخصية على قانون "التجارب السريرية": تعديلات مُرحَّب بها وتعكس مقترحات المجتمع المدني
text:
On August 24, 2020, the Egyptian Parliament approved the amended version of the Clinical Medical Research Regulation Law, incorporating several modifications in response to recommendations submitted by the Presidency in October 2018. The Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR) considers the amendments to the law regulating clinical trials to be positive and consistent with the recommendations it presented during a hearing with members of Parliament in 2018, as well as its commentary submitted after Parliament passed the law in May 2018. These recommendations aim to address the fundamental shortcomings in conducting clinical research in Egypt.

EIPR also views the passage of the Clinical Trials Law as a clear and effective example of the role that civil society and human rights organizations can play when given the opportunity to collaborate and partner with executive and legislative bodies, both globally and locally. In April 2018, EIPR was invited to participate in a hearing held by the Parliament’s Health Committee to gather the views of various stakeholders on the draft Clinical Medical Research Regulation Law.

In 2016, the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, in collaboration with several local and international research organizations, published its report, "Ethical Questions about Drug Clinical Trials in Egypt: Local Challenges and Funding from Manufacturers."

This report generated widespread public and media attention both locally and internationally. While the report affirmed the legality of the practices of international companies funding clinical trials in Egypt, in accordance with Egyptian legislation, it also found these laws insufficient to protect Egyptian patients and riddled with flaws that are inconsistent with similar laws in other countries.

It is worth noting that Egypt ranks second only to South Africa in the number of African countries hosting clinical trials for drugs sponsored by multinational pharmaceutical companies. This is attributed to the availability of infrastructure, researchers, and physicians who are attractive to researchers. Furthermore, Egypt's demographics, patient profile, and the relatively low cost of conducting these trials are key incentives for doing so. However, the downside is that the Egyptian healthcare system does not provide some patients with access to basic treatment, potentially forcing them to participate in these trials despite the risk of exploitation in order to obtain free treatment, even if the outcome is unknown. This general climate facilitates the exploitation of the most vulnerable and needy citizens. Therefore, the Egyptian Initiative report presented a set of proposals to the Egyptian authorities and decision-makers, including several recommendations for the new law.

title: تزامنًا مع فعاليات اليوم العالمي للتغطية الصحية الشاملة، المبادرة المصرية للحقوق الشخصية تنشر تقريرها حول التشغيل التجريبي للتأمين الصحي الشامل في بورسعيد: تقييم مجتمعي للمرحلة وإصلاحات واجبة
text:
The report presents a model for activating the role of community accountability as a guarantee for the sustainability of various reform efforts, enabling society to systematically monitor the development process. This stems from the initiative's belief that enjoying the highest attainable standard of health is a fundamental human right, as enshrined in the World Health Organization Constitution and the Egyptian Constitution. The right to health includes access to acceptable, affordable, and appropriately sized healthcare at the right time.

Community participation and dialogue formed the foundation of the new Comprehensive Health Insurance Law and its executive regulations. This law is the product of ongoing work involving experts, government officials, and civil society representatives. Numerous hearings were held to design a system that ensures accessibility, availability, acceptability, and quality of services and healthcare protection, without discrimination and regardless of income level.

The Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights (EIPR) participated in the drafting of this law through advocacy and strategic litigation when proposed legislation conflicted with the fundamental right to health without discrimination. EIPR also contributed proposals as a member of the drafting committee, aiming to ensure a comprehensive legal framework for the healthcare system—a plan for its complete and sustainable overhaul. It is worth noting that EIPR participated in Universal Health Coverage Day 2018 by publishing the compiled results of a community-based assessment of hospitals and health services in Port Said prior to the implementation of the Comprehensive Social Health Insurance System.

The Comprehensive Health Insurance System was launched in Port Said Governorate last July, with implementation to follow in the other governorates of the Suez Canal and Sinai. The government has already announced the collection of the various financial resources stipulated by the law for this purpose. Furthermore, various international funding bodies have provided additional resources and technical support for the necessary reforms to implement this law in Port Said.

The field research team observes that "in general, there has been a noticeable improvement in the services provided by the new insurance system, reflecting a degree of seriousness in its implementation. This is primarily reflected in the visible buildings, equipment, and infrastructure. However, several shortcomings are evident, most notably the absence of a clear and separate master plan encompassing procedures, management and monitoring frameworks, information systems, education, accountability mechanisms, and community participation in monitoring services and educating citizens about their operation. These problems represent fundamental obstacles that increasingly affect citizen satisfaction and, if they persist, pose the greatest threat to public trust in this system. This, in turn, could impact beneficiary acceptance and reduce usage rates, particularly regarding the retroactive collection of contributions."

Today, we present a phased assessment of the implementation steps of this law, in recognition of and to complement the role of civil society in community monitoring and oversight. This effort primarily aims to offer a scientific and community-based perspective on the implementation challenges, how to overcome them, and to propose clear suggestions that will ensure the law achieves its objectives.

The report also raises some important questions about the mechanisms for implementing the law, mainly pointing to the importance of providing information and full transparency regarding the implementation process so that society can interact positively in this project, and achieve full community oversight of the implementation process in a way that reduces the waste of resources and ensures that the voice of those concerned and the beneficiaries of the system is continuously conveyed.

title: 最後一線抗生素－萬古黴素（Vancomycin）
text:
In 1928, Fleming discovered that Penicillium mold had the ability to inhibit bacterial growth in his unwashed petri dishes. However, because he was unable to isolate the antibacterial components, it did not receive much attention. It wasn't until the 1940s that two other scientists, Florey and Chain, first isolated penicillin from Penicillium mold cultures and confirmed its bactericidal effect in mouse experiments. Subsequently, due to the need for treating wounded soldiers during World War II, penicillin was mass-produced and applied. Fleming, Florey, and Chain were awarded the 1945 Nobel Prize in Medicine for this achievement.

Since penicillin, many microbiologists have devoted themselves to the search for and isolation of antibiotics. Following penicillin, streptomycin, chloramphenicol, oxytetracycline, tetracycline, and others were successively isolated and applied for various bactericidal purposes. Humanity has achieved considerable success in this period of combating bacteria. However, bacteria are living organisms; in other words, bacteria evolve. Although bacteria do not reproduce sexually, they can still undergo genetic recombination through processes such as conjugation and transformation. Mutated bacteria that develop drug resistance can then transfer this resistance to other bacteria through various genetic recombination mechanisms.

Vancomycin is currently known as a last-line antibiotic, commonly referred to as the "silver bullet." Unlike most antibiotics that can be taken orally, vancomycin must be administered by injection over several weeks, making it expensive. Furthermore, due to its high toxicity and potential kidney damage, it is mostly considered by doctors only when commonly used antibiotics have failed.

Common antibiotics work by acting on the bacterial cell wall. The bacterial cell wall is composed of peptidoglycan, and the synthesis of this cell wall requires the catalysis of various enzymes to form a strong network structure. Penicillin, for example, has a structure similar to that of the bacterial cell wall, thus competitively inhibiting cell wall synthesis enzymes, thereby inhibiting cell wall synthesis and killing the bacteria. Vancomycin's bactericidal mechanism is similar to penicillin's; both inhibit bacterial cell wall synthesis. However, vancomycin's cup-shaped structure allows it to bind to the terminal segments of the cell wall's sugar chains via hydrogen bonds, preventing enzymatic activity from extending the original chain structure and thus disrupting the cell wall's structure.

Drug-resistant bacteria counteract this mechanism. For example, penicillin-resistant bacteria produce an additional enzyme that destroys the portion of penicillin's structure that resembles the bacterial cell wall, preventing penicillin from binding to cell wall synthesis enzymes and thus losing its bactericidal effect. Although vancomycin is a last-line antibiotic, some resistant strains have been discovered. Vancomycin-resistant enterococci, for instance, have altered the terminal structure of their cell wall chains, significantly reducing vancomycin's affinity for the cell wall and thus losing its ability to inhibit cell wall synthesis enzymes. These drug-resistant strains often transfer their resistant plastids to other non-resistant strains through conjugation. This transfer can even occur between different species. In recent years, some vancomycin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus strains have proliferated rapidly, which is due to this.

title: 淺談臺灣森林療癒發展之契機
text: Industrialization and urbanization are the environmental development trends of modern countries. The IUCN estimates that by 2050, 70% of humanity will live in cities. This development has led to human alienation from nature. The book "Children Who Have Lost Their Forests: Saving Children with Nature Deficiency Syndrome" mentions that many modern children suffer from emotional control and psychological problems, and what they need most is natural therapy, which means frequently getting close to nature and experiencing it with all five senses. The paradigm shift in forest management over the past few decades has also led to the development of multi-objective management methods in modern forest management projects in response to rapid environmental changes. Among these, forest recreation has become an emerging trend in order to adjust the imbalance of modern lifestyles and improve the health of forest users. Utilizing forests as a space for health care and treatment has become one of the international methods of forest management, and is gradually shaping into an interdisciplinary integrative science called forest therapy, forest wellness, or forest health. The development of forest therapy is one of the feasible solutions to the challenges of an aging society and lifestyle-related diseases, aiming to promote health and improve quality of life. In addition, utilizing the natural environment can enhance the experience of forest users, improve their environmental identity, increase their awareness and sensitivity to the environment, and enhance their knowledge of the environment and the concept and connotation of ecological wholeness. This can establish environmental ethical values, cultivate users' environmental action skills and experience, and ultimately achieve multiple goals of environmental education. By using the natural environment to improve physical and mental health, the public's respect for environmental ethics can be increased, and they will be more willing to protect nature. Therefore, the promotion of forest therapy has made important contributions to human health and natural environment conservation (Yu Jiabin et al., 2015). Psychology professor Kaplan (1989) proposed the "Attention Recovery Theory," arguing that the experience of the natural environment has a positive effect on human focus and cognition. Urich (1991) proposed that in a healing environment, people can experience positive feelings such as "control and privacy," "social support," "physical activity and exercise," and "closeness to nature," thus achieving health benefits. Therefore, forest therapy is a comprehensive utilization of the forest environment, increasing the connection between people and nature through activities such as leisure, exercise, work, meditation, or spiritual conversation. Activities such as walking, guided tours, conversations, rehabilitation, group activities, and aromatherapy in the forest all fall under the scope of forest therapy. Forest therapy is suitable for both healthy individuals and those experiencing stress or sub-health. From the perspective of preventative medicine and complementary therapy, the healing power of forests is irreplaceable. Broadly speaking, when people are close to or appreciate the beauty of nature in a forest, they feel relaxed and their health is improved; the so-called "forest bathing" is actually a part of forest therapy. From a professional perspective, forest therapy refers to a process in which a professionally trained companion, tailored to the specific needs of the individual, sets specific goals, utilizes specific forest facilities and equipment, designs activities, and evaluates the effects to promote physical, mental, and spiritual health, and enhance community and ecological development.

title: Depressive Symptomatik bei Erwachsenen in Deutschland
text:
Depression is among the most common mental disorders and is associated with a high individual and societal burden of disease [1–3]. In Germany, social security institutions have also documented a significant increase in the importance of depression in healthcare provision in recent years, accompanied by growing public awareness [4–6].

Depression encompasses a heterogeneous spectrum of depressive disorders, which differ, among other things, in the severity and course of depressive symptoms [7]. For a diagnosis to be made, specific diagnostic inclusion and exclusion criteria must be met in addition to the presence of depressive symptoms—for example, the presence of certain key symptoms is required. Depressive symptoms, such as low mood and loss of energy, can also occur without a clinical diagnosis of depression—for example, as a subthreshold form of depression when the diagnostic criteria are not fully met, as well as in the context of other mental disorders and physical illnesses. This also includes depressive symptoms resulting from stressful life events, as well as in the course of substance-related disorders (e.g., alcohol and drugs), in chronic physical illnesses, or as a side effect of medication. Regardless of its diagnostic classification, depressive symptoms lead to subjective impairments in general health and health-related quality of life [8, 9] and are associated with increased morbidity and mortality [10, 11]. Furthermore, the presence of depressive symptoms is associated with increased outpatient physician visits and sick leave [12]. Increased utilization of health and long-term care services is particularly evident in older age [13].

Epidemiological estimates of the prevalence and distribution of depressive symptoms in the population are therefore highly relevant public health information and provide an important basis for planning prevention and healthcare. Prevalence data for the adult population in Germany are already available from the German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (DEGS1, 2008–2011) [14] and are now being reported for the German Health Interview and Examination Survey for Adults (GEDA 2014/2015-EHIS).

title: Alkoholkonsum bei Erwachsenen in Deutschland: Rauschtrinken
text:
Alcohol is a psychoactive substance that can cause addiction. Harmful alcohol consumption is considered a contributing factor to more than 200 diseases and is among the top five risk factors for illness, disability, and death worldwide [1]. In addition to the health consequences of risky alcohol consumption for consumers, the World Health Organization (WHO) also lists the socioeconomic consequences for those affected, as well as the damage to other people and society as a whole [1]. The societal consequences of alcohol consumption include not only direct costs to the healthcare system and losses in productivity, but also intangible costs such as a loss of quality of life. The economic costs of alcohol consumption in Germany are estimated at up to €40 billion per year, depending on the source, with approximately one-quarter of this amount attributable to direct costs to the healthcare system [2, 3].

Binge drinking is a particularly risky drinking pattern that can cause acute harm such as alcohol poisoning, injuries, and violence. In the long term, alcohol dependence and various organ damage can result from binge drinking [4]. These can also occur when the average amount of alcohol consumed by a person is relatively low [1]. To reduce harmful alcohol consumption in the population, the WHO has developed strategies at the global and European levels [5, 6]. The WHO Global Action Plan for the Prevention and Control of Non-Communicable Diseases aims for a relative reduction in risky alcohol consumption of 10 percent by 2025 (compared to 2010) [7]. The National Health Goal "Reduce Alcohol Consumption," which was first published in 2015, is partly based on the WHO strategies [8].

title: जानलेवा हवा
text: Dharam Singh, a surgeon posted at Dholpur District Hospital, explained that a heatwave-like situation had already developed here in March. This is why 40 percent more children and elderly patients visited the hospital in March-April this year compared to January-February. Children comprise 70 percent of these cases. Most children complain of diarrhea, restlessness, and dizziness. Dholpur's stone is famous not only in Rajasthan but throughout the country. Mangatram, a 44-year-old stone quarry worker, explained that while working in the mines provides money, the heat of the stone burns the bodies of laborers like him. Dharam Singh said, "I come from an area that is most affected by heatwaves because there are underground stones everywhere. 80 percent of the rural workers here are affected by heatwaves. MNREGA workers are also affected." However, the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) issued new heatwave-related guidelines to all 17 heatwave-affected states on March 3, 2018. It clearly states that MNREGA workers will work only in morning and evening shifts. The directive states that work will be done only where there is adequate water supply. Singh explains that the duration of heatwaves has steadily increased over the past four years. While this duration was 40-45 days in 2015, it has now increased to 60-70 days.

title: ‘मन की बात’ की 51वीं कड़ी में प्रधानमंत्री का संबोधन
text:
My dear countrymen, this December we lost some extraordinary countrymen. On December 19th, Dr. Jayachandran of Chennai passed away. Dr. Jayachandran was fondly called "Makkal Maruthuvar" because he held a place in the hearts of the people. Dr. Jayachandran was known for providing affordable treatment to the poor. People say that he was always ready to treat patients. He even paid the travel expenses of elderly patients who came to him for treatment. I have read about many of his inspiring social work on the betterindia.com website.

Similarly, on December 25th, we learned of the passing of Sulagitti Narasamma of Karnataka. Sulagitti Narasamma was a birth attendant. She served thousands of mothers and sisters in Karnataka, especially in remote areas. Earlier this year, she was awarded the Padma Shri. There are many inspiring figures, such as Dr. Jayachandran and Sulagitti Narasamma, who have dedicated their lives to the welfare of all in society. While we're talking about health care, I'd also like to discuss the social efforts of doctors in Bijnor, Uttar Pradesh. Recently, some of our party workers told me that some young doctors in the city set up camps and provide free treatment to the poor. The Heart Lungs Critical Centre here organizes such medical camps every month, providing free testing and treatment for a variety of ailments. Today, hundreds of poor patients benefit from these camps every month. The enthusiasm of these doctors, who are engaged in selfless service, is truly commendable.

title: Prevenzione e trattamento delle reazioni avverse ai mezzi di contrasto. Uno studio osservazionale sulla qualità dell’assistenza infermieristica
text: Introduction: Contrast media (CMA) are diagnostic drugs with a high risk of adverse drug reactions (ADRs) due to the toxicity of their compounds and the dynamics of rapid intravascular infusion. The aim of this research is to evaluate the quality of nursing care for patients receiving CMA. Materials and Methods: This is a quantitative observational study using stratified convenience sampling. Data collection was conducted through a structured, anonymous, and confidential questionnaire with closed-ended answers administered to nurses working in diagnostic radiology units of Rome's healthcare facilities. Statistical analysis was descriptive. Results: 74.49% of nurses in the sample responded to the questionnaire, of whom 84.93% were familiar with protocols for the prevention and 82.19% with protocols for the treatment of ADRs, but 76.71% had not attended training courses in this regard. 87.67% of respondents stated that they systematically perform nursing assessments, but in 67.12% of cases, they do not use risk factor rating scales. 24.66% of the sample is not qualified to perform Basic Life Support & Defibrillation (BLSD) procedures, and 54.80% stated that they assist at-risk patients during the examination without the presence of the anesthesiologist-resuscitator. 75.34% of nurses stated that they educate patients on the recognition of late ADRs; 79.45% reported the absence of students in training in the diagnostic radiology units. Discussion: There is an exception in compliance with the protocols, presumably due to a misconception of the protocols. Scientific evidence demonstrates that the best guarantee for patient safety with immediate ADRs is not premedication but first aid, and 24.66% of the nurses interviewed are unable to provide this because they have not received any relevant training. Conclusions: In clinical practice, nurses must systematically apply drafted, shared, and approved protocols and must be included in a continuing education program for BLS procedures. Further research on this topic is recommended.

title: Triage Infermieristico in Pronto Soccorso: analisi delle sottostime e sovrastime nell’assegnazione del codice rosso
text: Introduction: The accuracy of a triage decision is very important. In the nursing triage process, the greatest critical issues arise when lower (= underestimation) or higher (= overestimation) priority codes are assigned compared to the patient's condition. An underestimation can lead to delays in accessing medical visits and treatment, while an overestimation can cause delays in providing treatment to patients with lower codes. While the application of the triage system in Emergency Departments is now a widespread practice, assessing the correct assignment of the assigned code remains little studied. Purpose: This retrospective study aims to analyze the phenomenon of underestimations and overestimations in the assignment of red codes by analyzing the concordance between the nursing triage coding and the coding assigned by the physician at the conclusion of the assessment process. The appropriateness of this assessment is based on the Emilia-Romagna Region's indicators and standards and the triage protocols of the Triage Training Group (GFT) as the analysis tool. Materials and Methods: The study was conducted by analyzing all triage records of patients assigned a red code upon admission and/or discharge from two emergency departments in a province of the Emilia-Romagna region, relating to the year 2009. Results and Discussion: The data collected showed that nurses in the two emergency departments analyzed tended to underestimate excessively. In Hospital A, during 2009, the underestimation rate was 6.2%, while in Hospital B it was 10%. Conversely, in both emergency departments, the overestimation rates of red codes fell within the appropriate range. Conclusions: Since the underestimations did not meet the expected standards, although delays were limited and there were no negative impacts on patient outcomes, it is nevertheless considered necessary to adopt corrective measures to reduce these percentages and keep them within 2%. The tools that will be used will be retraining of nurses, periodic analysis of all underestimations, and verification of identified critical cases.

title: 平成22年版 厚生労働白書・新型インフルエンザの性質と特徴
text: Influenza is an infectious disease caused by the influenza virus and is classified into three types: "Type A," "Type B," and "Type C" *1. Type A, to which the "novel influenza (A/H1N1)" that spread from 2009 to 2010 belongs, is classified into many "subtypes" based on the properties of the proteins on the surface of the virus. Type A is originally an avian virus, and theoretically there are 16 x 9 subtypes, and it is known that some infect not only humans but also birds, horses, pigs, etc. For example, the influenza virus called "A Hong Kong type," which had been spreading every year until then, is "A/H3N2," and the "A Soviet type" is "A/H1N1." In addition, "avian influenza," which has occurred in large numbers in various Asian countries since 2003 and caused significant damage to the poultry industry in Japan, is "H5N1." Influenza viruses can mutate while multiplying within a host or hybridize with the genes of other influenza viruses, resulting in the formation of viruses with new characteristics. Influenza strains such as "A Hong Kong type" and "A Soviet type" mutate slightly each year, changing their properties (antigenic changes), and have been prevalent almost every year from winter to early spring; they are also called "seasonal influenza." However, the current novel influenza (A/H1N1) is a different type from the seasonal influenza that has been prevalent in the past (its genetic structure is different). The symptoms of this novel influenza (A/H1N1) are largely similar to those of seasonal influenza, and the number of severe cases and deaths has not been reported as high as initially feared. However, it is quite possible that another "novel influenza" will emerge in the future, requiring an even stronger response than this time. Furthermore, there remains the possibility that avian influenza (H5N1) could become easily transmitted from person to person in the future, leading to a global pandemic. The Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare is working closely with the World Health Organization (WHO) and various governments to gather information and promptly and clearly disclose the information obtained to the public, while taking necessary measures in a timely and appropriate manner. We would also appreciate it if the public would accurately grasp the information regarding the epidemic situation and take appropriate measures according to their individual circumstances, such as in their local area, workplace, school, and other family and social life. Symptoms of the novel influenza that has spread this time include sudden high fever, cough, sore throat, fatigue, as well as runny nose/nasal congestion and headache. Most people who are infected and develop symptoms recover with mild symptoms, but some people with underlying medical conditions are at high risk of developing severe symptoms*2. In particular, people with underlying medical conditions as shown in Figure 1-1-2 need to take precautions to avoid infection during the epidemic, such as frequent handwashing and avoiding crowded places, and those around them also need to take precautions to prevent infection.

title: 平成23年版 厚生労働白書・がん対策の推進
text: Cancer has been the leading cause of death in Japan since 1981, and currently, more than 300,000 people die from it annually. It is also estimated that one in two men and one in three women will develop cancer in their lifetime. Furthermore, the number of deaths from cancer is expected to continue to increase in line with the aging population. For this reason, the government has implemented research-focused initiatives since 1984 with the "Comprehensive 10-Year Strategy Against Cancer," followed by the "New 10-Year Strategy to Overcome Cancer" in 1994, and the "Third Comprehensive 10-Year Strategy Against Cancer" in 2004, resulting in advancements in cancer diagnosis and treatment technologies. Furthermore, based on the "Basic Act on Cancer Control" enacted through a legislative initiative by Diet members in June 2006, the "Basic Plan for Promoting Cancer Control" (hereinafter referred to as the "Basic Plan") was approved by the Cabinet in June 2007, and cancer control measures are being promoted comprehensively and systematically. Regarding radiotherapy and chemotherapy, which are part of cancer treatment in Japan, there have been criticisms that the provision system for these is insufficient. Therefore, the Basic Plan positions "promotion of radiotherapy and chemotherapy" as one of the issues that should be addressed as a priority, and sets goals such as establishing a system to implement radiotherapy and outpatient chemotherapy at all "cancer treatment collaboration base hospitals" (medical institutions designated by the Minister of Health, Labour and Welfare to provide high-quality cancer treatment anywhere in the country. These hospitals provide specialized cancer treatment, build collaborative systems for regional cancer treatment, and provide consultation support and information to cancer patients) by fiscal year 2011. For this reason, in March 2008, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare revised the "Guidelines for the Development of Cancer Treatment Collaboration Hub Hospitals" (hereinafter referred to as the "Guidelines") and implemented training for physicians and other personnel involved in radiation therapy and chemotherapy in order to improve the quality of radiation therapy and chemotherapy. Since many cancer patients suffer physical and psychological pain from the time they are diagnosed with cancer, and their families also suffer various kinds of pain, the basic plan positions "implementation of palliative care from the early stages of treatment" as one of the issues that should be addressed with priority, and sets a goal that all physicians involved in cancer treatment will acquire basic knowledge of palliative care through training, etc., within 10 years. Therefore, in order to achieve this goal by fiscal year 2011, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare established model programs for training content in April 2008 as "Guidelines for Holding Palliative Care Training Sessions for Physicians Involved in Cancer Treatment." These guidelines include: ① conducting training for physicians who are primarily responsible for providing palliative care at "cancer treatment collaboration base hospitals," etc., so that they can guide palliative care training in each region; and ② conducting palliative care training for physicians involved in cancer treatment in each region, conducted by these physicians. Furthermore, the Ministry is working to establish a system that can provide appropriate palliative care, including ③ developing palliative care teams composed of physicians and nurses with specialized knowledge and skills in palliative care, and ④ developing a system that can provide palliative care in outpatient settings. In addition, the Ministry is working to promote the appropriate use of medical narcotics necessary for palliative care by promoting awareness of palliative care among the general public and by holding workshops for medical professionals.

title: СОВРЕМЕННЫЕ АСПЕКТЫ И ПРОБЛЕМЫ ВАКЦИНАЦИИ
text: In some areas of Africa, due to the widespread prevalence of infectious diseases, the average life expectancy is still 35-40 years [1, 2]. In the last 40 years, 72 new infectious diseases have been identified; a resurgence of "old" infections is also observed after a significant decline in their prevalence. Numerous studies have confirmed the association of certain somatic and oncological diseases with infectious agents. Vaccination is an area of medicine that is the subject of much debate. If you ask a specialist (infectious disease specialist, epidemiologist) whether vaccination is necessary, we will hear: "This is the only, safest and most effective means of protecting people from infections and is a major achievement in medicine, having extended human life from 30-40 to 70-80 years." Mass immunization over the last 100 years has not only eliminated many dangerous epidemics, but also reduced mortality and disability. Infections have become rare, and we've begun to forget how severe they can be and the consequences they cause. This has created the false impression that all is well, raising the question: are the measures offered by medicine (vaccines) necessary and are they safe? Therefore, specialists have begun to study the effects that vaccines can cause. Particular attention has been paid to the problem of post-vaccination complications, which has been widely discussed both in our country and internationally since the 1950s and 1960s. During this time, it has become clear why such reactions are possible, that the quality of vaccines has improved, measures to prevent complications have been developed, and, most importantly, it has been proven that the solution does not lie in refusing vaccinations [3, 4]. Unfortunately, recently, publications and programs have appeared in the media focusing on the negative effects of vaccinations, and the authors of these reports are not always conscientious in their selection of material.

title: Вакцина против ротавирусной инфекции как кандидат для включения в Национальный календарь профилактических прививок
text: According to the state report "On the state of sanitary and epidemiological well-being of the population in the Russian Federation in 2015", the incidence rate of acute intestinal infections in the Russian Federation was 545.89 per 100 thousand population, which was practically no different from the 2014 figure [4]. At the same time, the share of acute intestinal infections of unknown etiology accounted for 63.4% of cases. Among acute intestinal infections of established etiology, viral infections predominated (60%). Moreover, 84.5% of cases of acute intestinal infections of viral etiology were accounted for by acute respiratory viral infections. From 2010 to 2014, the incidence of acute respiratory viral infections stabilized at high rates - 69.6-74.9 per 100 thousand population, in 2015 an increase in incidence by 14.0% was noted - more than 124.8 thousand cases were registered, the incidence rate was 85.45 per 100 thousand population. Statistical accounting of RVI incidence is hampered by incomplete registration of cases, however, the registered data (the incidence rate of RVI in children under 1 year of age in 2015 was 1307, and 1442 per 100,000 children in this age group among children aged 1-2 years) indicate the seriousness of the problem [4, 5]. In 2016, the incidence of RVI stabilized at the 2015 level and amounted to 83.26 per 100,000 population [6]. In 2016, the positive trend of decreasing the proportion of RVI incidence registered in children of younger age groups continued. The proportion of RVI cases in children under 12 months has decreased from 26.3 to 22.1% over the past 5 years. The highest incidence of acute respiratory viral infections in 2016 was observed in the Trans-Baikal Territory, the Republics of Buryatia, Dagestan, Sakha (Yakutia), Novosibirsk Oblast, and elsewhere. Incidence rates more than 10 times lower than the Russian average were observed in the Chechen and Karachay-Cherkess Republics and the Republic of North Ossetia. This, along with high incidence rates of acute intestinal infections of unknown etiology in these same regions, may indicate insufficient work by medical organizations in diagnosing acute respiratory viral infections.

title: Espiritualidad y salud: problemas de salud durante el embarazo y el puerperio y sus consecuencias en las trayectorias de mujeres y niños (Salta, Argentina)
text: Our research acknowledges its roots in studies initiated in the 1970s in the Molinos department. Much of this initial body of documentation describes culturally specific illnesses affecting individuals at different stages of their lives, as well as references to beliefs and practices surrounding their etiology, symptomatology, and treatment. As a result, issues emerge that justify the need to address the variability of beliefs and practices related to healthcare, incorporating case studies into the approach to strategies for dealing with illness in its articulation with other domains of collective life, thus transcending expert discourse. Research resumed in 2009, focusing on the study of child-rearing and healthcare practices through caregivers' narratives and observation of their domestic routines and daily itineraries. The aim is to identify, characterize, and evaluate the factors that shape the developmental niche and its impact on children's health trajectories from an ecological perspective. From there, a line of inquiry opens up, focused on the study of cases and pathways related to maternal and child health care during the perinatal period. Within this framework, we are interested in the description and comparative analysis of therapeutic sequences involving, for example, episodes of fright and other local categories of illness, identifying the actors, relationships, and resources selected and articulated in their development. These sequences are of interest to us insofar as they connect the health trajectories of mothers and their children and reveal the expectations and values surrounding children's growth and development. Methodologically, this research follows a qualitative design and is based on the complementary use of semi-structured interviews, observations (systematic, spot, and participant), and audiovisual recording. The discursive information on which this article is based comes from interviews conducted with 33 women of varying ages (18 to 70 years) who are caregivers for children under 6 years old. Some of these women were interviewed more than once between 2009 and 2017. They were selected based on their diverse household compositions, locations, and subsistence levels, as well as their varying access to educational and healthcare institutions. Each interview lasted an average of one and a half hours. From these, we selected 12 narratives that illustrate the sequences of interest for the analysis and the diversity of life trajectories among the interviewees. For each narrative, we identified categories used to refer to ailments suffered during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period, as well as expressions used to describe symptoms and the sequence of diagnoses and treatments applied. We also delineated the events that preceded and followed the reported episodes. We comparatively analyzed the narratives to identify and characterize recurrences and differences using NVivo 10. This software allows us to formalize, code, and systematize qualitative data and identify categories for describing the conceptual field and its semantic relationships. This research was ethically approved by the Bioethics Committee of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences (Catholic University of Salta). The interviewees provided their free and informed consent in accordance with Law 25326, and their personal data was protected through the use of initials.

title: Escuela comunitaria para modificación de conocimientos en pacientes con hipertensión arterial
text:
The results regarding age and sex coincide, according to both national and international authors, with those reported by the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES), which recorded a clear increase in the disease among women. This finding aligns with the theory that hypertension is more frequent in women after age 50, due to the combination of weight gain and age-related hormonal changes.

In São Paulo, Cervato et al. found in their series that most patients suffered from stage I hypertension, which allows physicians to implement preventative health measures and, therefore, reduces the risk of progressing to stages II or III. This result is consistent with the findings in this case study. According to other opinions on the matter, it is possible to work towards achieving better control and appropriate rehabilitation for those classified in advanced stages of the disease, with a view to preventing serious complications and even death or disability.

It is worth noting that in this study population, patients in stage I hypertension predominated, since these are the patients with whom the family doctor can manage in their office. This is not the case with those categorized in the more advanced stage, who require care at the secondary level and, sometimes, hospitalization.

It was very encouraging that 93.8% of hypertensive patients gained a better understanding of the symptoms and signs of their disease, considering that they had to live with them. The percentage of those who continued to have inadequate knowledge, and consequently, those who required more intensive medical intervention to ensure they acquired the necessary information, was practically negligible. In fact, efforts to achieve this began immediately.

Regarding pharmacological treatment, the results coincide with those obtained in educational interventions carried out in other regions, where a significant variation in the use and abuse of sedatives was also found.

A decisive factor in reducing sedative use was the application of Cattell's IPATT (Individualized Attention to Tranquilizers), as it demonstrated to patients that many of them were resorting to these tranquilizers unnecessarily, since there was no justification for their use, given that the anxiety they experienced was normal in their case.

It is important to highlight that in the study, at the beginning and end of each session, the blood pressure of each participant was taken to evaluate the variation in blood pressure readings after the application of the corresponding techniques. This allowed for the discontinuation of unnecessary medications or the readjustment of the dosage.

The information provided in the sessions ensured a positive change in the group's knowledge, making this teaching-learning method effective and very well received by the participants in the health field.

title: Waganga, Wakunga na Wananchi Mkoani Pwani Waipongeza Serikali kwa Kuboresha Huduma za Afya.
text:
Doctors, Midwives and Citizens of the Coast Region have commended the Fifth Phase Government for the steps it is taking to improve health services by providing funds for the expansion of health centers and the construction of District hospitals in the region.

The commendations were given by the health stakeholders earlier this week, while commending President Magufuli for the great efforts he is making.
