The Acting Medical Officer of the Lugoba Health Center, Chalinze Council, Dr. Maganga Kazuri said they have received shillings. 400 million from the central government where the funds have been used to build five new buildings at the center, which are a laboratory building, surgery, mother and child, morgue and the house of the medical officer in charge of the center.

He said these improvements directly affect them as service providers as well as citizens who are currently receiving good and modern services.

"We were forced to refer patients to Tumbi or Bagamoyo hospitals due to the lack of surgical services at the facility, but due to these improvements, the service is provided here at the facility," said Dr. Maganga.

For his part, the Medical Officer of Kerege Health Center, Bagamoyo District Council, Dr. Nyangasi Gideon has commended President Magufuli for the efforts he is making in improving health services which has given them the morale to work and provide better services to the citizens.

"We officially started the construction of the Kerege center in October, 2017 which was completed in March, 2018 and officially started providing services to the citizens of Mapinga, Kerege and Kiromo wards, where after the improvements 360 mothers have given birth," said Dr. Nyangasi.

He said, before the facility was renovated, it was receiving two to ten mothers every day.

He also said, mil. 500 provided by the Government have built a laboratory, a mother and child building, a surgery building and a doctor's house. The remaining funds were used to build a morgue and a laundry building.

Meanwhile, the Regional Health Centre Nurse, Kibaha Town Council, Immaculate Sangu said the improvements made at the centre will relieve the congestion of patients where it receives 350 to 400 patients per month.

title: Uchambuzi wa Maudhui katika Matangazo ya Ngono-Salama kwenye Ukurasa wa Shabiki wa Durex Facebook
text:
Purdy (2011) says that condoms are the second method of protection against sexually transmitted diseases and family planning. Companies and governments around the world have started advertising on social media to sensitize members of society about this method. By simply clicking on the topic of sex on social media, the results are many, for example; videos, images, texts that can be viewed and read by anyone as long as they are connected to the network. The texts of safe sex advertisements on social media emphasize content that shows sexual pleasure. This study examined the content that is dominant in Durex advertisements.

Some countries have enacted laws that regulate advertisements related to sex. The Kenya Films and Classification Board (KFCB) in 2015 opposed the airing of safe sex advertisements on television and radio from 5 am to 10 pm (Standard Media Group, 2015). The KFCB claimed that such advertisements encourage society, especially children, to participate in sex. Safe sex advertisements were moved to social media because they were not properly regulated by law. This study examined in depth the content emphasized in Durex advertisements based on the theory of critical discourse analysis to uncover hidden themes that emerge from the advertisements.

title: York
text:
Although only the sixth-largest city in Yorkshire and having no official status, York is regarded as the county's capital, and is also positioned just east of its geographic centre. For 1800 years, it was the largest and most important city in northern England, though today has a rather modest population just shy of 200,000 people. Despite its size, York packs in more history and culture than many much larger places, and is a fascinating and beautiful destination any time of year.

York city centre is a compact and dense warren of mostly pedestrianised streets lined with centuries-old buildings in a mix of architectural styles, from timber frame medieval structures, to much grander stone and brick edifices from later periods. The centre straddles both banks of two rivers - the Ouse (pronounced ooze) and the Foss - which merge just south of the castle. At the city's heart stands the imposing York Minster, one of the largest Gothic cathedrals in the world, and the mother church for northern England's Anglican community. The Archbishop of York (Stephen Cottrell, as of 2020) holds the third-highest office in the Church of England, after the Archbishop of Canterbury and the Queen. York's old town is completely encircled by a series of defensive medieval walls. At just over 2 miles (3.2 km) long, 13 feet (4 m) high, and 6 feet (1.8 m) thick, they are the UK's most extensive and best-preserved city walls.

Most visitor attractions are within or just outside these walls, so you will seldom find yourself venturing into York's outer neighbourhoods. However, if you do, you will find them pleasant and residential, mostly containing red brick houses from the 19th and 20th centuries. There is a modern university campus around Heslington in the south-eastern suburbs, a large racecourse called the Knavesmire in the south-west, and extensive parks along the Ouse's journey through the northern and southern suburbs. This urban sprawl is bounded by a modern day city wall of sorts: the ring road separates York from its rural surroundings, the well-endowed farmlands and villages of the Vale of York.

title: Edinburgh
text:
This was an exciting place to be 300-350 million years ago, as volcanoes raged and flared across the region. The biggest was what we now call Arthur's Seat, with smaller cones at Castle Rock, Calton Hill, and elsewhere. Then they fizzled out and started to be buried by other rock layers. Much later came the Ice Ages, the last some 20,000 years ago. Vast glaciers from the west scoured away the surface, but where they hit Castle Rock they had to divide and flow around. They left the Rock intact with a scooped-out hollow to its north, west and south, and a tail of stone debris dumped in its lee to the east. This created an obvious defensible spot for early settlement. By the 12th century Edinburgh was the chief city of Scotland; the Old Town grew up with the Castle at its head, the Royal Mile stretching down the debris tail, and Holyrood Palace at its foot.

And up and up it grew: space was limited, so buildings became taller, ten or more storeys high even in medieval times. But no lifts or pumped water of course, and sanitation was taken care of by opening a window, shouting "Gardyloo!" and letting gravity do the rest. Every medieval city stank, but Edinburgh became known as "Auld Reekie" from the distinctive stench of sewage mingled with smoke from coal, mined and burned here from early times.

Edinburgh lost some of its importance after 1707, when Scotland united with England and political power ebbed away to London. But in the mid-18th century it revived, when it broke out of the confines of the Old Town, by creating a graceful New Town to the north. The intervening midden, the "Nor Loch", was drained, bridged, and an earth mound pushed across. There was similar expansion on the south side. Victorian times saw an industrial boom fuelled by the coal deposits nearby to the east, and by shale oil produced to the west. Canals and then railways brought in materials and a labour force.

title: من "روضة" دمشق إلى "آينشتاين" برلين.. خفقة قلب
text:
Once, a friend arranged to meet me at a café called Al-Rawda on Al-Abed Street in Damascus, a place I hadn't known before. As soon as I entered, I was overcome with a sudden joy. I felt my body blossom like a rose on a summer night, floating on clouds like a Sufi, my heart floating on waters of spirit like a prophet after receiving a divine revelation. It was the same feeling I had when I found "my seat" at the Einstein Café in Berlin, where I'm writing now (although today, June 10, 2019, I'm writing from a different seat because someone has taken mine, and I'm waiting for them to leave).

Amidst this spiritual surge, I also encountered the poet Muzaffar al-Nawab at the café/Al-Rawda, which I had just discovered. I greeted him and went to my friend's table. From then on, this café became my familiar place, my home in Damascus, and, as I would gradually discover, the home of Damascus's intellectuals and artists.

My favorite chair, when I was alone without friends, was the one overlooking Al-Abed Street, right by the glass. As soon as I sat down, the hookah and freshly brewed tea would be brought to me in a small cup. I would spend pleasant moments there, my eyes flitting between the book and the life unfolding before me like a television series, the thousandth episode of which I'm watching in Berlin today. In Damascus, the waiter knew my secret to the chair, without even asking or saying a word. As soon as he saw me sit in another chair, he would come over and say, "When the customer leaves, I'll reserve the table for you, don't worry." And indeed, he would delay the hookah until the chair was free, unless the customer had just sat down and was going to be staying a long time.

Einstein's Café in Berlin bears no resemblance to Al-Rawda Café in Damascus, except perhaps for the spiritual connection my imagination has forged between them. Al-Rawda Café in Damascus, established in 1938, embodies the history of Damascus itself. It's rare to find an intellectual, artist, or politician who hasn't frequented this café, located just meters from the Syrian Parliament. It possesses the very essence and spirit of Damascus, a haven of heaven within the earthly realm (the café spans 750 square meters, accommodating approximately 600 chairs and 150 tables). Those who haven't entered the café wouldn't expect to find within it multiple cafés, each with its own clientele, tables, and chairs, and each chair with its own devotee, and each devotee with their own story. There's the section overlooking the street, the open-air section frequented by Damascus's intellectuals, and the interior section, popular with Damascus's artists (actors). Sometimes, the sections and their patrons blend together.

In the morning, you'll always find the café's regulars: retired writers, politicians who've faded from the political scene, political prisoners no one recognizes anymore, political refugees, and former officers released after years of detention simply for contemplating a military coup. Around midday, intellectuals and the unemployed flock there to play chess or backgammon, joined by former employees who've lost their jobs. In the evening and well into the night, you'll rarely find a seat; you feel like you're surrounded by a familiar, yet endearing, bustle—a city within a city.

There are multiple forms of intimacy within this chaotic yet organized space, governed by rules well-known to its patrons. There's an intimacy that connects the café's regulars with its staff, an intimacy between young men and women seeking love or a fleeting night out, and an intimacy among the patrons themselves, where anyone can suddenly sit at your table and strike up a conversation. Friendships are forged here, only to end as soon as you leave the café or due to the ceaseless gossip. This is precisely what's lacking in Einstein's café. There's no connection between the patrons and the café; a fleeting encounter dictated by the fast-paced rhythms of life and capitalism. There's no intimacy between the patrons and the waiters, no regular customers, no conversations between one customer and another. At Einstein's café, the individual is a transient customer, rarely returning or developing a close relationship. In contrast, at Rawda's café, the individual is a seeker, a lover, searching for a moment of longing. This is facilitated by the café's geography and its atmosphere, resembling a Damascene house escaping the confines of modernity.

When I look at the faces of the workers at Einstein Café, I feel that the only similarity to Rawda Café lies here. Their faces suggest they are immigrants or the children of immigrants, university students searching for a source of income to help them withstand life's hardships and complete their studies. They are poor in a way, much like the poor people of Rawda Café in Damascus, most of whom (Arabs, Kurds, and other groups) worked from morning till night to ward off the specter of poverty.

Einstein Café, in both form and spirit, is closer to my café in Beirut, even though all three share the same impoverished workers.

title: رحلة الزيت والشتاء
text:
Every olive harvest season, Afrin attracted hundreds of workers from outside the region, sometimes reaching thousands in bountiful seasons, to work in harvesting the crop. The sheer number of olive trees in Afrin was disproportionate to the population, necessitating assistance from neighboring and distant rural areas. The southern Aleppo countryside provided the largest share of this labor force. Other reasons for the lack of employment among Afrin residents included education, which kept the majority away from agricultural work.

Those who traveled were entire families, young and old, men and women. They left their homes locked behind and went to camp in the olive groves of Afrin. Each family typically made an agreement with a specific landowner, returning annually to his olive groves to harvest the olives.

These families, known locally as "Zayata," were transported by hop-on hop-off buses in a festive procession, complete with the distinctive sound of the bus horns and the loads of olives they carried. Some of these buses would return laden with their cargo a few days later, or even on the same day, due to a family dispute. This was considered a disgrace in the village.

What made this journey so deeply affect me, and what I could express in this text, might be that families took all their children, even those still in school. Their words still echo in my ears:

-Where's so-and-so?

-He went with the olive harvesters.

The olive harvesters would camp in the vineyards for about a month, harvesting thousands of trees.

title: 引領民眾走入森林生態旅遊的絕佳入口 林務局「台灣山林悠遊網」
text: Since the beginning of the 21st century, the preservation and sustainable management of forest diversity has become a global trend, with countries worldwide adopting "environmentally conscious policies" to safeguard the social, economic, ecological, cultural, and spiritual needs of modern and future generations. Taiwan, the "Island of Mountains," boasts 220 mountains exceeding 3,000 meters in altitude. Its rich geological and topographical landscapes have nurtured many precious and unique species, habitats, and ecosystems, attracting numerous people to explore the mountains and experience nature. With ecotourism, hiking, and nature education becoming increasingly popular, the Forestry Bureau has been developing forest recreation services since the 1960s, effectively leveraging the economic and social functions of the forest environment while protecting its ecological balance. However, with the increasing prevalence of information technology, the internet is considered a crucial interface for information transmission and communication in the future information technology society. The various electronic services that accompany the internet, with their speed, convenience, and immediacy, bring a new dimension to modern society, which values knowledge capital and the knowledge economy. Given the ubiquitous reach of the internet, the Forestry Bureau is expanding its forest ecotourism network to assist in the transformation of traditional forestry production into a tertiary industry. At the same time, it is building the "Taiwan Forest Leisure Network" (Figure 1), which transforms the Forestry Bureau's forest ecotourism sites, such as national forest recreation areas, nature education centers, and nature trails, into a system in the online world. This will enable the government to serve the public more quickly and effectively and assist in the development of forest ecotourism. To provide the public with convenient and comprehensive information and services that combine environmental education, leisure and recreation, and life experience, and to fully showcase the development achievements of the forest ecotourism network, effectively implementing the goal of sustainable and healthy forests, the Taiwan Forest Leisure Network is an integrated portal website encompassing guides to the Forestry Bureau's ecotourism sites. In addition to assisting the development of forest ecotourism, it aims to achieve functions such as education and promotion, enhanced interaction, increased international visibility, and forest ecotourism guidance. Based on this, it is planned with 11 functional modules: "Homepage," "National Forest Recreation Areas," "National Trail System," "Plain Forest Parks," "Nature Education Centers," "Leave No Trace" activities, "Home of National Forest Volunteers," "Tourism E-Point," "Digital Forest Chronicle," "Interactive Corner," and "Others." The overall architecture of the portal website is shown in Figure 2. Most experts and scholars emphasize that ecotourism is based on nature and culture, and is responsible and sustainable tourism. Simply put, the core value of ecotourism is natural and cultural resources, and the spirit of the "Taiwan Forest Leisure Network" website is to showcase the natural and cultural resources of forests. Typical recreation or tourism websites often use prominent or large headlines to tell their target audience how fun and attractive the recreational destinations offered by the website are, and how many people have already visited, in order to attract the attention of their target audience as soon as possible. The "Taiwan Forest Leisure Network" is different. Unlike typical travel websites, its two main modules, "National Forest Recreation Areas" (http://recreation.forest.gov.tw) and "National Trail System" (http://trail.forest.gov.tw), do not rely on aggressive marketing to attract visitors to their designated forest ecotourism areas. Instead, they aim to inform the public that these areas not only boast beautiful mountain scenery but also rich forest ecology and cultural resources. The website features abundant images of forests and provides detailed descriptions of the natural environment, ecological resources, and historical sites of each forest recreation area, nature trail system, and plain forest park. Each page unfolds like a captivating story or musical movement, guiding visitors to understand the beauty of these forest ecotourism areas and fostering the motivation and proper attitude to engage in ecotourism there. In this way, the Taiwan Forest Leisure Network attempts to bring the right visitors to the right places.

title: 第 62 輯 產地餐桌綠遊趣 縱谷篇-不只種米，也種下對土地的愛- 鋤禾日好Bike De Koffie
text: Bike De Koffie's owner, Hao Chaoyang, is a young man from the Puyuma tribe in the mountains of Taitung. Born in 1982, he has a refined appearance and exudes a scholarly air, though he jokingly admits that he doesn't actually enjoy studying. After studying international trade and culinary arts, he finally realized that the world of textbooks couldn't satisfy him; instead, he found the skills he learned at the Vocational Training Institute more practical. After completing courses at the Vocational Training Institute, Hao Chaoyang obtained Class C certifications in Chinese cuisine, baking, and bartending. Having previously worked in the coffee sales industry, Hao Chaoyang is not only familiar with the flavors of different types of coffee beans but also learned many marketing techniques. These experiences laid a solid foundation for his entrepreneurial journey. Hao Chaoyang's down-to-earth personality is similar to that of his sister and brother-in-law. Like Hao Chaoyang, his sister, Hao Suqing, and brother-in-law, Wei Wenxuan, also left their hometown to study and work. The couple originally ran an interior design studio in Taichung. After the 921 earthquake, they decided to return to their hometown to grow organic rice and established the bed and breakfast "The Crops Are Ripe" and the backpacker hostel "Good Days with the Farmers," taking guests to the fields to experience farming activities such as rice planting, weeding, pest control, and scarecrow making, bridging the gap between urban dwellers and the land. At the end of 2013, at his sister's invitation, Ah-Yang quit his job in the coffee bean business and returned to Chishang to provide them with afternoon tea in the fields, coffee, and snacks. He also created his own coffee shop, Bike De Koffie, on the first floor of "Good Days with the Farmers." The agricultural experience activities gave rise to Bike De Koffie's signature product, the rice bagel. Initially, the afternoon tea in the fields only included coffee and rice cheese, but later Ah-Yang developed the rice bagel using organic rice grown by his brother-in-law's family. The crispy exterior and soft interior of the bagel, after careful chewing, fills the mouth with the natural aroma of rice. Paired with pineapple and kiwi jam made from Guanshan pineapple, the sweet and sour flavor enhances the bagel's texture, making it more layered. In his second year back in his hometown, he won the "One Person's Farmhouse Table - Most Promising Slow Food Development Award." Ah-Yang continues to unleash his innovative potential, further combining local agricultural products from Taitung, such as Chulu fresh milk, red oolong tea, and millet from Jinfeng Township, to develop many different flavors of rice bagels. In addition, Bike De Koffie also offers pure rice milk without peanuts, rice pudding, and other snacks that best represent Chishang, the rice-producing region.

title: Fahrradtouren rund um Cottbus
text: The grand Spreewald tour is a beautiful full-day excursion that explores a large part of the Upper Spreewald. You leave Cottbus heading northwest, passing through the villages of Briesen and Guhrow, and approach the Spree River near Schmogrow. Continue along the Spree dike until the cycle path branches off to the left towards Burg. Follow this path for a short distance and then continue on the Nordweg (Northern Path) and the Ringchaussee (Ring Road) to Buschmühle. Those wishing to take a break beforehand, or to enjoy the view of the surrounding area from the Bismarck Tower, should not turn onto the Nordweg immediately upon reaching the Spree, but continue straight ahead and take a detour of about one kilometer to the tower and the Bismarck Inn. Returning to Buschmühle, continue north to Straupitz. After a short break and a visit to the Schinkel Church and the Dutch windmill, the route continues across the meadows north of the Hochwald (High Forest) through the villages of Neu Zauche and Alt Zauche. The route takes a wide arc along scenic paths through the eastern end of the Upper Spreewald forest to Lübbenau. After exploring the old town center, the journey continues to the Spreewald village of Leipe. From there, the route leads past the Waldschlösschen (Little Forest Castle) to Burg. The final leg takes travelers back to the starting point in Cottbus via Werben and Briesen. Note: The route described here, which can be downloaded, leads directly from the Lübbenau Spreewald harbor to Leipe. Those wishing to visit Lübbenau Castle and the charming open-air museum village of Lehde should consider taking this slight detour; it's not a significant out-of-bounds, but visiting these sites will require some additional time.

title: Heldrastein
text: The trail climbs steadily through mixed forest (partly via steps) to the Großenburschla - Schnellmannshausen road. Here, at the car park at an altitude of 340 meters, you've covered about half the elevation gain and distance. It's "only" 1.1 km to the summit. Incidentally, there are covered rest areas at the car park. From here, the really interesting part of the trail begins. A well-maintained path with steps leads steeply uphill through the beech forest. Those who want to take a breather can use the benches along the way. There are occasional beautiful views of the valley. You steadily approach the northern slopes of the Heldrastein, which the trail overcomes in a final effort. After more than 400 steps, you reach the summit plateau at an altitude of approximately 490 meters. From here, it's another 400-500 meters or so to the summit (503.8 meters) on a pleasant, wide track.

title: प्रकृति की गोद में तीन दिन
text:
The next morning, we set out to visit the Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary. Kerala's roads are excellent. Once, during a discussion in Parliament about roads, someone compared them to the cheeks of Om Puri and Hema Malini. Bihar's roads were described as being like Om Puri's cheeks; then, Kerala's roads are like Hema Malini's cheeks—absolutely smooth. Abdul, our taxi driver, could accelerate to the speed of an airplane in the blink of an eye. I had to tell him all the way, "I love Allah Miya, but not so much that I want to go to meet him a few years in advance."

On the way, we passed Pookode Lake. It's a picnic spot: peaceful, clean, and beautiful. Such cleanliness is rarely seen in a picnic spot; it was a delight. It was a bit sunny, so instead of boating, we decided to explore it on foot. After a while, we noticed some children singing on the boat. The song was in tune and sounded good, but I couldn't understand it. After the round, we met with these children and their teachers. I talked to them about their school and the song.

title: लखीमपुर खीरी की ऐतिहासिक धरोहर–‘विलोबी मेमोरियल’
text:
In the city of Lakhimpur Kheri, Uttar Pradesh, there is a nearly hundred-year-old historical monument called the "Willoughby Memorial." It's natural for a history student to step into any historical building and wonder about what, why, how, and for what. These questions constantly clashed with each other in search of logical answers. In answering these questions, we found some evidence and some legends related to the Willoughby Memorial. Generally, the people of Lakhimpur aren't particularly aware of it, except for its location as a protest site, a playground, a wedding venue, and a political party meeting place. Architecturally, this red building doesn't make a significant impression at first glance, nor is it a remarkable example of architecture. However, built in 1924, it holds historical significance. Although the surrounding area is known as Willoughby, even in this era of the information revolution, searching for it yields very little information. As students of history, it is our responsibility to draw the attention of intellectuals to this issue, to explore how this historical monument and its library can be made more useful to the general public.

To gather information, we visited the site and gathered information from both young and old members of the city. We received important documents from the Willoughby Memorial Trust's current secretary, Dr. Ajay Kumar Aga, Associate Professor of Zoology. The Aga family has served as the trust's secretary for four generations.

title: Itinerario francescano ad Assisi
text: This itinerary aims to follow the life of Saint Francis through visits to the Franciscan sites of Assisi (including easily accessible neighboring hamlets such as Rivotorto and Santa Maria degli Angeli). Many of these sites were the scene of numerous events, some at the beginning and end of the saint's life, so there will be many "crossroads" (you may witness the consequences of events that have yet to happen chronologically in Saint Francis's life). Furthermore, a fair balance has been sought between the chronological order of events and a "practical" order (for example, trying to place two nearby sites next to each other, even if they were not strictly chronologically consequential). The third day of the itinerary contains just a few stops, ideally filling only the morning and thus allowing for an easy return home if you are coming from far away. The ideal times to complete the itinerary are late spring or early autumn (even summer, if desired, as long as you don't choose excessively hot days). In practice, good weather is definitely recommended to enjoy the walk and the natural spaces, which are a crucial aspect of the journey. Furthermore, if you can choose the days of the week, it's best to go when there aren't too many people (for example, avoid religious holidays), to better enjoy the spiritual atmosphere without being overwhelmed by people (Assisi can be very crowded during the canonical holiday periods, especially religious ones). More than a simple tourist itinerary, it is also, and above all, a spiritual journey. Try to experience it as such, savoring the moments without rushing and trying to immerse yourself in what happened. If you are Christian, it will be natural to offer moments of prayer in the most important and meaningful places. During visits to the sacred sites (which will inevitably be the focus of the journey), it is mandatory to respect basic rules: maintain as much silence as possible and do not take photos or videos if prohibited. It is often possible to ask the friars who manage the churches or convents to accompany you on the visit to help you understand the history of the place. Although not mandatory, a donation is always appreciated (even more so if you are accompanied).

title: Castel Goffredo
text: Known worldwide for its production of women's hosiery—hence its nickname, "Stocking City"—Castel Goffredo is part of Textile District No. 6 in the provinces of Mantua and Brescia, home to over 250 industrial and artisanal businesses. The town was an independent fiefdom from 1444 to 1602 (Marquisate of Castel Goffredo) and one of the capitals of the Gonzaga States. In 1511, Marquis Aloisio Gonzaga founded the cadet branch of the Gonzaga family of Castel Goffredo, which died out in 1593. Under his rule, the town became an important fortress city, protected by seven towers and surrounded by a defensive moat; in the 18th century, the demolition of the walls began. In the 1840s, Castel Goffredo was the center of anti-Austrian conspiracies in the Upper Mantua area and attracted numerous patriots, led by the castellan Giovanni Acerbi, who later became the intendant of Garibaldi's Thousand. In 1859, it was the site of the Battle of Solferino. Since 1987, it has been one of the "100 municipalities of little, great Italy." It acquired city status in 2002 and is the eighth most populous municipality in the province of Mantua. It is among the municipalities promoting the "Ecomuseum between the Chiese, the Tartaro, and the Osone." Since 2017, Castel Goffredo has participated with its monuments in Wiki Loves Monuments, organized by Wikimedia Italia. In July 2020, it received the recognition of City that Reads 2020-2021.

title: 平成23年版 観光白書
text: Tourism in Furano City has developed primarily around the former Furano Town area. In the 1960s, tourism in the city began with the development of a ski resort-centered tourism industry, funded by local entities including the city government. Although this initiative ultimately failed, in the 1970s, the mayor initiated the attraction of a major resort development group, which promoted the full-scale development of the resort area. Subsequently, by strengthening existing resources, Furano established itself as a year-round tourist destination. In the 1970s, alongside these existing developments, efforts also began to develop tourism centered on agriculture, the city's core industry. Lavender became popular after being featured in the former Japanese National Railways calendar. Furthermore, the construction of a wine house as part of Furano City's nature recreation village project expanded both the tourist area and the number of people involved. In the 1980s, the city became known as a national tourist destination thanks to the popularity of television dramas set in Furano. In 1988, a hotel by the aforementioned major resort development group was constructed, adding a new appeal as the setting for television dramas, in addition to the previous efforts. In Furano City, the agricultural sector has developed further due to market expansion, and efforts to promote agricultural tourism are progressing. Furthermore, since 1994, the city has begun collaborating with surrounding municipalities, and since 2005, it has been working to attract overseas tourists, among other initiatives aimed at ensuring a stable number of visitors.

title: 平成22年版 観光白書
text: In France, the right to paid leave was first granted to workers in 1936. Subsequently, under the Mitterrand administration, the vacation check system was legalized and remains in place today. Initially, the vacation check system was only for salaried employees of companies with 50 or more employees, but this restriction was removed in a 1999 amendment, and a 2009 amendment made it easier for companies with fewer than 50 employees to implement it. France's annual paid leave law is commonly known as the "vacation law." When it was enacted in 1936, annual paid leave was two weeks, but after several amendments, it is now five weeks. The law stipulates that, in principle, four weeks of annual paid leave must be taken between May 1st and October 31st, and the remaining week between November 1st and May 31st of the following year. Furthermore, it is mandatory that two of the four weeks be taken consecutively. This system was introduced in 1982 with the establishment of the National Vacation Check Agency and aims to support workers' vacations. Companies contribute 20-80% in addition to workers' savings to purchase vacation checks from the National Vacation Check Agency and distribute them to their employees. Partial reductions in social insurance contributions are applied to purchasing companies. Vacation checks can be used at more than 130,000 establishments in France, including accommodations, transportation, restaurants, and sports venues. In 2008, the total amount of vacation checks issued was approximately 1.2 billion euros (approximately 180 billion yen), and the number of users was approximately 3 million (including those who benefited but did not use the checks, the total was approximately 7.5 million). Introduced in 2004 with the aim of alleviating loneliness among the elderly, building social solidarity, and improving the occupancy rate of holiday facilities during the off-season, the National Vacation Check Agency provides a daily allowance of 140 euros to seniors aged 60 and over who have not taken a long vacation. During the off-season, it is possible to stay in a vacation village, and support such as inexpensive bus services and various exchange events are provided.

title: Великий Новгород
text:
Founded in ancient times, Veliky Novgorod served for several centuries as the commercial, political, and cultural center of the entire Russian North. Conducting a lively trade with Western Europe, the city had very close ties with the Hanseatic League, although it was not formally a member. With the rise of first Kyiv, then Moscow, and later St. Petersburg, Novgorod gradually lost its former power and by the 18th century had become a quiet provincial town with a large number of monuments reminiscent of its former grandeur.

Wooden buildings predominated in ancient Novgorod, but the most significant religious buildings were constructed of stone. This, coupled with Novgorod's escape from the Mongol-Tatar raids, allows us to see the stages in the development of the Novgorod style, which evolved from its imitation of Byzantine churches, exemplified by the grandiose St. Sophia Cathedral, to the pinnacle of Novgorod architecture in the 14th and 15th centuries, represented by the churches of the Savior on Ilyin, Theodore Stratelates on the Ruchey, and Peter and Paul in Kozhevniki. After its annexation by Moscow, the city's distinctive architecture came under the influence of Moscow's canons, although local flavor is still evident in 16th-century monuments. Novgorod's subsequent development followed Russian traditions. Like other cities, it experienced redevelopment, leading to the absurd results of rebuilding old churches and new construction in all the prescribed styles.

Unfortunately, most of the ancient monuments were destroyed during the Great Patriotic War, and in the first years of reconstruction, due to a shortage of building materials, many of the ruins of ancient buildings were dismantled for their bricks and ruins. Nevertheless, the city's restoration plan—designed by A.V. Shchusev, an expert in ancient Russian architecture—envisioned the creation of an urban environment in which ancient monuments and modern structures would harmoniously coexist. Although actual construction quickly exceeded the project's scope, overall, today's Novgorod has achieved the near-impossible: in the historic center, modern buildings modestly coexist with majestic churches standing proudly in open spaces, and the lack of residential buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries is more than compensated for by numerous cozy parks and urban alleys.

title: Старая Русса
text:
Staraya Russa is located in the southern Ilmen region, 96 km from Novgorod by road and only 60 km as the crow flies. The city stands at the confluence of the Porus'ya River, also known as the Pererytitsa, with the Polist' River, which in turn is a tributary of the larger Lovat' River, which flows 15 km to the east. The city's inhabitants are called Rushans.

The origins of Staraya Russa are shrouded in legend. According to one, princes Sloven and Rus founded the cities of Slovensk (the future Novgorod) and Rusa near Lake Ilmen. Another legend holds that Sloven never existed, and that Lech and Czech, the founders of Poland and the Czech Republic, joined Rusa in his stead. Scholarly versions of the legends associate the name "Staraya Russa" (until the 16th century, simply "Rusa") with the Rus tribe, which either lived in the Ilmen region before the arrival of the Varangians, or were themselves Varangians—Rurik's retinue—who arrived in the then-nonexistent and nameless "Rus." However, neither buildings nor even archaeological sites from the 9th century have been discovered in the territory of Staraya Russa, so the official date of the city's founding is considered to be 1167—the first mention in the chronicles, although the oldest finds date back to the mid-10th century, i.e., the semi-legendary pre-Christian period of Ancient Rus' history. Later, Staraya Russa became one of the most significant northwestern cities and a center of salt production, and the Lovat River served as a trade route "from the Varangians to the Greeks."

From its founding, Staraya Russa was under the influence of Novgorod, as evidenced by the birch bark letters, of which more than forty have been discovered here. From the late 15th century, the city fell under Moscow's control, without losing its importance as a trade and salt producer. At the turn of the 16th and 17th centuries, Staraya Russa suffered greatly during the Livonian War, and then during the Time of Troubles, when the Swedes held sway for ten years. A fire in 1763 destroyed all the wooden buildings, after which Staraya Russa was rebuilt with stone houses on a regular rectangular plan. Salt mining gradually declined, but the salt itself remained in demand in the form of mineral waters and the accompanying mud, which began to be used for therapeutic purposes. In 1828, what was arguably Russia's first balneological mud resort opened in Staraya Russa. Over the next 90 years, it was visited by Dobrolyubov, Gorky, the sons of Alexander II, and, of course, F.M. Dostoevsky, who wasn't actually recovering here, but rather seeking refuge from gambling addiction and St. Petersburg creditors. Staraya Russa suited him: there was some cultural life around the resort, but there wasn't much room for carousing. In Staraya Russa, the writer completed "Demons" and wrote the entirety of "The Adolescent" and "The Brothers Karamazov." But don't look for rapturous descriptions of Staraya Russa (or anything else, for that matter) in Dostoevsky's books, for the name of Skotoprigonyevsk, where the novel's action unfolds, conceals Staraya Russa itself. Cattle were indeed driven here, but otherwise there was no trace of Dostoevsky: St. Petersburg society gathered in the summer, a railway had already been built through the city in 1878, and after the Revolution, a tramway was even launched, though it disappeared with the onset of the Great Patriotic War and was never restored.

title: Viaje a La Habana y Varadero, Cuba (II)
text: It's part of the Varadero Internacional Hotel Complex and is located right next to the renowned Hotel Internacional in Varadero, famous for having one of its best beaches. This establishment consists of chalet-style cabins with 1, 2, and 4 bedrooms, totaling 149 rooms, all nestled among coconut palms and right on the beachfront. The one we stayed in was a one-bedroom cabin, with the living room and kitchen on the ground floor and the bedroom and bathroom upstairs. The cleaning was impeccable, carried out by a dedicated employee throughout our stay. It was a First Class (Cuban rating) and all-inclusive. We ate at the "El Galeón" buffet restaurant or at a beach bar serving snacks, hamburgers, and pizzas. There was another snack bar by the pool and a party room with nightly entertainment. The food was just adequate, the beach was excellent, and the activities were limited to water sports lessons, which had to be paid for separately if they involved motors. Guests could use the facilities of the Hotel Internacional and attend its famous Cabaret Continental, after paying an entrance fee. Drinks were included until midnight. We ran into a German group, among whom was a Spanish immigrant, five minutes before midnight. The Germans were stocking up on drinks, up to four mixed drinks per person, so the husbands always ended up drunk and being wheeled back to their rooms on the laundry cart, while their brazen wives took the opportunity to go to the disco with the waiters. Other simple hotels where we stayed in Varadero were the Hotel Atabey, now renamed Palma Real, and the Hotel Club Tropical, part of the Cuban chain Horizontes; we were the first to stay at the latter.

title: Viaje a San Andrés y Cartagena de Indias, Colombia (III)
text: When we arrived, in a reception room, they gave us the usual sales pitch for their excursions. We ignored it; I won't go into the commercial reasons behind it here, but I will mention a new variation so you're aware. It's not uncommon for a couple to approach you offering an emerald, which they present as exceptional, but for financial reasons, they're forced to sell it at a bargain price. They're usually mixed couples, one Colombian and one European, to give you a sense of security, and they've already won your friendship. Don't even think about falling into this trap! A close relative of mine, whom I won't name to avoid embarrassing him again, was scammed this way on his honeymoon. When he arrived back in Spain and the jeweler had the emerald appraised, he estimated its quality to be similar to the crystal used to make champagne bottles. After the ordeal of getting up to our room—the hotel is a 24-story tower with only four elevators—we were rewarded with beautiful views of the city as night fell. All the buildings of the historic center were illuminated, with the dome of the San Pedro Claver Cathedral and the San Felipe de Barajas Castle standing out in the distance. This hotel is very close to the walled city; a stroll along the beach is easily accessible. However, a taxi to the historic center costs just 5,000 pesos. To get around the city, several buses ("chivas") from up to 30 different private companies operate. Currently, the City Council is promoting a project to build bus stops to implement a municipal transport system throughout the district, which they have named Transcaribe. The city beach is disappointing, nestled between breakwaters to protect it from the wind, which creates quite a swell. But there's always the option of taking a boat to the paradisiacal white-sand beach of Isla Barú. You can go by boat or by minibus, which crosses the Magdalena River by ferry to reach its destination. This latter option, although longer, is ideal for enjoying the scenery. Another way to get there independently is to take a minibus from the India Catalina Monument to Pasacaballos (1,300 pesos), then take the ferry across the Magdalena River (1,000 pesos), and finally a motorcycle taxi (10,000 pesos) to Playa Blanca on Isla Barú. The next morning, as we walked through the curtains, we were surprised to see painters hanging from a simple trapeze in front of us, like a circus act, without any safety equipment and at the considerable height of the 18th floor. We had breakfast at the all-you-can-eat buffet restaurant by the pool, which was full of excellent natural fruit juices, and then set off to visit the city.

title: Vivutio vya Utalii vya Tanzania Kuanza Kuonekana Baidu Septemba Hii
text:
Tanzania has focused its efforts on attracting tourists, especially those from abroad, with a particular focus on capturing the Chinese market, which has the largest population in the world. Recently, the Tanzania Tourism Board conducted a major tour to promote Tanzania's tourist attractions in the cities of Beijing, Shanghai, Chengdu, Guangzhou, Hong Kong, Nanjing and Changsha.

Speaking in Dar es Salaam, Chairman of the Tanzania Tourism Board (TTB), Judge Thomas Mihayo, said that the fruits of the visit to China have now begun to be seen with the action of the Baidu company coming to the country to carry out a project to take live and immersive photos of Tanzania's tourist attractions in order to advertise them on the network with more than 700 million followers.

“The fruits of the visit to Chinese cities have begun to be seen where this time a team of 11 experts from the country's largest internet company (Baidu) arrived in the country on August 22, 2019 and visited some of the tourist attractions in the country with the aim of obtaining live and immersive photos to advertise those attractions to the tourism market of more than 700 million people who follow this Baidu network”, said Judge Mihayo.

China is one of the countries in the world that uses their Baidu network, so it is clear that the production of various articles and photos they found from attractions in the country will be able to increase tourists from China as the photos will be seen by more than 700 million users of the network.

He added that the goal of TTB is to enable the tourism sector to get more tourists from China and increase the number of foreign tourists coming to visit Tanzania due to seeing the attractions that will be included in the Wander Planet project from the BAIDU company, from September 2019 onwards.

Mihayo said that out of seven countries in the world, Tanzania has emerged as the first country in the Project and is the only country from the African continent and other countries targeted by the project are from the continents of America, Asia and Europe.

While in the country, the experts in the field of mobile and still photography had the opportunity to visit various tourist destinations in the country including the historical city of Bagamoyo, the Ngorongoro Conservation Area Authority, the Oldvuai Gorge Museum, the Serengeti National Park, Lake Manyara, the City of Mwanza and Zanzibar. And all of these places have been photographed in order to be advertised on the large network with 700 million followers in China.

In addition, Judge Mihayo said that the aim of the experts' visit is to take mobile and still photography and write reports on various tourist attractions in the places they visited and then post them on their network, and they have promised to implement as they aimed to advertise Tanzanian tourism in China where some reports by the World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) explain how China has the largest tourism market in the world.

“Statistics from the World Tourism Organization (UNWTO) show that China is the largest tourism market in the world. In 2018, 130 million Chinese people traveled abroad, while Tanzania received 32,773 tourists, a small number compared to the number of tourists from China to other countries. Therefore, these efforts are being made to capture the Chinese market in this important sector,” said Judge Mihayo.

For his part, the Executive Director of the Tanzania Tourism Board (TTB), Devota Mdachi, said that the Chinese company Baidu has done well to bring in these experts to carry out the work of taking dynamic and dynamic photos and to be able to promote Tanzanian tourism in China to the market of 130 million people who travel abroad to various parts of the world.

"We thank the Baidu company from China for bringing these visitors, as they have seen and what they saw is enough to go and explain it to their home in China. Tanzania has many attractions, so photos and videos taken at attractions that everyone in the world wants to see and visit Tanzania will help bring in more tourists from China," said Mdachi.

title: Watalii 64 Wawasili Dar Kupitia Reli Ya TAZARA
text:
64 tourists from Germany have arrived in Dar es Salaam today via the TAZARA railway from South Africa using the country's famous tourist train known as ROVOS.

The tourists have come to Tanzania to visit various tourist attractions in the country including wildlife parks and the islands of Zanzibar.

Speaking at a short reception for the tourists held at the TAZARA station in Dar es Salaam, TAZARA Tanzania General Manager, Fuad Abdallah explained that the train departed Cape Town in South Africa on August 18, this year. "Various tourists come to the country five times a year using ROVOS via the TAZARA railway and our country benefits from this arrival, especially economic benefits," said Fuad.

He also noted that the ROVOS train is among the three best trains in the world, so the arrival of the train and tourists is due to the excellent tourist attractions and good infrastructure of the TAZARA railway.

“This train uses the TAZARA railway to bring tourists because our country has met the tourism standards and our railway has met the safety and reliable communication standards,” added Fuad. He said that during the train trip, the tourists also had the opportunity to visit the Selous National Park located in southern Tanzania and see the various animals found in the park.

Speaking with joy at arriving in Tanzania, the German tourists said that they had enjoyed the trip and the warm welcome of the Tanzanians and promised to return again.

For her part, a ROVOS train employee, Monica Rieder of German origin, said that she had been to Tanzania 14 times and was impressed by the major developmental changes taking place in the country day by day. TAZARA is a joint railway company of Tanzania and Zambia that began in 1976 and is owned by 50 percent each side.

title: Remarks by the President at Visit with the 2014 NBA Champion San Antonio Spurs
text:
But it's also because this is an international team. It's the U.N. of basketball teams. And it shows the way that this wonderful sport has become an international sport. Some people have, rightfully, started calling it -- the Spur’s style of basketball “the beautiful game.” And when you look at the passing and guys back-cutting the hoop and sharing the basketball, you see basketball the way it should be played. And I was telling these guys you can now see everybody around the league actually stealing, first of all, assistant coaches who then become coaches and then start applying that style of play all around the league. And it's made the game better.

Now, this has not always been the case, all the accolades that the Spur’s received. Let’s face it, just a little while back people were saying that the Spurs were passed their prime, not just old but kind of boring. Now they’re fresh and exciting -- which is basically the exact opposite of what happens to Presidents. (Laughter.) It's a different trajectory.

Last season was all about redemption for the Spurs. Everybody remembers the heartbreaking loss -- for the Spurs, not for Miami -- two years ago. And game six obviously was crazy. I'm not going to make you relive all the details. As Tony Parker said, it seemed like the basketball gods were just being cruel. But the Spurs came back focused.

title: Remarks by the President Honoring the 2015 NCAA Men's Basketball Champion Duke Blue Devils
text: They ran off 14 straight wins to start the season. But by tournament time, they were down to just eight scholarship players -- four freshmen, one senior. They had a soft-spoken all American in the middle, Jahlil Okafor -- from the Chicago area, I might just add -- (laughter) -- whose size and footwork bent defenses in a way that people hadn’t seen in a very long time. There was the Final Four’s Most Outstanding player, Tyus Jones -- or “Tyus Stones” -- (applause) -- because of all the shots he made. There was Justise Winslow flying all over the place -- (laughter) -- dominating some of the games in the tournament. Quinn Cook provided senior leadership, setting a school all-time assist-to-turnover record. (Applause.) And then there was Grayson Allen, who just went crazy -- (laughter and applause) -- who clearly didn’t know any better and just said, well, I’m going to score eight straight points at the end of a game. And in that championship game against Wisconsin, the four freshmen scored every point in the second half. The Blue Devils shut down the most efficient offense in the country when they needed to. And that lockdown defense -- which, let’s face it, had not been evident in every game during the season -- (laughter) -- was the key to Duke’s fifth title run. And Coach K described this year’s championship as “the best moment of his coaching career.” And with five career championships, second to only the legendary John Wooden, that’s saying something.

title: علاقة مستوى الثقافة الرياضية بالصحة النفسية لدى لاعبي كرة السلة على الكراسي المتحركة
text:
Wheelchair basketball is a complex activity with numerous effects on the player's body and involves many relationships, such as those with teammates and coaches. Therefore, it is essential to understand the psychological characteristics and details of each player, as this provides them with many psychological and social benefits (Drinkwater et al., 2008).

Wheelchair basketball is considered one of the most appealing sports, regardless of the cause of the disability. It is linked to cognitive abilities, which are crucial for achieving positive results. It contributes to improving communication skills and interpersonal relationships, as well as enhancing the psychological and social characteristics of these players (Paunic, 2007).

Therefore, engaging in sports activities of all kinds has a positive impact on physical and social well-being, in addition to the psychological and social benefits. It contributes to increasing the ability of these players to cope with various life pressures and reduces levels of depression and anxiety (Miyahara et al., 2008). The results of a study by Martin (2008) indicate that wheelchair basketball players are able to overcome painful thoughts resulting from their disability.

With the multifaceted nature of sports culture, encompassing the cognitive domain (which includes knowledge of rules, regulations, and game plans), the social domain (which aims to nurture and educate individuals in sports and cultivate socially and athletically acceptable behavior), the educational domain (which aims to prepare and guide individuals physically, psychologically, and morally), and finally, the health domain (which aims to develop an individual's ability to care for their body and meet its various needs) (Shehadeh, 2009), we can see that sports culture includes many physical, psychological, ethical, and social aspects. It strives to cultivate the individual physically, psychologically, and behaviorally, and influences the formation of both individual and group character (Aweys & Al-Hilali, 2005).

Furthermore, sports culture includes many elements such as healthy behaviors, sports habits and values, and information and knowledge related to sports activities (Al-Zyod, 2013). Shafei (2001) points out that sports culture contributes to increasing an athlete's sports knowledge base, including rules and regulations, which in turn contributes to a better understanding and appreciation of players. It is part of the general culture and is considered an indicator of a society's progress; therefore, athletes must be sufficiently familiar with sports culture due to its effective role in disseminating and instilling the principles of sportsmanship.

From the foregoing, we find that mental health is linked to sports culture so that athletes can achieve harmony with their environment, face various challenges, and adapt to life's demands. Hassan (2001) indicates that manifestations of mental health include an individual's ability to balance their desires and goals, establish ideal and acceptable relationships, cope with frustration, and experience tranquility. This leads to self-harmony through balancing desires, motives, and goals, as well as social harmony through the ability to establish acceptable social relationships. Studies indicate that these individuals have a lower level of health than normal individuals and suffer from conditions that hinder their participation in sports activities compared to others (Altman & Bernstein, 2008). These studies support the need for these individuals to understand their motivations and interests to help them integrate into society (Deci & Ryan, 2002).

Researchers believe that sports culture influences the formation of an athlete’s personality, helps improve their social interaction, and contributes to increasing their experience and shaping their acceptable social behavior. All of this contributes to improving their mental health by developing their ability to establish acceptable social relationships and improving their ability to deal with various life pressures.

title: مدى مساهمة الصلابة العقلية بالسلوك التنافسي لدى السباحين
text:
Sports training relies on a set of interconnected elements. Understanding and implementing these interconnected elements is fundamental to achieving optimal results. Success in any sport requires a combination of essential elements, including physical and technical skills, tactical strategies, and psychological preparedness. Therefore, comprehensive training necessitates considering all these elements. A successful athlete possesses a well-integrated combination of effective strategies, advanced skills, psychological readiness, and physical capabilities.

Crust and Clough (2005) indicated that sports psychology is a crucial field that has contributed to athletes reaching their full potential. Psychological preparation helps athletes enhance their abilities and overcome challenges encountered during competition.

Christiane and Sophie (2014) argue that psychological skills represent a crucial dimension in athlete preparation, playing a fundamental role in performance development. They are now considered one of the variables that must be addressed alongside physical, technical, and tactical requirements. High-level athletes tend to be remarkably similar in terms of physical, technical, and tactical abilities.

Kishore (2017) emphasizes that maintaining optimal performance under intense competitive pressure requires both skill and mental agility. Inconsistent performance during competitions is primarily attributed to psychological factors, foremost among them being mental toughness.

Shamo'on (2001) argues that mental toughness plays a crucial role in maintaining optimal performance and aims to build mental and emotional strength. Training in mental toughness is both an art and a science, enhancing an athlete's ability to cope with and manage all types of physical, mental, and emotional pressures, leading to greater competitiveness. This, in turn, improves athletic skill development and reduces the risk of injuries and emotional withdrawal.

Adas and Qtame (2000) point out that competition represents the highest stage in the development of athletic activity. It allows everyone to observe the strengths and weaknesses of athletes in terms of physical, technical, and psychological aspects, and it cultivates and refines the athlete's physical attributes.

Omran (2016) argues that competitive behavior is purposeful and achievement-oriented, with motivations differing in type and intensity from those of training. The state of readiness in competition, the presence of the opponent, the judges, the audience, and other variables of the competitive situation stimulate an athlete's motivation to achieve in a way that differs from the motivations induced in training.

Alhmdani (2016) points out that many factors influence swimmers during performance, which can be considered competitive behavior. These factors, therefore, cause individual differences in swimmer behavior in competitive situations. A large number of swimmers can be observed striving to win during races. Cowden (2017) believes that athletic excellence depends on the extent to which athletes utilize their psychological capabilities as much as their physical ones. Psychological capabilities help individuals channel their physical energy to achieve maximum and optimal athletic performance, and these capabilities can be developed through specialized training programs, namely psychological skills training programs.

Jones, Hanton, and Connaughton (2002) argue that mental toughness is the highest psychological level attainable, granting athletes greater endurance compared to their competitors during competitions. This is achieved by developing focus, confidence, and resilience under pressure, which influences athletic behavior. Saleh and Hassan (2012) point out that competitive behavior is an activity in which athletes strive to win. This is based not only on the athlete's intrinsic motivation but also on external influences. Therefore, competitive behavior, especially in individual sports, is distinguished from other human activities by the clear and direct impact of winning and losing, or success and failure, and the behavioral aspects associated with each. Competitive behavior requires athletes to mobilize their maximum physical and mental capabilities to achieve the best possible performance, which contributes to the development and enhancement of psychological traits, particularly moral and volitional traits.

Through his work in the field of teaching and training swimming, and through his monitoring of swimmers' levels, the researcher observed that some swimmers experience a decline in their performance in certain competitions despite their adherence to their training programs. Studies by Omran (2016), Kamal (2015), Alfartosse (2014), and Saleh & Hassan (2012) indicate that competitive behavior plays a role in influencing athletic achievement. Furthermore, the mental toughness possessed by the athlete plays a role in determining psychological aspects and the ability to withstand the pressures that accompany competition, as noted in studies by Cowden (2017), Kishore (2017), Ibrahim (2015), Mehrparvar & Soltani (2013), Hassan (2010), and Crust & Clough. (2005) Does the level of mental toughness possessed by Jordanian swimmers play a role in their competitive behavior during competitions and championships?

title: 2006台北101登高 在世界之最发挥极限
text:
The "2006 Chang Hwa Bank Taipei 101 International Mountain Climbing Race," hosted by Taipei 101 and sponsored by Chang Hwa Bank, officially kicked off at 8:00 AM today. Following the positive reception of last year's event, in addition to the standard elite and self-challenge categories, the organizers have officially included the "Corporate Team Category," which was piloted last year, as a formal competition category to encourage corporate participation and enhance employee cohesion.

As is customary, this year's competition is limited to 101 elite athletes, 1001 individual participants, and 10 corporate teams. However, due to overwhelming participation from corporate teams, additional slots were added, resulting in 11 corporate teams and 26 participating teams. Chang Hwa Bank, the title sponsor, submitted 16 teams to celebrate its 101st anniversary, making them the most favored team in the competition.

Last year's champions, Paul Crake and Andrea Mayr, lived up to expectations, retaining their titles in the men's and women's elite competitions with times of 10:31.57 and 13:28.70 respectively.

Meanwhile, last year's Taiwan champion, Chen Chung-jen, who was also fifth overall in the men's division, had a slightly off year, narrowly missing the podium. He finished eighth with a time of 12:46.76, likely due to his poor performance, and left before the awards ceremony. His teammate, Chen Fu-tsai, improved significantly, finishing sixth in the men's elite competition with a time of 12:24.81, making him the best-performing athlete from Taiwan this year.

The competition in the women's elite competition was even fiercer. This year, Taiwan's home team athletes made significant strides, demonstrating their strength and maintaining their home advantage with excellent performances. Li Xiaoyu finished second overall with a time of 14 minutes and 51.96 seconds, making her the best-performing female runner from Taiwan. Lin Fangzhen, Zhang Meilian, and Yun Chunping finished fifth, sixth, and eighth respectively. Taiwanese female runners comprised half of the top eight, making them the best performing group in the elite competition.

In the self-challenge category, besides Xue Qingguang (who ran backwards), Zhan Junzhi (a Taiwanese Olympic volunteer), Peng Hongnian (the oldest runner), and Zhang Wenyan (a visually impaired runner), the Wrigley's chewing gum group also participated. Former and current Taipei City Deputy Mayors Ye Jinchuan and Jin Pucong also participated in the elite category, serving as a warm-up for the Taipei International Marathon half marathon at the end of the year.

Many elite runners and challenge group participants commented that the ventilation at Taipei 101 still has room for improvement, and the ventilation in the rest and adjustment areas could theoretically be further enhanced. In addition, Extraordinary Television also stated that the Taipei 101 International Climbing Race, which has reached international competitions, should also conduct doping tests on all elite athletes (regardless of whether they have won awards) in order to maintain the principle of fairness.

title: 2007年香港国际赛事落幕 莲华生辉好爸爸大热胜出 迪诺医生夺碗 威满蹄击败爆冷夺杯
text:
The 2007 Cathay Pacific Hong Kong International Races were successfully held at Sha Tin Racecourse. All four Group 1 races saw their winners. In the fourth race, the Hong Kong Sprint, Lotus Blossom easily took the title. In the fifth race, Dr. Dino of the Hong Kong Bottle won with a strong comeback, beating many horses. In the seventh race, the Hong Kong Mile, Hong Kong's representative, Good Dad, narrowly defeated Chisley. In the final race, the Hong Kong Cup, Wynn Wings defeated a surprise to win over HK$10 million in prize money.

At 1 pm, the opening ceremony of the Hong Kong International Races was held. The ceremony began with the "March of the Volunteers," sung by Hacken Lee and accompanied by the Hong Kong Jockey Club Silver Band.

After three local races, the first Group 1 international race was the Hong Kong Sprint. This race was considered a duel between Lotus Blossom, considered the new Hong Kong Sprint King, and the Australian filly, Miss Scent. Lotus Blossom was the favorite, with odds of 1.4, while Miss Scent was the second favorite at 4. After the start, Singapore's Wibby, Hong Kong's Heroine and Ms. On took the lead, while Lotus Shining held a steady position in the middle. On the turn, Ms. On and Wibby overlapped and began to fall behind. In the final 200 meters, Lotus Shining surged forward, overtaking Heroine and winning by more than two lengths, while Qi Cai overtook Heroine to take second place.

title: German Open 2016 im Inline-Alpin fanden in Chammünster statt
text:
Cham (Germany), August 21, 2016 – On Saturday, August 6, and Sunday, August 7, 2016, the FC Chammünster club hosted the German Open Inline Alpine and the Bambini Inline Cup on Pfarrer-Mandl-Straße. The races were held in the following age categories: Children U10, Children U12, Schoolchildren, Youth, Adults, and Seniors. Around 80 athletes from five European nations competed over the two days, including Claudia Wittmann and Katharina Hoffmann from FC Chammünster, who became world champions in the first part of the World Championships in Unterensingen in June of this year.

On Saturday, the first run of the giant slalom started at 1 p.m. with 78 athletes. The second run was scheduled to begin at 3:30 p.m. but was postponed to 4 p.m. Spectators witnessed exciting races in both runs. In the evening, after the awards ceremony, the band Take Off Your Shirts performed on the main stage. After their guitar-fueled roar, they had to end their performance at 10 p.m. out of consideration for the neighbors' peace and quiet. Afterwards, DJs CAT and Ben tried to keep the party going.

On Sunday, the first run started at 10 a.m. with 84 athletes, and the second run began at 1:30 p.m. Under a bright blue sky, spectators watched this slalom race with great excitement in every category. Top favorite Sigi Zistler crashed in the second run and, based on the combined results of both runs, finished fifth in his senior category.

title: Blindenfußball: Deutsche Nationalmannschaft und der SSG Marburg trennen sich 0:0
text:
Marburg (Germany), June 9, 2008 – The match between the German national blind football team and the first German Blind Football Bundesliga champions from Marburg ended 0-0 after a high-class game. SSG Marburg managed to snatch a draw from the overwhelming favorites with a cohesive team performance, proving themselves at least their equals. The spectators in the arena and those listening to the live stream were treated to a high-level match with numerous scoring opportunities for both sides.

At 11:00 a.m., the refereeing duo of Mankel and Lürding kicked off the game between the German national blind football team and the hosts, SSG Marburg. National coach Pfisterer had instructed his team to play offensively from the outset: As a result, the national team frequently came dangerously close to the Marburg goal, guarded by Markus Moj, in the opening minutes. Franzka, Fangmann, and Schwarze applied considerable pressure, initially causing problems for the Marburg defense led by Beck and Warzecha. After about five minutes, Fangmann had a good scoring opportunity for the visitors, but Moj made the save. This seemed to awaken Marburg's attack, and Hoß and especially Pektas began putting pressure on the national team's defense, though without creating any clear-cut chances. With the introduction of Koparan for Marburg, the game became an open, back-and-forth affair with some attractive attacking moves from both sides. However, both defenses remained solid, preventing any further clear scoring opportunities.

In the second half, it was Marburg's new attacking substitute, Felix Johnson, who came into his own. He generated a lot of pressure on his side of the attack, and the national team's defense could hardly contain him. Fueled by this, Marburg's forwards put a lot of pressure on national goalkeeper Müller's goal. A shot from Johnson was only parried by Markus Moj with a lightning-fast reaction. The national team only occasionally threatened the Marburg goal, but the hosts' defense stood firm, preventing any truly dangerous situations for Moj. Marburg's strong attacking play drew several fouls from the national team. Johnson had three opportunities to put his team ahead with a penalty kick, but apart from hitting the post, nothing came of it. The national team was also awarded a penalty kick, but they too failed to convert it.

title: क्रिकेट, बॉल ट्रैकर, और अम्पायर डिसिशन रिव्यू सिस्टम
text:
The 2011 India-Pakistan semi-final match was the most watched match in sports history. We have fought three wars with Pakistan. But the tension in this match was no less than the tension of those three wars.

We won this match by 27 runs. People say that the Pakistani players contributed to this, as they dropped three catches of Sachin. This led to his innings of 85 runs.

In fact, we should first of all be thankful to the new technology of ball tracking, incorporated into the Umpire Decision Review System (UDRS). Sachin was able to score so many runs. Otherwise, he would have been declared out much earlier.

India started batting first. When India had 75 runs and Sachin's individual score was 23, the on-field umpire declared him LBW off Saeed Ajmal.

Sachin spoke to Gautam Gambhir and asked for the decision to be referred to the third umpire. The third umpire, after watching the TV broadcast at the time with Ball Tracker technology, overturned the on-field umpire's decision. According to him, if the ball hadn't hit Sachin's pad, it would have gone past the wicket instead of hitting it.

If the UDRS hadn't been implemented in the World Cup or hadn't incorporated Ball Tracker technology, Sachin would have been out for 23. Instead of making 260, we would have been all out for 198, and Pakistan would have won the match.
