title: Ciclismo: Tom Boonen fa tris, il Giro delle Fiandre è ancora suo
text:
The start is still in Bruges, West Flanders, while the finish is not in Meerbeke, where it was from 1973 to 2011, but in Oudenaarde, East Flanders, after 256.9 kilometers of racing. The final section of the route has been modified: the main change is the absence of the famous—and now traditional, having been climbed continuously since 1969—Grammont Wall.

To make the race more spectacular, the organizers have decided to transform the final 80 kilometers into a sort of circuit, with Oude Kwaremont (2,200 meters at an average gradient of 4.2%) and Paterberg (400 meters at an average gradient of 12.5%) to be tackled three times. There are a total of sixteen walls in this edition of the Ronde van Vlaanderen, 10 cobblestones and six asphalt. The Taaienberg opens the race after 109.3 kilometers (average gradients of 6.6% and maximum gradients of 10%), while the final climb is the third Paterbeg, 13.3 kilometers from the finish. Also tackling the Molenberg (7% average gradient) are the 131.3-kilometer-long (131.3-kilometer-long) and, with 70 kilometers to go, the extremely tough Koppenberg, 600 meters at 11.6% with peaks of 22%. There are eight flat cobblestone sections, all in the central section of the race.

The race, the eighth event on the 2012 UCI World Tour calendar and the second Monument Classic of the season, features 199 professional cyclists representing twenty-five teams. All eighteen UCI World Tour teams are competing, as well as seven UCI Professional Continental teams invited by the organizers via wildcards: Accent.jobs-Willems Veranda's, Argos-Shimano, Farnese Vini-Selle Italia, Landbouwkrediet-Euphony, Team Europcar, Team NetApp, and Topsport Vlaanderen-Mercator.

The 2011 winner, Nick Nuyens, is not competing due to a hip fracture sustained at Paris-Nice; interestingly, the number 1 bib number is worn by Matteo Tosatto. Among the big names present at the start are the Belgians Tom Boonen, Björn Leukemans, Sep Vanmarcke and Philippe Gilbert, the Norwegian Edvald Boasson Hagen, the Swiss Fabian Cancellara, the Italians Alessandro Ballan (winner of the 2007 Tour of Flanders) and Filippo Pozzato, the Slovakian Peter Sagan, the Spaniards Óscar Freire and Juan Antonio Flecha, the Frenchman Sylvain Chavanel and the Dane Matti Breschel.

title: Ciclismo: colpo di Johan Vansummeren, la Parigi-Roubaix 2011 è sua
text:
The first two hours of the race were very fast, averaging 45 km/h; some initial breakaway attempts were unsuccessful. There were several crashes, one of which forced Russian Vladimir Gusev (Katusha) to retire. Just before the first cobbled sector, between Troisvilles and Inchy at kilometer 98, eight riders finally managed to break away: Frenchmen David Boucher (Omega Pharma-Lotto), Jimmy Engoulvent (Saur-Sojasun), and David Veilleux (Team Europcar), Swiss national champion Martin Elmiger (AG2R), Dutchman Maarten Tjallingii (Rabobank), Australian Mitchell Docker (Skil-Shimano), Portuguese Nelson Oliveira (Team Radioshack), and German Timon Seubert (Team Netapp), all second-place riders.

The escapees built up a maximum lead of 1:25, then, around the 140th kilometer of the race, they were caught by three other cyclists: German André Greipel (Omega Pharma-Lotto), Dutchman Koen de Kort (Skil-Shimano), and Slovenian Gorazd Štangelj (Astana). Meanwhile, Oliveira broke away: ten riders remained in front – reaching a lead of 2:40 – while another small group of four riders chased behind (they were absorbed by the peloton during the passage through the Arenberg Forest). As they approached the famous cobbled section, the group's speed increased, causing several crashes, involving Roger Hammond and Heinrich Haussler (Garmin-Cervélo).

The first dramatic turns of events came right at the 2,400-meter mark of the Trouée d'Arenberg (86 meters to go): Britain's Geraint Thomas (Sky) punctured, then one of the top favorites, Belgian Tom Boonen (Quickstep), winner of the 2005, 2008, and 2009 editions, suffered mechanical problems and was forced to wait for the team car; he lost more than a minute, as well as a good part of his hopes of matching Roger De Vlaeminck's record with a fourth Roubaix victory. Outside Arenberg, seven more riders set out in pursuit of the ten escapees: Dutchman Lars Boom (Rabobank), Belgians Johan Vansummeren (Garmin-Cervélo) and Jürgen Roelandts (Omega Pharma-Lotto), Australians Baden Cooke (Saxo Bank-Sungard) and Mathew Hayman (Sky), Danish rider Lars Bak (HTC-Highroad), Italian Manuel Quinziato (BMC), and Frenchman Fréderic Guesdon (FDJ). Meanwhile, some potential frontrunners remain behind, including Belgian Björn Leukemans (Vacansoleil-DCM), who crashed, and Frenchman Sylvain Chavanel (Quickstep), second in this year's Tour of Flanders, who suffered a puncture.

More bad luck for Quickstep: Boonen, who was riding a minute behind the peloton, crashed in the Sars-et-Rosières sector, 72 minutes to go. Then Chavanel, who had managed to rejoin the peloton, crashed and was dropped. It should be noted that in the following minutes, Peter Sagan, Filippo Pozzato, and Leukemans again also suffered crashes. With 60 minutes to go, 21 riders are in the lead: Germans John Degenkolb (HTC-Highroad) and Gabriel Rasch (Garmin-Cervélo), Swiss Grégory Rast (Radioshack), and Dutchman Tom Leezer (Rabobank) also managed to rejoin. Behind them, the top riders, including Fabian Cancellara (Leopard-Trek), Thor Hushovd (Garmin-Cervélo), Juan Antonio Flecha (Sky), and Alessandro Ballan (BMC), are trailing at 1:10.

title: 特集1　スポーツ立国の実現：文部科学省
text:
Comprehensive community sports clubs are community-based sports centers operated independently and proactively by local residents, conducting daily activities at nearby schools and public facilities. They contribute to the realization of a lifelong sports society and are expected to have various benefits, including providing sports opportunities for local children, fostering family interaction, promoting healthy youth development through intergenerational exchange, and maintaining and improving the health of local residents. The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology has supported the establishment of comprehensive community sports clubs through on-site guidance by club development advisors and the provision of information on successful establishment cases, promoting their nationwide expansion. As a result of these efforts, the number of comprehensive community sports clubs increased 5.8 times over the eight years from FY2002 to FY2010, and the number of municipalities with comprehensive community sports clubs increased 2.9 times. Furthermore, the club establishment rate (the ratio of municipalities with comprehensive community sports clubs to the total number of municipalities) reached 71.4 percent in FY2010 (Figure 1-1-20).

On the other hand, according to the "FY2010 Survey Results on the Actual Situation of Comprehensive Community Sports Clubs," the primary challenge for comprehensive community sports clubs is "securing members" (Figure 1-1-21). To secure and retain members, it is considered key for comprehensive community sports clubs to provide attractive programs that reflect the needs of local residents. Therefore, the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology plans to establish a system for providing attractive sports services at comprehensive community sports clubs, starting in FY2011. This includes assigning excellent instructors, such as retired top athletes, to core clubs and conducting itinerant instruction for multiple surrounding comprehensive community sports clubs (see Section 3(1)1.(a)).

Furthermore, looking at the self-financing rates of comprehensive community sports clubs, approximately half of the clubs have a self-financing rate of 50 percent or less (Figure 1-1-22). As the "FY2010 Survey Results on the Actual Situation of Comprehensive Community Sports Clubs" also lists "securing funding" as a major challenge, securing funding commensurate with activities is necessary for comprehensive community sports clubs to operate sustainably. To achieve this, it is crucial not only to expand membership fee revenue through securing members, but also to accept donations from local businesses and shops. Therefore, the Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) will promote initiatives to enable many comprehensive community sports clubs to effectively utilize the donation tax system (certified non-profit organization system) and accept a wide range of donations.

Through these initiatives, MEXT aims to support the independence of comprehensive community sports clubs facing challenges such as securing members, instructors, and financial resources. As stated in the "New Public" Declaration (June 4, 2010, "New Public" Roundtable Conference), MEXT supports these clubs in proactively shaping the local sports environment as "NPO-type community sports clubs independently operated through membership fees and donations contributed by local residents," while also considering the resolution of local issues (such as school-community cooperation and childcare support).

title: スポーツ基本計画：学校体育の現状と課題
text: Physical education activities in schools form the foundation for a fulfilling lifelong sports life. The revised curriculum guidelines of 2008 and 2009 aimed to systematize and clarify instructional content, taking into account developmental stages from elementary to high school. However, in elementary schools, with the aging of teachers, most teachers teach all subjects, leading to concerns among teachers about physical education classes and insufficient implementation of specialized instruction. In junior high schools, with the mandatory inclusion of martial arts, efforts are needed to enhance safe and smooth instruction. In high schools, there is a need to improve instruction that enables students to engage in a continuous sports life throughout their lives. Furthermore, junior and senior high schools are required to help students understand the significance of sports, such as the important role of international sports competitions like the Olympics in international goodwill and world peace. While promoting the placement of specialist teachers and local sports instructors with expertise is effective in improving the instructional system, overall, their utilization is not sufficient. Regarding school sports clubs, for example, the participation rate in junior high schools has remained relatively stable. However, the declining birthrate has led to a decrease in the number of students participating in sports clubs, particularly in team sports, which is causing difficulties in these activities. There are also challenges in securing sports instructors to reduce the burden on supervising teachers, and further ingenuity is needed in their format and operation. Furthermore, some sports are difficult for girls to participate in, and there is a need to improve opportunities for participation. In addition, serious accidents are reported every year in school physical education activities, such as physical education classes and sports club activities, and further consideration and ingenuity in safety are needed. Regarding physical education activities for children and students with disabilities, while measures have been taken to meet the educational needs of the children and students, the Basic Sports Act also requires consideration according to the type and degree of disability. Regarding school physical education facilities (*1), the seismic resistance rate has not yet reached 100%, and although the rate of grassing of grounds is increasing, it remains at a low level, and improving these facilities is a challenge. Furthermore, with the mandatory inclusion of martial arts in the curriculum following the revision of the national curriculum guidelines, promoting the development of martial arts training facilities has become a challenge.

title: Массовый спорт и его роль в социализации молодежи в современной России
text: The experience of developed capitalist countries around the world demonstrates the importance of mass sports or sports for all (the terms "mass sports" and "sport for all" are currently used synonymously in many countries). However, the organization, management, and financing of mass sports vary widely in these countries. While the United States, for example, is characterized by a lack of direct support for sports from the state budget, and the physical education and sports movement there is largely financed by the private sector, stimulated by a large number of tax breaks and incentives, Western European countries, by contrast, have a mixed funding system for mass sports, with the state budget predominating. In developed capitalist countries, the involvement of citizens of various age groups, including young people, is achieved primarily through a system of sports clubs, operating both independently and within physical education and sports organizations, which presupposes the development of a commercial sector in physical education and mass sports. It should be noted that the European system of organizing mass sports, despite all its undeniable advantages, also has certain shortcomings. Thus, modern Western researchers B. Vanroysel and M. Tax, having analyzed the results of the development of "sport for all" in the countries of the European Union over the past several decades, came to the following conclusions: on the one hand, according to the data of these researchers, thanks to sport for all, the number of people involved in sports has increased, however, on the other hand, the proportion of young people and the elderly among those involved is relatively small. Despite the support of mass sports from sports organizations, including clubs and federations, in the opinion of B. Vanroysel and M. Tax, this support is generally quite weak. Along with the aforementioned shortcomings, the system of organizing mass sports in European countries is characterized by other negative features: despite the democratization of sport, opportunities for participation in the sports movement for representatives of various socio-demographic groups, ethnic and other minorities remain uneven, local traditional sports and folk games feel quite disadvantaged. In addition, mass sports and its legislative base are becoming increasingly dependent on the economy of the countries in question [3, p. 283]. Clearly, these specific features must be taken into account when organizing a mass sports system in modern Russia. Currently, as shown by the results of specialized studies, the number of citizens in the Russian Federation who regularly engage in physical education and sports constitutes 22.5% of the country's total population (it should be noted that over the past few years, the number of people involved in mass sports has been growing: from 2008 to 2012, for example, it increased by 9.7 million people and currently stands at 32.2 million). Statistics also indicate that the most physically active groups of the Russian population are children and young people under 30: in the group of people aged 15 to 29, in particular, the share of young people involved in physical education and sports is 13.3 million people, or 43.4% of the total population in this age group. At the same time, it's important to consider that the youth's activity in question is largely due to the fact that a significant portion of them are students at educational institutions where physical education is a mandatory subject within existing curricula. The number of individuals systematically engaged in physical education and sports declines sharply as they age: after completing school and university, motivation to engage in physical education and sports declines (among employed individuals, the overwhelming majority, up to 90%, no longer participate systematically in physical education and sports) [4].

title: Состояние массового спорта в регионах ЦФО
text: In the context of socio-economic transformations in Russia, issues of strengthening the physical and spiritual health of people, the formation of a healthy lifestyle are of particular importance, therefore the development of physical culture and sports is a relevant area of social policy of the state. Despite this, in the regions of the Central Federal District, there is an uneven trend in attracting the population to sports and physical education. The development of this industry in the Kursk region is due to the promotion of a healthy lifestyle and the improvement of sports infrastructure. At the same time, the main problem in attracting young people to physical education and health activities is the lack of material and information resources, the deficit of which arises from insufficient financial support from the regional budget. According to A.A. Sakharova [1], physical culture and sports are an indicator that ensures the physical and moral health of the population, supporting the ability to work and competitiveness of an individual in the labor market. P.V. Vavilov [2] agrees with this position, arguing that the physical and social well-being of the population as a whole depends on an understanding of the importance of a healthy lifestyle, as well as on the development of mass sports in the regions. Therefore, the importance of promoting a healthy lifestyle is growing, which, according to O.P. Golovchenko [3], is a catalyst for increasing the number of people involved in physical education and sports. The problem of popularization, according to E.V. Kuznetsova [4], is associated with the lack of social advertising aimed at involving young people in physical education and sports, as well as with insignificant attention in the regions to the development of mass and street sports, and a minimal number of city holidays attracting a large number of young people. At the same time, P.A. Ganin [5] mentions that many sports stars take part in various advertising campaigns that are a negative example of healthy eating and a healthy lifestyle ("Lay's", "Pepsi"), which has a detrimental effect on the perception of young people about sports culture. Therefore, there is a need to raise the prestige of sports, since thanks to it, as V.V. notes, Popova [6], many socially significant problems are being solved: reproduction of the labor force, deepening intra-group and inter-group integration, socialization, as well as raising a healthy and physically strong generation.

title: Italia se proclama campeona de Europa de hockey sobre patines en Alcobendas
text:
Italy has been crowned European Roller Hockey Champion for the third time in its history after defeating France on the final day of the tournament held in Alcobendas, following Spain's draw against Portugal.

The Italians were the first to take to the rink at the Amaya Valdemoro Pavilion in Alcobendas to defend their hopes of victory against France. The first half was end-to-end, with constant scoring opportunities for both teams, which was reflected in the score: 3-2 in favor of France at halftime. Goals from Florent David and Davide Motaran were particularly noteworthy. After the break, France scored immediately, but Italy came out with renewed energy and quickly turned the score around. However, France put Italy under serious pressure in the final ten minutes, but Italy ultimately celebrated their hard-fought victory in style.

In the least important match of the final day, Germany easily defeated Switzerland, who finished the tournament as the only team without a single point. Although the Swiss started well, they allowed Germany to pull away, and their 2-4 lead proved meaningless, as the Germans extended their advantage to 2-6, snatching fourth place from France.

For the final and decisive match of the 51st European Championship, the Amaya Valdemoro Pavilion was finally packed with around 2,000 spectators. It was a beautiful and intense match in which Spain trailed throughout. Portugal took a two-goal lead three times, and Spain equalized three times, ultimately ending in a 6-6 draw that satisfied neither side.

title: El Deportivo Cali celebra sus primeros cien años de vida
text:
November 23, 2012, Santiago de Cali, Colombia — Deportivo Cali, founded on November 23, 1912, celebrated its centennial, becoming the first team in Colombia to reach this milestone. Various activities were held in the capital of Valle del Cauca to commemorate the occasion.

A commemorative caravan had been announced several days prior, scheduled to depart from the Plazoleta de San Francisco, where a religious ceremony would take place before proceeding to the team's administrative headquarters, Alex Gorayeb, on Avenida Vásquez Cobo, where the remaining activities would be held.

However, due to the announcement of Vice President Angelino Garzón's arrival in the city, the centennial celebrations had to be rescheduled. On the 23rd, news arrived that DAGMA (the Administrative Department of Environmental Management) had denied permission to use the park, seemingly canceling the entire nighttime itinerary. However, at the last minute, the event was reorganized to take place at the Orquideorama.

Starting at 4:00 pm, fans gathered at the Monument to Solidarity, from where they marched towards the team's headquarters. At 6:00 pm, the scheduled march began, ultimately heading to the Orquideorama, where various musical and culinary activities took place. During the gathering and march, fireworks were set off, supporters chanted, and banners alluding to the celebration were displayed. Attendance at the Orquideorama is estimated at 11,000 people, while the march attendance is estimated to be higher due to the fact that many Verdiblanco fans were unable to enter the venue because of space limitations.

At the team's headquarters, a commemorative prayer was held, attended by directors, players, former stars, members, and fans. Following the prayer, a toast was offered, and a slideshow highlighting the team's key achievements over the past one hundred years was shown. Afterward, the sky lit up with fireworks launched from San Antonio and Santa Mónica Hill. Following the formalities, the commemorative birthday cake was cut, and musical performances were given by the salsa group Azul Profundo and Julio Martínez, singer of the official centennial song, a version of the traditional "Pachito E'che." The evening then proceeded as usual.

title: Mwanza, Songwe Kucheza Nusu Fainali Leo UMISSETA Soka Wavulana
text:
The ongoing UMISSETA championship in Mtwara has reached the semi-finals for the boys' soccer category, where in the games that ended this evening, boys' soccer teams from Lindi, Ruvuma, Mwanza and Songwe regions have successfully entered the semi-finals after defeating their opponents including defending champion Tanga, which was played by Lindi.

With these results, the boys' soccer team from Lindi region will meet Ruvuma in the first semi-final, which is expected to be played tomorrow at 8 pm, followed by the second semi-final that will bring together the Mwanza giants who will compete with the tough Songwe team.

The first team to enter the semi-finals was the team from Lindi region, which eliminated the Tanga region team on penalties 3 to 1 after a scoreless draw after ninety minutes of play.

Another quarter-final clash involved teams from Ruvuma and Kilimanjaro regions where the Ruvuma regional football team, which is made up of 8 players from the Ruhuwiko secondary school sports center located on the outskirts of Songea Municipality, defeated the Kilimanjaro team by two goals to zero.

In the matches that ended this evening, the Songwe and Manyara teams and the Mbeya and Mwanza teams fought hard in other quarter-final matches where Songwe defeated Manyara by one goal to zero and Mwanza defeated Mbeya by 5 goals to 3 on penalties after the teams ended in a goalless draw within 90 minutes of the game.

However, Mwanza had every reason to win the game as in the 72nd minute they missed an open goal after their penalty was saved by Mbeya goalkeeper Gerald Hatson and saved by the team's defenders.

Immediately after the game, Mwanza Coach Mwalimu Tito Mkami said that his boys fought hard but praised the Mbeya team for the way it bothered them and admitted that the team was tough because it gave his players a hard time throughout the game.

In addition, Mwalimu Mkami called on the Football Association in Tanzania (TFF) not to include other competitions when the championship organized by the UMISSETA and UMITASHUMTA governments is held so as not to cause this championship to lack important players for their teams.

And the captain of the Mwanza football team Kimwaga Kalunga who is the only student playing for the team from the Alliance special football school who said that they are not afraid of the Songwe team but respect it because all the teams that entered that stage are tough.

Early tomorrow morning the semi-final games for the girls' football will be played at the Mtwara Teachers' College grounds where the first game will bring together the Dar es Salaam giants who will sweat and the team from Iringa region, and the other game will bring together the Mwanza giants who will compete with Ruvuma.

In the handball quarter-final results of the game played this evening show that the Geita and Unguja boys teams have successfully qualified for the semi-finals and are scheduled to play tomorrow, while the other semi-final will bring together Tanga and Morogoro.

In the girls' handball, the qualified teams are Unguja who will play tomorrow with Morogoro and Songwe who will play with Mbeya.

Another game in which the qualified teams have been announced is netball where the teams of Morogoro, Tanga, Dar es Salaam and Mwanza have qualified for the stage where the games will be played tomorrow with Tanga meeting with Mwanza and Morogoro playing with Dar es Salaam.

In the boys' basketball game, the teams that qualified for the semi-finals are Pwani, Unguja, Tanga and Shinyanga where according to the schedule released Pwani will play with Unguja and Tanga will compete with Shinyanga.

In the girls' basketball, Kilimanjaro will face Mwanza and Morogoro will play with their neighbors Dar es Salaam.

title: Ah! Mpira!
text:
I like to play with my friend Chuma.

Chuma and I love each other very much. When we are sent, we go together.

One day, my grandmother sent me to the store to buy salt and oil. I went with Chuma.

On the way, we saw our friends playing soccer.

I really wanted to play soccer. I said, “Oh! Soccer!”

I told Chuma, “Let’s go and ask them to play soccer with me. I love soccer.”

Chuma replied, “Let’s go to the store first, then we’ll come back and play.”

But I told Chuma, “Let’s play first! If we go home, grandma won’t let us.”

We were accepted by our friends and we played soccer. I was the goalkeeper.

I tried my best to catch the ball. My friends couldn’t score a single goal.

title: Weekly Address: This Labor Day, Lets Talk About the Budget
text: On Friday, we found out that the economy created another 173,000 jobs in August. Over the past five and a half years, our businesses have created 13.1 million new jobs in total – the longest streak of job creation on record. The unemployment rate dropped to 5.1%, the lowest it’s been in seven years. The American auto industry is on track to sell more cars and trucks this year than it has in more than a decade. Sixteen million Americans have gained the security of health insurance. Seventeen states and about 30 cities and counties have raised the minimum wage. And we’ve proposed extending overtime protections to as many as five million Americans. All of that is progress. This month, Congress has an opportunity to continue that progress. As always, the deadline for Congress to pass a budget is the end of September.

title: Remarks by the President on Raising the Minimum Wage
text:
We know these Americans. We depend on them. The workers who’d benefit from a minimum wage increase often work full-time, often in physically demanding jobs. They average 35 years of age. Most low-paying jobs are held by women. But because Republicans in Congress said “no” to even allowing a vote on the floor of the Senate, these folks are going to have to wait for the raise they deserve.

Now the good news is outside of Washington folks aren’t waiting. While Republicans have been deciding whether to even allow a minimum wage bill to even come up for a vote, you’ve seen 10 states and the District of Columbia go ahead and raise theirs. (Applause.) Yesterday, the Hawaii legislature voted to raise their minimum wage to $10.10 an hour. Maryland did the same thing earlier this month -– and I know we’ve got some Maryland state legislators here today. Thanks for the good work. (Applause.)

So the actions that have been taken in just four states -- Maryland, Connecticut, Minnesota, and Hawaii -– means that over a million workers will see a raise. What’s more, we’ve seen big companies like The Gap, and small businesses -- from a pizza joint in St. Louis to an ice cream parlor in Florida -- increasingly choosing to raise wages for their employees because they know it’s good business. They know that it means employees are more likely to stay on the job, less turnover. It means that they’re going to be more productive, and customers see the difference. That’s one of the reasons I issued an executive order requiring employees on new federal contracts to be paid a fair wage of at least $10.10 an hour. (Applause.)

title: ثلاثة أسباب للاحتفاء بالحد الأدنى للأجر.. مع ضرورة مد مظلته إلى العاملين في القطاع الخاص
text:
A minimum wage is the most suitable tool in Egypt for eradicating poverty, and it also helps to improve the significant income inequality among Egyptians. The share of wages in national income has declined over the past quarter-century. Conversely, the share of profits (the income of business owners and companies) has increased, as has the share of rent-seekers (landowners, property owners, and holders of government debt). These distortions in the distribution of the benefits of growth create a constraint on opportunities to raise growth rates. The inability of large segments of the poor to access quality education, adequate food, and healthcare means a lack of social mobility and a shortage of a skilled and healthy workforce capable of developing the economy.

What are the risks of this measure and other social measures on the budget deficit?

There is no negative impact on the budget deficit. Egypt intends to reduce the budget deficit to less than 8% during the coming year, in which this package is implemented—a level that can be described as a benign deficit. The planned package is designed to compensate for the damage and address income inequality between different segments of society. In return, the government is expected to increase its revenue from the wealthier and more consuming income brackets through taxation. In public finance theory, this is called the distributive role of the budget. This is instead of increasing the budget deficit to support the wealthy, which is the malignant deficit that Egypt has suffered from for many years, through unfair regressive taxes and generous subsidies that go to inefficient government institutions as well as private companies, and without merit.

title: ادفع بالتى هى أحسن: الحد الأدنى للأجر يعود
text:
The share of wage earners has been steadily declining globally in recent decades, while the share of profit reapers has increased. In Egypt, the absence of collective bargaining, trade union freedom, and necessary studies, coupled with the lack of a national minimum wage, has become a source of concern for international financial institutions that lend to us, such as the World Bank. The Bank notes that for every ten Egyptian pounds generated by the Egyptian economy, 7.5% goes to a small minority of wealthy individuals and capital owners, while only 2.5% goes to the majority of wage earners. Furthermore, senior public and private sector employees receive the lion's share of that meager portion.

In Egypt, the wealthiest 1% are estimated to hold 18% of total income. This means that 900,000 individuals alone possess a share of the national income equivalent to the combined income of 45 million citizens, according to a study conducted by Thomas Piketty and his research team on Egypt and several other Middle Eastern countries.

As in South Africa, the phenomenon of the working poor is widespread in Egypt—those who toil and work, but whose wages do not allow them to escape the poverty line. The World Bank estimated in 2009 that the working poor comprised half of Egypt's workforce. This percentage appears to have increased after the January Revolution, according to data published on the website of the Central Agency for Public Mobilization and Statistics. This situation can be explained by the absence of a national minimum wage. In 2011, a minimum wage was established, but it benefited only a small minority of government employees (only 200,000 government employees benefited from the minimum wage introduced as a result of the January Revolution).

Egypt is one of the few countries in the world that does not have a national minimum wage. Most of the working poor are concentrated in the informal sector, followed by the private sector (together, they constitute more than 85% of the working poor), according to official data from 2012–2013. The public sector is not immune to poverty; those who did not qualify for the minimum wage established by President Adly Mansour in 2013 remain below the poverty line.

Therefore, given the prevalence of this phenomenon, perhaps the most effective approach to eradicating poverty in Egypt, as in South Africa, is to establish a unified minimum wage across all sectors, enforced by national law and periodically adjusted according to a socially acceptable mechanism.

title: 2007台湾品牌趋势论坛 品牌专家建议政商界重视“微笑曲线”理论
text:
Concurrently with the formal merger of the Republic of China Self-Created Brands Association and the Taiwan Excellence Manufacturers Association into the "Taiwan Excellence Brands Association," the "Taiwan Brand Trends Forum" held today (20th) at the Leofoo Palace in Taipei invited brand experts from the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the business community to share Taiwan's brand marketing experience under the theme of "Winning the Global Economy with Taiwanese Brands," encouraging Taiwanese brands to market internationally through innovation.

At the opening ceremony, Hsieh Tzu-jen, the newly appointed chairman of the Taiwan Excellence Brands Association, stated clearly: "Made in Taiwan does not represent 'cheap,' but rather symbolizes the 'value' of excellent quality." Minister of Economic Affairs Chen Jui-lung echoed Chairman Hsieh's remarks, stating: "With the innovation, research, and development of brands, many self-created brands have embarked on a path of refinement, and excellent brands have even become world-renowned. However, brand management is not guaranteed to be successful, because with the continuous emergence of small and medium-sized enterprises, cultivating a good brand image requires long-term management."

The forum's focus... The highlight was the opening speech by Stan Shih, founder of Acer Group. Besides explaining global and Taiwanese brand development trends using the "flat world" theory, he further utilized his most acclaimed "smile curve" theory to demonstrate the trend of global corporate integration. He stated, "The quality of a brand is not determined by its size, but by its essence and brand awareness." He even emphasized, "Taiwanese manufacturers cannot forever remain OEMs! Because some people confuse the concepts of 'brand Taiwan' with 'Taiwanese brands.' A good brand requires not only good creativity but also effective management." "Strategy is key to marketing Taiwanese brands internationally."

In her subsequent keynote speech, Deputy Director-General Hsu Chun-fang of the Bureau of Foreign Trade, Ministry of Economic Affairs, stated: "Taiwanese brands have evolved from ODM to the more common OEM, and even, with the emergence of products manufactured under Taiwanese brands, have officially entered the important OBM era. This has enabled many brands to gain international recognition, with BenQ, Giant, Maxxis, and Acer serving as prime examples. If Taiwan can maintain its OBM strategy, it can significantly enhance a brand's competitiveness in the market." Increased influence and exposure can further promote the industry's commitment to remaining rooted in Taiwan.

BenQ Vice Chairman Wang Wen-tsan, in his speech, used the definition from Wikipedia to clarify the difference between "value" and "value system." He stated, "Value includes both value system and customer value. A consumer's motivation for purchasing a product can vary due to emotional factors or personal needs. Furthermore, the attributes of a product or brand can be understood through differences in consumer groups. Of course, this applies not only to Taiwan, but also to products and private label brands in different countries, each with its own characteristics and style."

title: 2008年环台赛 将与自行车展、体育用品展、世贸南港馆 产生四合一效益
text:
The 2008 Tour of Taiwan International Cycling Race is about to begin on March 9th. The Taipei International Cycling Show and the Taipei International Sporting Goods Show will be held simultaneously at the Taipei World Trade Center and its Nangang Exhibition Hall for four days starting on the 13th. Furthermore, the opening of the Nangang Exhibition Hall on the opening day, along with the addition of a "Nangang Exhibition Hall stage" to the Tour of Taiwan, will bring multiple benefits to the sporting goods, cycling, competitive sports, and exhibition industries.

This year's Tour of Taiwan will not only eliminate cross-county/city competition, but with the Nangang Exhibition Hall opening simultaneously with the Taipei International Cycling Show, Taipei City will see its first-ever dual-stage event for a single county/city. Moreover, the "Citizen Elite Circuit Race," promoting local cycling, will be significantly expanded in scale. Even disregarding international competition, this circuit race alone is a powerful tool for promoting grassroots cycling.

Beyond grassroots promotion, this year's Tour of Taiwan will be even more significant, as this international race, designated a 2.2 level by the International Cycling Federation (UCI), will determine riders' qualifications for the 2008 Beijing Olympics this summer. The long-distance road race, which tests riders' stamina and endurance, is particularly crucial, especially the two-day road race between Hsinchu City and Taipei County.

Since the separation of bicycle exhibitions and sporting goods exhibitions in 1988, both industry exhibitions have developed their own unique characteristics.

Taiwan has long been known as the "Kingdom of Bicycle Exports," a reputation stemming from the decline of the American bicycle industry. The rise of brands like Merida and Giant, increased productivity in Asian countries, the fact that the vast majority of bicycles in the US are imported from Taiwan, and Taiwan's industrial development—from OEM manufacturing to the "Three New Movements" promoting high added value and new materials, functions, and uses in cycling—have led to the rise of local brands and Taiwan's place in the global bicycle industry. Currently, Giant and Merida are the 7th and 19th largest bicycle brands globally, respectively. In contrast, the sporting goods exhibition, after undergoing relocation, disputes over management rights among trade associations, and the completion of the Taipei World Trade Center, has not only witnessed part of the export history of the Taiwan External Trade Development Council (TAITRA), but also, due to technological advancements, innovative concepts, and market changes, has become not only a long-standing exhibition but also a benchmark for business opportunities in Asia.

Although the development of the sporting goods industry has also been driven by changes in modern lifestyles, leading to the rise of the fitness and leisure industries, this year's simultaneous exhibition with the bicycle show will undoubtedly bring shared benefits to the bicycle, sporting goods, and leisure sports industries.

Since the Nangang Pavilion was completed in late December last year, many year-end parties have held preliminary events before its official opening, garnering praise from numerous large enterprises. In fact, the Nangang Pavilion's popularity stems not only from its size being twice that of the existing Taipei World Trade Center but also from its unique double-story exhibition hall, with the upper hall featuring a column-free design, further attracting the attention of the exhibition industry.

title: Ehemalige Conradty-Mitarbeiter feiern Übernahme
text:
Nuremberg (Germany), February 27, 2005 – A rather inglorious chapter of history recently reached a somewhat positive conclusion. 240 employees of the former companies Conradty Carbon and Conradty COVA, based in Röthenbach an der Pegnitz, celebrated the takeover by an Indian investor, which had been agreed upon in December 2004. Prominent figures and politicians from the region and Munich attended the celebration. Fortunately, 240 jobs were saved instead of the expected 200.

The company is now called "Graphite Cova GmbH," and Adrian Bojilov is the new managing director. The investor, "Graphite India," is headquartered in Kolkata. With this acquisition, the company is attempting to gain a foothold in the European Union.

Not only the employees and banks contributed to the smooth handling of the takeover; the local municipality, the district, the Franconian regional government, as well as members of parliament and three ministries in Munich, all worked diligently to preserve the jobs. The insolvency administrator found an investor in India who was willing to keep the company in Germany. Relocating the production facilities to Asia was never mentioned during the entire negotiations.

title: Friedensnobelpreisträger Muhammad Yunus an der Universität Karlsruhe
text:
Karlsruhe (Germany), June 6, 2007 – As part of a special event in the lecture series "Shaping Globalization," organized by AIESEC, the Global Marshall Plan University Group Karlsruhe, and the Interfaculty Institute for Entrepreneurship, Muhammad Yunus and Eduardo Suplicy gave presentations today in the auditorium of the University of Karlsruhe. Heidemarie Wieczorek-Zeul, Federal Minister for Economic Cooperation and Development, is the patron of the lecture series.

Muhammad Yunus was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006. Eduardo Suplicy (Workers' Party) represents the state of São Paulo in the Brazilian Senate and, as an advocate of the idea of a universal basic income, has succeeded in enshrining elements of this idea in the Brazilian Constitution. Götz Werner, founder of the drugstore chain dm, moderated the event. All three speakers are professors of economics. In his opening statement, Götz Werner said that Muhammad Yunus also deserved the Nobel Prize in Economics.

Muhammad Yunus delivered a freely spoken address in English to the packed auditorium, peppered with many amusing anecdotes that illustrated the history of the Grameen Bank. His approximately one-hour lecture was frequently interrupted by laughter and applause. The Nobel Peace Prize laureate began his speech by saying that he always enjoyed speaking to students, as the idea for the microcredit institution had originated on the campus of a university in Bangladesh. Yunus admitted to feeling guilty about teaching economics at a time when his homeland was experiencing a severe famine, especially since the textbooks offered no solution to the crisis and seemed "pointless" to him.

title: मुफ्त बांटे – पैसा कमायें
text:
I heard something similar in Kerala. Fishermen there, upon catching fish, check the price on their mobile phones and take their boats to the place where they get the best price.

The story is similar with open source. People often think that it's impossible to have ownership of open source; that it can't be paid for – and therefore, it can't be monetized. This thinking is wrong. Distributing open source software for free doesn't mean it can't be monetized. This is a similar tactic to that used by financial institutions in Africa.

The method of earning money in open source is different from proprietary software. Perhaps, this is a better approach. That's why open source is being promoted in Extremadura.

title: मछली पालन कर सुनील कमा रहे लाखों रुपए
text:
After completing his studies, when he could not find employment anywhere, he started fish farming. Initially, he faced a lot of difficulties. Now, he has built a hatchery on about 9 acres. title: Francesco Cirillo: i programmatori agili, una nuova filosofia dello sviluppo software
text:
FC: Agile methods seek a winning solution where developers have better working conditions and content, and companies can make more money. How? In an agile team, every member has the opportunity to contribute to improving the process. Each team member takes responsibility for developing entire features (and doesn't have them assigned to them by someone else). They know they can propose new, even highly creative, ideas. Their ideas will be harshly criticized but objectively and always with respect. They develop production software in collaboration with another developer to improve the quality of their work, learn from those who know more than them, or discover new things through discussion. They can communicate their development problems without fear, knowing the team will help them. They are committed to writing high-quality software that everyone can understand. And above all, they build software that grows evolutionarily, driven by testing.

All this leads to fewer defects, greater overall flexibility, and a resulting lower cost of change. Managers reduce monitoring activities—the team is interested in its own improvement—and, above all, they stop motivating people. The team is motivated by the content of the work and the process they've chosen to follow. They experience greater satisfaction at work, increasing the company's productivity and profits.

title: La Luna e i Robot
text:
The century we have begun represents a true crossroads in human history. Not only is the need for raw materials, energy, and water severely testing the planet's stability, its environmental cycles, and the balance between living species, but the forms of commodity production, the distribution of resources, and the progressive concentration of power in a few hands are severely testing contemporary societies.

These processes are the result of the major transformations that technologies are injecting into the heart of our societies. The strategic innovation of recent years has been the introduction of digital technologies. Their ubiquity, flexibility, and pervasiveness have transformed the entire human environment. But these transformations are only in the first phase of their development. Indeed, the acceleration we are destined for predicts an exponential increase in changes in all areas of daily life, starting with working conditions.

Given the exponential increase in the potential for automation of production processes, what kind of work will still exist in 50 years? Will work still be the means of distributing the income necessary for people's livelihoods? What will tomorrow's work look like? Can new modes of production, increasingly interconnected and intertwined with personal relationships, coexist with a nineteenth-century work-life model that divided the day into 8 hours of work, 8 hours of life, and 8 hours of sleep? Could the decline in equipment prices, their miniaturization, the development of 3D printers, and the prevalence of immaterial goods herald a reduction in the scale of global production and counterbalance the push toward gigantism by large corporations?

The potential of digital technology is now being harnessed by old forms of ownership, control, and commodification, and bent to the needs of old forms of capitalist production. What can we do to strengthen the logics that counter this trend and are already building other forms of production, work, and sociality?

title: 特集2　教育と職業：文部科学省
text:
A major characteristic of employment practices in Japan is the in-house education and training based on the premise of long-term employment. Until now, it was common practice to acquire basic knowledge at school, and then develop the specialized knowledge and skills necessary for a job mainly through in-house education and training while working. However, as shown in Figure 1-2-9, approximately 70% of companies report having challenges in human resource development. The reasons cited include a shortage of personnel to provide instruction (approximately 50 percent) and a shortage of time (approximately 47 percent), indicating that companies are losing the capacity to provide human resource development (*4). In addition, the increase in non-regular employees, as seen in section 1, is also creating problems in the development of professional skills. Non-regular employees have fewer opportunities to receive in-house education and training compared to regular employees, making it difficult for them to improve their skills through work. Furthermore, as shown in Figure 1-2-10, companies tend to prioritize specialized knowledge and skills when hiring mid-career employees. This poses a challenge for non-regular employees in building their careers (see Section 2, 1(1) for the definition of "career").

Moreover, with the advancement of science and technology and rapid technological innovation, the specialized knowledge and skills required for occupations are becoming more sophisticated and diverse. Therefore, it is believed that there is a growing need for workers to further their education at universities and other institutions to enhance their expertise or acquire the knowledge and skills necessary to adapt to new occupations. For example, as shown in Figure 1-2-11, approximately 80% of workers cite acquiring the knowledge and skills necessary for their current jobs as the reason for engaging in self-development. However, regarding adult education at universities and other institutions, as shown in Figure 1-2-12, the proportion of university entrants aged 25 or older is approximately 21 percent on average in OECD countries, but remains at only about 2 percent in Japan.

The underlying issues include securing the necessary funds and study time to balance work and learning, the content of available educational programs, and gaining the understanding of employers and other organizations. Educational institutions are also required to implement measures to allow working adults to take classes flexibly, such as offering classes on weekends. For example, as shown in Figure 1-2-13, regarding recurrent education for working adults, the most common challenges cited were "busy work schedule" (approximately 72 percent) and "high cost" (approximately 71 percent). However, a significant number of respondents also cited "difficulty gaining company understanding or disclosing it" (approximately 21 percent) and "lack of comprehensive curricula for working adults" (approximately 16 percent). Furthermore, the most important factor in choosing an educational institution was "attractive curriculum" (approximately 74 percent), followed by "convenient location" (approximately 62 percent), "low tuition fees" (approximately 55 percent), "flexible scheduling" (approximately 52 percent), and "weekend and holiday classes" (50 percent).

Regarding the relationship between the level of education attained and post-graduation employment and income, as shown in Figure 1-2-14, the percentage of people who remain in regular employment is highest for both men and women in the following order: "university/graduate school graduates," "junior college/technical college graduates," "vocational school graduates," and "high school graduates." On the other hand, those who are "junior high school graduates/high school dropouts" or "higher education dropouts" are more likely to be in non-regular employment for both men and women.

Furthermore, as shown in Figures 1-2-15 and 1-2-16, internationally, those who have completed higher education tend to have lower unemployment rates compared to those who have completed upper secondary education (general education), and those who have completed higher education tend to have higher incomes by level of education attainment compared to those who have completed upper secondary education or less. From the above, it is considered important to ensure diverse learning opportunities throughout one's life so that individuals can develop their abilities according to their aspirations and life stages, from the perspective of achieving stable employment and household finances.

title: 平成23年版 厚生労働白書・非正規労働者の正社員化
text: The number of non-regular workers has been increasing in recent years, reaching 17.55 million in 2010, accounting for approximately 30% of the total workforce. Compared to regular workers, non-regular workers face several problems, including: (1) being more susceptible to employment adjustments such as layoffs and termination of contracts, especially during economic downturns; (2) having lower wages and a lower marriage rate; and (3) having fewer opportunities to receive vocational training within companies to improve their skills. To address these issues, and to reduce the number of non-regular workers who are unable to become regular employees despite their desire, and to improve the treatment of non-regular workers, the government is working to support their employment as regular employees, facilitate their conversion to regular employment, and promote equal and balanced treatment through the measures listed below. In addition, the government is promoting comprehensive measures for non-regular workers by utilizing the Job Card system to support career development (see Chapter 2, Section 3, Item 2) and by expanding the safety net through job seeker support systems, etc. (see Chapter 2, Section 1). Amidst the still severe employment and unemployment situation, securing job openings remains a crucial issue, and in particular, there is a need to actively work towards securing more stable permanent positions (employment contracts without a fixed term). Therefore, Hello Work (public employment service) is actively working to secure permanent positions, including conversions from non-regular employment, and promoting permanent employment. Socially problematic forms of dispatch work, such as daily dispatch, and the so-called "dispatch worker layoffs" that became a social issue after the Lehman Shock in the fall of 2008, have highlighted the instability of employment in registered dispatch and manufacturing dispatch work. Furthermore, it has been pointed out that dispatch workers are not receiving treatment commensurate with their work, such as having their wages fixed at low levels. Therefore, the revised Worker Dispatch Act, currently submitted to the Diet, includes provisions to improve the stability of employment and treatment of dispatch workers, such as the principle of prohibiting registered dispatch and manufacturing dispatch, and the obligation to consider equal treatment. If the revised Worker Dispatch Act is enacted, in addition to disseminating information and providing guidance on the legal system, including the obligation to consider equal treatment, the "Special Incentive for Stabilizing Employment of Dispatched Workers" (1 million yen per person (500,000 yen for fixed-term employment) (half price for large companies)) will be utilized to promote the direct employment of dispatched workers at client companies, and guidance and supervision will be thoroughly implemented to correct illegal dispatching practices.

title: Фандрайзинг на аутсорсе: когда пора обращаться к консультанту
text:
Evgeny Zubov believes it's very difficult for NGOs to hire full-time employees these days. Everyone needs fundraisers, marketing, and PR specialists, but no one is applying for these positions. Because there are almost no people with successful experience in the third sector, NGO employees turn to consultants.

"People try to find a solution themselves. For example, they want to increase fundraising through a VKontakte group. The employee sees that we're working on this issue, that we have a ready-made solution because we've already tackled this task. We also communicate when we'll see results and provide guarantees. Not every full-time employee can do this." Evgeny Zubov

Hiring a specialist from a commercial company isn't always the best solution either. They'll still need additional training, and some organizations need results right away. Furthermore, in a large company, a person might only be responsible for one narrow area, such as SMM. At an NGO, their range of responsibilities will likely expand significantly, and they'll have to do more than just write engaging texts for social media.

"In a non-profit organization, it's usually rare for just one thing to be poorly functioning. For example, a foundation has an active and well-functioning Facebook group. But the staff posts a link that leads to a donation page that's not mobile-friendly. A person clicks through to the group, ready to donate to the foundation, but it doesn't work. And an SMM specialist likely won't be able to fix the site."

title: Анастасия Ложкина: «Фандрайзер – заноза в организации»
text:
Numbers, arrows, and ornate diagrams—in the office of the Arithmetic of Goodness charitable foundation, the fundraising department hangs on huge sheets of paper covered in colorful markers. This is the foundation's fundraising strategy for working with individuals. Department head Anastasia Lozhkina believes that fundraising shouldn't be a spontaneous endeavor. She spoke to Teplitsa journalist Ekaterina Ulyanova about how to effectively manage fundraising in a nonprofit.

Imagine that this month, the manager asked a fundraiser to raise 100,000 rubles for the foundation. They expended effort, talked to donors, and brought in the required amount. And then they're told that expenses have increased and they urgently need to raise another 100,000 rubles. This isn't fundraising management, but ad hoc collections that don't lead to the financial stability of the nonprofit, says Anastasia Lozhkina.

Fundraising shouldn't be seen as supporting the organization's core activities. This is a common mistake managers make, the expert emphasizes. They consider working with beneficiaries to be their primary focus, while fundraising is relegated to administrative duties.

"This is the wrong approach. Fundraising is also a programmatic activity of the organization. It's the fundraisers who are the first people donors see. They're the people who talk about the foundation, the social problem, and how the NGO is solving it. Fundraisers are the face of any organization."

title: Falta transparencia en el Plan de Pensiones de Empleados de Telefónica
text:
February 14, 2007 Spain — Telefónica's Employee Pension Plan ended 2006 with a return of 5.5%. This plan has approximately 50% of its assets invested in the stock market, according to its annual report. Other Spanish pension plans with a similar investment profile achieved returns in 2006 that were double that of this plan.

The Spanish stock market rose by an average of 32% last year, and most international markets rose between 15% and 20%.

Telefónica, the General Union of Workers (UGT), and the Workers' Commissions (CCOO) are the only members of the Pension Plan's Oversight Committee. This committee is responsible for monitoring the investments made by the management company (Fonditel), which is owned by Telefónica (70%), CCOO (15%), and UGT (15%). This Commission has not issued a statement regarding the results obtained in the pension plan.

Thus, UGT and CCOO obtained a profit of 4.5 million euros in 2005 from their 30% stake in Fonditel, of which the remaining 70% belongs to Telefónica. According to its latest published results, available on its website, Fonditel Memorias, this company obtained an annual profit of 15.025 billion euros and annual expenses of 6.010 billion euros, of which 3.6 million euros correspond to the salaries of 29 employees, or an average of 124,000 euros per year per employee. This company collects commissions of more than 18 million euros, giving Telefónica, CCOO, and UGT a return of 39% on equity.

It so happens that the elections to the Pension Plan Control Commission were abolished in February 2005. This Commission is the body that should safeguard the interests of the workers in the plan; its election was replaced by the direct appointment of the Telefónica Inter-Center Committee, thus excluding all early retirees from being able to decide on their own money and preventing direct election by active workers.

title: Preocupación en Costa Rica por alto precio en combustibles y electricidad
text:
July 2, 2014 San José, Costa Rica — Two products threaten to drain the wallets of Costa Ricans: electricity and fuel. President Luis Guillermo Solís's government is working to find ways to lower prices after fuel reached its highest cost in Costa Rican history this week.

Gasoline reached 816 colones per liter this week (an average of $1.43), the highest price ever recorded in Costa Rica. To stop these increases, President Solís had requested a report from the Public Services Regulatory Authority (ARESEP), asking for details and recommendations to halt the price hikes.

ARESEP recommended eliminating the tax that funds several institutions, such as the one responsible for road maintenance and the University of Costa Rica laboratory that ensures the quality of materials and workmanship used in public works projects. The president ruled out eliminating this tax.

On the other hand, electricity is becoming a looming threat to the Central American nation. Electricity bills for businesses and homes are steadily increasing due to new rate hikes approved by ARESEP (the Public Services Regulatory Authority). This cost has been responsible for investors fleeing to other countries.

The Solís administration announced yesterday at a press conference the creation of a commission to explore alternatives for lowering electricity prices. These efforts will be led by the Ministry of Environment and Energy, with representatives from business chambers, environmental and academic sectors, and the general public. The commission will study the country's energy matrix and its potential modifications, analyze different energy alternatives such as gas, geothermal, wind, and solar power, examine the formula for calculating electricity rates, and address other related issues.

title: Tanzania: Mgomo wa Walimu Watikisa Nchi
text:
As the teachers' strike continued, President Jakaya Kikwete spoke to the editors of major media outlets on August 1, 2012.

Irenei Kiria tweeted:

I beg for your support. What decision has the President made regarding the teachers' strike?

A user of the JamiiForums network reported online that the President had said that the teachers' demands were unworkable. Dada Subi of the web blog posted the President's speech along with the audio on her blog.

TheHabari blog summarized the statement of Haki Elimu ‏@HakiElimu, an organization that advocates for education issues in Tanzania, regarding the strike:

HakiElimu insists that the country will succeed in improving education only if it invests in teachers by improving their working conditions, teachers' welfare, involving teachers in decisions about education issues and providing them with on-the-job training. Quality education cannot be achieved by helpless teachers

The blog continued:

Government leaders should not belittle teachers; by doing so they are disappointing them. Even if some teachers have not studied for many years as is the case in other professions, they are of great importance. They are the ones who prepare the Tanzanians of today and tomorrow in terms of attitude and knowledge. Therefore, demanding improved working conditions is their right; and the Government can fulfill its duty by listening to them and consulting with them without arrogance and sarcasm

On Thursday, August 2, 2012, the High Court, Labour Division, suspended the teachers' strike on the grounds that it did not comply with the law. MjengwaBlogu reported:

The court today has annulled the ongoing teachers' strike in the country on the grounds that the strike is illegal. The court has also ordered CWT to pay compensation to students affected by the teachers' strike

title: Mbinu za Lugha Zinazotumiwa katika Matangazo ya Biashara ya Kampuni ya Safaricom.
text:
Advertisements are messages sent by sellers of products to the audience to inform them about the existence of various products. Advertisements can be text, audio, visuals, images, paintings or wall paintings. Nowadays, advertisements are made through media such as television, radio, computers, newspapers or posters that are pasted in various parts of the country. According to Vahid and Esmae’li (2012), advertising through the media began between the 1950s and 1960s. They say that at that time, advertisements were broadcast in ordinary language and there were no complex methods used to convey the message to the audience. The increase in industries has led to the increase in various companies that are in a hurry to compete for the few existing customers. This situation has led to the creation of new advertising strategies with the aim of attracting customers.

Safaricom is among the companies that have achieved great success due to their ambitious strategies to advertise their products and services. The company was established in 1993 under the management of Kenya Posts and Telecommunications System (Mwenda, 2015). It was privatized in 1997 and granted a license to operate telecommunications services in 1999. Later in 2000, Vodafone from the United Kingdom acquired a forty percent stake in the company and began to develop it. Later in May 2002, the government sold forty percent of its shares to the public and Safaricom became a public limited company.

title: How Many Species Are There on Earth and in the Ocean?
text:
Robert May [1] recently noted that if aliens visited our planet, one of their first questions would be, “How many distinct life forms—species—does your planet have?” He also pointed out that we would be “embarrassed” by the uncertainty in our answer. This narrative illustrates the fundamental nature of knowing how many species there are on Earth, and our limited progress with this research topic thus far [1]–[4]. Unfortunately, limited sampling of the world's biodiversity to date has prevented a direct quantification of the number of species on Earth, while indirect estimates remain uncertain due to the use of controversial approaches (see detailed review of available methods, estimates, and limitations in Table 1). Globally, our best approximation to the total number of species is based on the opinion of taxonomic experts, whose estimates range between 3 and 100 million species [1]; although these estimations likely represent the outer bounds of the total number of species, expert-opinion approaches have been questioned due to their limited empirical basis [5] and subjectivity [5]–[6] (Table 1). Other studies have used macroecological patterns and biodiversity ratios in novel ways to improve estimates of the total number of species (Table 1), but several of the underlying assumptions in these approaches have been the topic of sometimes heated controversy ([3]–[17], Table 1); moreover their overall predictions concern only specific groups, such as insects [9],[18]–[19], deep sea invertebrates [13], large organisms [6]–[7],[10], animals [7], fungi [20], or plants [21]. With the exception of a few extensively studied taxa (e.g., birds [22], fishes [23]), we are still remarkably uncertain as to how many species exist, highlighting a significant gap in our basic knowledge of life on Earth. Here we present a quantitative method to estimate the global number of species in all domains of life. We report that the number of higher taxa, which is much more completely known than the total number of species [24], is strongly correlated to taxonomic rank [25] and that such a pattern allows the extrapolation of the global number of species for any kingdom of life (Figures 1 and 2).

Higher taxonomy data have been previously used to quantify species richness within specific areas by relating the number of species to the number of genera or families at well-sampled locations, and then using the resulting regression model to estimate the number of species at other locations for which the number of families or genera are better known than species richness (reviewed by Gaston & Williams [24]). This method, however, relies on extrapolation of patterns from relatively small areas to estimate the number of species in other locations (i.e., alpha diversity). Matching the spatial scale of this method to quantify the Earth's total number of species would require knowing the richness of replicated planets; not an option as far as we know, although May's aliens may disagree. Here we analyze higher taxonomic data using a different approach by assessing patterns across all taxonomic levels of major taxonomic groups. The existence of predictable patterns in the higher taxonomic classification of species allows prediction of the total number of species within taxonomic groups and may help to better constrain our estimates of global species richness.

title: Widespread Forest Vertebrate Extinctions Induced by a Mega Hydroelectric Dam in Lowland Amazonia
text:
Hydroelectric dams are rapidly emerging as the new villain in the myriad of anthropogenic threats to tropical forest biotas. Dams displace indigenous communities [1], disrupt the natural flow of rivers [2], critically affect fish populations [3], release vast amounts of greenhouse gases [4], and promote wholesale deforestation and fragmentation of pristine forests [5]. From China to Brazil, hydroelectric dams have been built at an unprecedented scale to supply burgeoning energy demands [6]. More than 945,000 dams higher than 15 m have been built worldwide, altering >50% of all major rivers [7]. In South America alone, some 2,215 new hydroelectric dams are expected to be erected within the next few years [8]. Assessing the true impacts of hydropower infrastructure on natural ecosystems has therefore become an urgent priority for the environmental policy agenda of emergent economies.

In Brazilian Amazonia, over 10 million ha of forests are expected to become permanently inundated following the planned construction of new dams [9], potentially leading to a colossal impact on both terrestrial and aquatic biotas at regional scales. Hydroelectric dams in lowland forests typically resort to low-declivity river basins, submerging vast upstream areas per unit of megawatt output generated, thereby often creating vast archipelagos of forest isolates. Land-bridge islands formed by these artificial lakes may experience stronger isolation effects than forest remnants embedded within a terrestrial landscape, largely because the open-water matrix is invariably less permeable to terrestrial organisms than pastures and second-growth vegetation (e.g. [10–12]). However, despite an embryonic set of studies investigating the long-term impacts of major dams on biodiversity worldwide [13–15], the extinction dynamics of archipelagic landscapes created by hydroelectric reservoirs remains poorly understood in tropical forest regions, specially for Amazonian reservoirs (but see [16–17]).

Terrestrial vertebrates are pivotal components of tropical forest dynamics through their ecological roles as hyper-consumers, large predators, frugivores, seed dispersers, and structural habitat modification [18–19]. They are also widely hailed as pinnacle conservation icons, contributing much public charisma for tropical forest conservation. In Amazonia, hunting pressure is the strongest driver of local extinctions of medium and large mammals stranded in fragmented landscapes [20–21]. With the exception of primates [16], no study has assessed the long-term impacts of a hydroelectric reservoir on medium and large-bodied vertebrates at the community level in Amazonian land-bridge islands. Yet this is required to both elucidate the positive or negative effects of existing dams on biodiversity, and refine environmental impact assessments of future dams.

title: تعليق المبادرة المصرية للحقوق الشخصية على تعديلات اللائحة التنفيذية لقانون البيئة: المزيد من التنازلات في شروط استخدام الفحم
text:
Last March, the Prime Minister issued Decree No. 618 of 2017, amending the executive regulations of the Environmental Law. Most of the amendments focused on the standards and conditions for coal use outlined in Appendix No. 12 of the previous executive regulations. These amendments, with their exceptions, omissions of controls, and vague wording, indicate a clear trend toward weakening and dismantling the application of environmental and health protection standards against the harmful effects of coal.

The previous executive regulations were issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 964 of 2015, following the decision to include coal in the energy mix, in order to establish rules governing its use in Egypt. It is worth noting that several environmental organizations objected at the time to some of the provisions of those regulations, arguing that the environmental standards and conditions they contained did not provide sufficient protection for the environment and public health.

Dr. Environmental researcher Rajia Al-Jarzawi stated, "The inclusion of coal in the energy mix, which faced widespread opposition due to its harmful effects on health and the environment, was accompanied by assurances from government authorities that coal use would adhere to strict standards comparable to the latest international standards. While this argument is weak in the face of numerous scientific proofs confirming the harmful effects of coal even when international standards are met, and while the environmental standards in the previous regulations did not truly meet the latest international standards, the recent amendments threaten even greater environmental and health risks."

The recent amendments introduced further exceptions to compliance with environmental conditions and standards. The most egregious of these exceptions appeared in Article 4 (amending clause (1) in Section 2, "Requirements and Standards for Intermediate Storage Stations Outside Ports"), which allowed coal storage stations to be exempted from the requirement to be located 3 kilometers away from residential areas, citing "necessity" as the reason, according to the regulations. It is worth noting that the previous regulations themselves had already included an exception allowing the burning of coal as fuel in residential areas "for reasons of necessity and the public interest." These new amendments, however, have added an exception regarding storage, further exacerbating the anticipated harm. While this is not the first time the administration has attempted to justify this retreat from environmental protection by citing "necessity and the public interest," it fails to define the nature of these "necessities" or how they might serve the public interest rather than the private interests of companies, making this justification difficult to accept.

The amendments also resorted to eliminating many of the details of the conditions and standards explicitly stated in the previous regulations. They delegated the task of defining these details and granting approvals to the Ministry of Environment, its agency, or its coal committee, without establishing specific controls and rules for the conditions or approvals. This could open the door to evading strict environmental standards. While the omission of details might be justifiable in legislation, it is not so in regulations. Laws are not easily changed, while regulations are easily amended and even necessary to keep pace with changes and developments. The executive regulations for the environment themselves have been amended twice in the past two years. The benefit of including details in the regulations lies in their clear and public disclosure of what is permitted and prohibited, ensuring that everyone is aware of it and that those affected can appeal to the courts. Details drafted internally within ministries and government departments, however, may lack this clarity.

title: هل أعجبك طعم البلاستيك اليوم؟
text:
The world first learned to manufacture plastic from petroleum in the early 20th century, and its use expanded significantly in the 1950s, with production reaching two million tons in 1950. Since then, plastic production has increased exponentially, reaching 381 million tons in 2015. Plastic is truly a unique material: versatile, inexpensive, easily molded, and durable. It is used in the manufacture of almost all products, including cars, airplanes, weapons, electrical and electronic devices, medical equipment, building materials, clothing, furniture, packaging, and much more.

Humans have produced and consumed enormous quantities of plastic without giving much thought to what to do with its waste after use. Most plastic products are not suitable for recycling, and even those that can be recycled are of lower quality and cannot be recycled more than once or twice. Furthermore, plastic is not biodegradable; it only breaks down very slowly into microscopic particles (microplastics) through ultraviolet radiation. These particles do not appear to decompose completely but accumulate in marine and terrestrial environments and enter the food chain.

The excessive use of plastics, particularly in single-use and disposable applications, has exacerbated the situation. Packaging accounts for 47% of plastic use; one million plastic water bottles are purchased every minute, and the world produces 500 billion plastic bags every year. A single water bottle could take five centuries, and a plastic bag about 30 years, to disappear, leaving behind an environmental legacy that may last forever.

The world has produced 9 billion tons of plastic throughout history. Only 9% has been recycled, and about 15% has been incinerated. Approximately 6 billion tons of plastic waste are with us and are constantly increasing. Every year, 300 million tons of plastic waste are added to the world's plastic reserves—a figure equivalent to the average weight of the entire human population.

Where does all this waste go?

It's simply all around us, inside us, and everywhere.

Every year, about 13 million tons of plastic end up in the oceans—roughly the equivalent of a truckload of waste being unloaded every minute. This debris accumulates due to ocean currents in five major eddies in the ocean, the combined area of which is equal to the size of Europe. The largest of these is located in the South Pacific and covers an area three times the size of Spain. It is estimated that by 2050, the weight of plastic in the oceans will exceed the weight of all the fish in the world.

Plastic waste reaches the oceans either through direct dumping into waterways, or through dispersal by wind, rain, and tides from its sources or from open landfills.
