Before that, plastic waste, especially lightweight plastics, may be found in streets, farms, and everywhere else. It may be ingested by animals and livestock, or it may clog canals and drains. People may burn it, releasing toxic substances into the air, or it may decompose on-site, releasing these toxins into the soil and groundwater.

Birds, land and sea animals, and fish swallow plastic bags and small pieces, causing them to choke, become ill, have their intestines ruptured, or die of starvation. It has been found that more than 260 marine species have swallowed plastic, including 15% of endangered species. 70% of sea turtles in the Red Sea have died due to ingesting plastic. By 2050, 99% of seabirds will have swallowed plastic.

title: 臺灣森林濕地的保護網評估初探
text: According to the results of the "Pilot Project for the Survey of Forest-Type Wetland Resources in Taiwan," commissioned by the Forestry Bureau and conducted by research teams from Chinese Culture University and Ilan University, Taiwan has 276 forest wetlands, a considerable number. Theoretically, including all these wetlands in protected areas would be a foolproof approach. However, this idea faces substantial difficulties in implementation. Therefore, the biggest challenge in forest wetland conservation currently lies in determining which wetlands should be included in the conservation scope. To differentiate the conservation value of wetlands, conservation grading is an effective approach. Grading wetlands not only helps understand their conservation value but also serves as a basis for determining the conservation network. The concept of a conservation network is particularly important in wetlands because wetland organisms often cannot rely on a single wetland for survival. The Ramsar Convention emphasizes international cooperation, with the ultimate goal of establishing an international wetland conservation network. Taiwan's forest wetland conservation should adopt this approach, which not only aligns with the spirit of the Wetland Conservation Act but also provides a more comprehensive protection for wetland ecosystems. Assessment is a crucial means of determining conservation. Currently, the assessment of the importance of wetland conservation in Taiwan is conducted through the "National Important Wetland Selection and Survey Mechanism" proposed by the Construction and Planning Agency. However, this mechanism passively selects wetlands for evaluation (e.g., through group recommendations) and relies primarily on expert discussions. Therefore, it depends heavily on the subjective opinions of those involved in the selection process and lacks objective evaluation indicators. To avoid the dilemma of subjective judgment regarding wetland conservation value, using objective evaluation indicators is a feasible approach. Objective indicators refer to the inherent characteristics of wetlands. A review of previously published research reveals that characteristics such as biodiversity, rarity, naturalness, area, representativeness, threat of human disturbance, scientific value, and ecological vulnerability are frequently used. Data for each of these indicators must be collected through on-site surveys.

title: 生物多樣性的永續使用與「里山倡議」
text: What exactly does the Satoyama Initiative advocate? Simply put, it promotes the maintenance, restoration, or reconstruction of "Socio-ecological Production Landscapes" (SEPLs) worldwide to improve human well-being and achieve the three goals of the Convention on Biological Diversity. A landscape refers to a heterogeneous region composed of various distinct patches arranged in a mosaic pattern. Landscape ecologists call these patches landscape elements; for example, agricultural landscapes include farmland, grasslands, streams, forests, and villages. These elements (patches) are interwoven like patches of varying sizes, colors, and patterns. An agricultural landscape is also a production landscape because it is primarily used for producing crops (such as rice and forests) or harvesting livestock and fish. A healthy productive landscape not only produces goods such as food and timber, but also provides services beyond those goods, such as nutrient cycling, soil conditioning, flood control, water and air purification, and spiritual inspiration. However, many productive landscapes overuse fertilizers, pesticides, and herbicides to increase yields; and they switch from multi-crop to single-crop farming to improve efficiency. These agricultural practices reduce the naturalness of the landscape, making it difficult to sustain its ecological functions or provide complete ecosystem services. Over time, this inevitably leads to environmental problems and may even cause a gradual decline in crop yields or quality. Therefore, the European Union has recently begun subsidizing farmers to encourage them to improve unsustainable production methods in order to maintain ecologically sound productive landscapes.

title: Quartäre Klimaschwankungen: Schätzung der Temperaturschwankungen in Grönland mittels hochaufgelöster Isotopenmessung an im Eis archivierter Luft
text:
Ice core measurements can yield a wealth of information, much of which is relevant to questions about climate change, as ice archives the climate history of hundreds of thousands of years. Therefore, such measurements allow us to retrospectively explore the Earth system: Why did ice ages occur, why did they end, and what caused this? Why was the climate so unstable during the ice ages? How large were the temperature variations between ice ages and interglacial periods, or between warm and cold phases during the last ice age? These are questions that can be investigated using ice cores, sometimes in combination with other climate archives (marine sediments, lake sediments, tree rings, and others).

However, ice cores offer far more than the extremely useful concentration measurements mentioned above. Physical parameters of the ice, such as electrical conductivity, dust content, and others, allow for the creation of a preliminary timescale through comparison with other measured ice cores, which is then refined through subsequent analyses. These follow-up analyses include the determination of chemical traces in the ice, which provide information about the emission intensity, emission locations, and atmospheric circulation of chemical substances, and can also suggest chemical reactions.

This article, however, will focus specifically on the analysis of stable isotopes in ice cores. Within an element, there are usually several isotopes (nuclides with different numbers of neutrons), which are either stable or radioactive. Both types are of great importance in research, including ice core analysis. Here, however, only stable isotopes are considered. The aim is to investigate the extent of temperature fluctuations during the last ice age in Greenland.

title: Mensch - Umwelt - Klima: Perspektiven der Quartärforschung in der Schweiz: Einführung zum Themenheft
text:
The Quaternary (Ice Age), the most recent period in Earth's history, spans the last 2.6 million years and continues to the present day. This epoch is characterized by significant climate fluctuations, which are documented in geological deposits on the continents and in the oceans, as well as in polar ice cores. The image of a nearly completely glaciated Switzerland over 20,000 years ago contrasts sharply with the current climate scenario of a potentially soon completely ice-free Alpine region.

Humans first appeared in Europe during the Quaternary. Since around 5,500 years ago, the beginning of settled life, modern humans (Homo sapiens) have become a significant factor in the environmental system. They are primarily responsible for the transformation of the former natural landscape into the cultural landscape of today. During the warm and cold phases of the Ice Age, specific plant and animal communities developed, and their remains provide important insights into the natural environment and the lifestyles and economic practices of people in earlier times. The aspect of climate and climate change on a wide range of spatial and temporal scales is always and inextricably linked to Quaternary research. Given the current accelerated development in the "greenhouse Earth," deciphering climate history has become one of the most important sectors of Quaternary "research into the past."

Since the time of Louis Agassiz, one of the main founders of the Ice Age theory at the beginning of the 19th century, Switzerland, repeatedly shaped by Ice Age glaciers, can undoubtedly be called the "cradle of Quaternary research." It continues to offer an extraordinary wealth of formations and archaeological sites for deciphering environmental and human history, addressing a wide variety of questions in the geosciences and human sciences. A whole range of scientific disciplines are currently concerned with the Quaternary period and the development of early humans. Communication, exchange, and networking between the often independent and isolated researchers—individuals or groups from universities, institutes, government agencies, or even practically oriented companies (e.g., geological surveying firms)—have become central and indispensable concerns of modern Quaternary research.

title: हलमा से बनाई हजारों जल संरचनाएँ
text: Once again, the tribals astonished everyone with the power and brilliance of their labor. The confidence of these people, sweating for water, was palpable. The dream of a lush green hill shimmered in their eyes. Their passion was such that they even brought their own spades and shovels from their homes. The women, too, were not to be left behind. They too, carrying baskets, walked alongside. This scene unfolded on Hathipawa Hill, near Jhabua city in the tribal-dominated Jhabua region of Madhya Pradesh. Here, the tribals performed Halma. Halma means collective labor. Determined to transform a barren hill into a lush green one, more than six thousand tribals transformed the face of the hill in a matter of hours. In just five hours, they constructed more than fifteen thousand water structures (contour trenches) and cleaned nearly 25,000 old contour trenches, all without spending a penny. This will make the hill lush with the next rains, while also allowing a large amount of water to percolate into the ground. If the government were to undertake this work, it would cost at least ten lakh rupees. This will allow approximately 400 million liters of rainwater to reach the ground every year. This water could provide daily water for over 5 million people.

title: सब कुछ लौटा रहा है समुद्र
text: City sewers aren't just filled with bodily waste, urine, soap, and oil; they also contain a variety of other impurities. Many factories dispose of various synthetic chemicals and toxins into municipal sewers because the cost of cleaning them eats into their profits. While there are laws to prevent this, the government is unwilling to crack down on violators, seeing it as a hindrance to industrial development. Therefore, factories willfully release toxic chemicals into drains or groundwater. Our environment has become so polluted that there's no escape from these toxins. Not just factories, our homes, schools, and hospitals are also filled with a variety of synthetic chemicals. These include pesticides and medicines, but the biggest danger lies in metals that can cause significant harm even in minute quantities. These are called "heavy metals." These include elements like arsenic, mercury, and lead. These are used in many factories, but safe disposal methods are not adopted in our country. The effects of these toxic substances do not become apparent immediately, but gradually over many years. Therefore, their dangers are often overlooked.

title: Italia: continua l'ondata di neve e gelo, disagi nelle regioni adriatiche
text:
In the Marche region, snow has been falling steadily since Saturday morning, causing disruptions especially in the provinces of Ascoli Piceno and Macerata. In Ascoli Piceno, 50 cm of snow fell, while in some peripheral areas and the Sibillini Mountains, at least 1 meter of snow is estimated. Numerous calls to the Fire Department were received, primarily due to accidents caused by ice and fallen trees. A fir tree fell on the Statale Piceno Aprutina highway, causing no casualties but blocking traffic for several hours. Another tree fell on Viale Benedetto Croce, in the Porta Maggiore neighborhood, where it hit a car parked underneath.

The greatest difficulties were encountered in the municipalities of Piagge, Rosara, and Venagrande, also in the Province of Ascoli Piceno, where law enforcement had to intervene. On the highway leading to Offida, a man was seriously injured when his car collided with a tree due to slippery asphalt and ice. In Maltignano, a bus on the ARPA line connecting the Ascoli and Teramo areas was stuck for several hours, having come to a halt across the road and preventing normal traffic flow. Another bus, this time a city bus, was stopped on Viale Treviri. At the Porta Cartara interchange, three accidents occurred due to the completely icy ramp. In the Ropaga area, seven cars went off the road, and it took hours of work before the firefighters, along with the ACI and ANAS, were able to get the vehicles back on the road.

title: Suolo, pioggia, disastri e modello di sviluppo
text:
Disasters and floods aren't just the fault of local governments. It's the development model that's disrupting the planet's climate. Anyone who doesn't speak out against this model of consumption is complicit in the disasters and the planet's upheaval. Don't look elsewhere for blame. Ask yourself what you're not doing to prevent the environmental crisis.

In every broadcast, we witness a discussion that seems to ignore the root causes of the conditions that are leading to the floods. The blackout seems incredible. As the wise man says: God blinds those who want to ruin!

The protests focus on the inability of municipalities, civil defense, the government, etc., to address the emergency.

Therefore, when addressed, the problems of the hydrogeological disaster remove the main cause of the disaster: the disruption of the planet's cycles due to the model of consumption for which we are all responsible as consumers within this development model.

No politicians are attempting to address this issue. It's too difficult to build consensus by addressing the facts. It's better to shift the blame to one or another decision by a city council, a local authority, or the government, to amnesties, land management, or the efficiency of intervention structures. All of these are right and proper.

Having consumed agricultural and mountainous land to build over it for the sole benefit of construction companies, on the altar of a concrete-based development model, is a curse we will pay for decades, perhaps centuries.

But we must not forget that from the use of private cars, to mobility never planned rationally and collectively, from the production and consumption of plastics, to the waste of water and land for food production based on increasingly unsustainable and unconscious dietary patterns—which among other things cause deterioration in people's health and often chronic diseases that then impact community healthcare costs—from the levels of waste production that often pollute land and water, to the destruction of renewable resources, the difficulty in switching to renewable energy, and so on, we have plundered a planet that is responding with new climate cycles that will increasingly disrupt "our beautiful garden."

title: 第5章　科学技術・学術政策の総合的推進：文部科学省
text: The Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT) is working on developing sensors and unmanned submersible technologies to investigate untapped marine mineral resources, including seafloor hydrothermal deposits, utilizing technologies from universities and the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC), as well as conducting research aimed at elucidating the origins of marine resources. In September 2011, the Marine Development Subcommittee of the Council for Science and Technology compiled the "Marine Resource Exploration Technology Demonstration Plan," a medium- to long-term technology demonstration plan of approximately five years, outlining the specific content and schedule of research and development. Furthermore, in light of the growing public interest in and need for the sustainable use of marine biological resources and the conservation of marine biodiversity, MEXT began research and development in FY2011 as part of the "Marine Resource Utilization Promotion Technology Development Program: Advanced Technology for Securing Marine Biological Resources," which aims to elucidate the physiological functions of marine organisms and lead to innovative production, as well as research and development to comprehensively elucidate ecosystems with the aim of accurately predicting fluctuations in the amount of biological resources. At the same time, the Marine Development Subcommittee of the Council for Science and Technology considered "the ideal way of conducting research on marine biological resources," and compiled a report in September 2011. The Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) conducts observations of the ocean, land surface, and atmosphere in the Asia-Pacific region and the Arctic region, using research vessels, marine environment observation buoys, and land-based observation equipment, with the aim of elucidating global environmental changes such as global warming. In addition, to conduct research on submarine crustal activity such as the movement of oceanic plates and research on organisms that widely inhabit the ocean, JAMSTEC conducts marine area surveys using ships, manned submersibles, and unmanned submersibles. Regarding the 2011 Tohoku earthquake and tsunami, JAMSTEC conducted an investigation using the deep-sea research vessel "Kairei" and showed that fault rupture along the plate boundary reached the trench axis of the Japan Trench, and that the crustal deformation was greatest near the trench axis, with a movement of approximately 50m in the east-southeast direction and an uplift of approximately 10m. Furthermore, using the manned submersible "Shinkai 6500" (Photo 2-5-11), we conducted a diving survey in the epicenter area and discovered numerous cracks in the seabed at depths of 3,200m to 5,350m in the epicenter region, and that bacterial mats formed by the proliferation of large amounts of bacteria were located around them (Photo 2-5-12). In addition, we are operating the deep-sea drilling vessel "Chikyu," which aims to reach the Earth's mantle, a place never before reached by humankind, and are promoting a deep-sea drilling project under the framework of the Integrated Ocean Drilling Program (IODP) with the aim of elucidating global environmental change, the Earth's internal structure, and the biosphere within the Earth's crust. In fiscal year 2011, we advanced the Nankai Trough earthquake zone drilling project, and by analyzing the collected geological samples, we achieved results such as the discovery of physical evidence identifying the fault that was active during the 1944 Tonankai earthquake and the discovery of traces of fault activity that caused the giant tsunami.

title: 神奈川県足柄下郡箱根町における特定外来生物オオハンゴンソウ（Rudbeckia laciniata L.）の駆除活動による著しい個体数減少
text: The issue of invasive species is one of the important challenges for the conservation of biodiversity in Japan (Somiya 2016). In 2015, the Ministry of the Environment presented the "Action Plan for Preventing Damage from Invasive Species," outlining its approach to "mainstreaming" invasive species countermeasures into social activities (Somiya 2016). At the same time, the "List of Invasive Species That May Cause Damage to Ecosystems in Japan" was also published, indicating a direction to further promote invasive species countermeasures, building upon the Invasive Alien Species Act enacted in 2005 (Somiya 2016). The number of confirmed and certified control measures based on the Invasive Alien Species Act has exceeded 1,000 nationwide (Ministry of the Environment https://www.env.go.jp/nature/intro/3control/kakunin.html Last accessed February 8, 2020), and it can be said that invasive species countermeasures are steadily being incorporated into social activities. While activities related to countermeasures against invasive species are expanding, it has also become widely recognized that eradicating invasive species once they have invaded and established themselves is extremely difficult (Akasaka and Goka 2012; Osawa and Ohmae 2016). In fact, reports of successful eradication of invasive species or minimization of population size in Japan are still few, although there are a few examples such as the Argentine ant Linepithema humile in Tokyo (Sakamoto et al. 2017), the mongoose Herpestes auropunctatus in Amami (Wataru 2019), and the Canada goose Branta canadensis around Mt. Fuji (Kato 2016). In addition, eradication activities for invasive species are almost always long-term, and those working on the front lines towards eradication often become exhausted by the continued effort with no end in sight (Osawa and Ohmae 2016). For this reason, the idea of setting realistic goals such as containment rather than eradication as the goal of management is gaining traction (Akasaka and Goka 2012; Osawa and Omae 2016; Osawa and Kawano 2019; Panetta and Cacho 2012). Nevertheless, if effective eradication measures are established based on scientific evidence and eradication activities can be carried out continuously at an intensity that exceeds the reproduction or dispersal rate of the target species, the target species should be eradicated or its population size minimized. In fact, some argue that eradication is now being recognized as a realistic goal for invasive species control (Wataru 2019).

title: Биоразнообразие в лесных экосистемах: зачем и как его оценивать
text: Biodiversity is currently a popular concept not only in specialized scientific literature but also in the international and public environmental movement. It should be noted that in the latter context—that is, in speeches by politicians, city administration representatives, the environmentally minded public, and the like—the term is particularly frequently and, unfortunately, in an amateurish manner (which, incidentally, also applies to the interpretation of the word "ecology"...). Because of this, the modern interpretation of biodiversity is ambiguous, leading to much debate and disagreement even among environmental specialists. Therefore, it is first necessary to understand the meaning of biodiversity. As a term in specialized literature, biodiversity has been used since 1894 to describe the number, variety, and variability of living organisms. As experience in bioecological research has accumulated, the concept of biodiversity has evolved and expanded its meaning. The first scientifically formulated concept of biodiversity as a phenomenon emerged from the research of population geneticists between 1908 and 1953. In the population genetic understanding, biological diversity is created by three independently acting processes: spontaneously arising genetic variations, the action of natural selection in mixed populations, and isolation—geographical and reproductive [4]. On this basis, as a result of natural selection over billions of years, two processes—speciation and extinction—have created the planet's most valuable resource—biodiversity. This gives rise to two levels of biodiversity: genetic—the diversity of genetic properties among individuals of a single species, and species—the diversity of species within a community of organisms. This led to the interpretation of biodiversity as a valuable natural resource, serving as a source of biological evolution and the basis for genetic engineering. Since the mid-1950s, two processes—a growing awareness of the dangers of increasing negative consequences of anthropogenic impacts on the biosphere and the development of the natural sciences—have led ecology to emerge from the realm of biology as an independent, interdisciplinary, and complex field, exploring the interactions of organisms with their environment and providing the scientific basis for rational nature management. At the same time, the concept of "biodiversity" has also been given a greening treatment. It has become clear that humans can be just as much a factor in the extinction of biological species as natural phenomena—climate change, volcanic eruptions, etc.—with one crucial difference: anthropogenic impact can contribute to the premature extinction of species, which cannot be compensated for by speciation: the development of a new species requires between 2,000 and 100,000 generations [5].

title: Динамика разнообразия лесных сообществ, флоры и фауны европейской тайги в естественных условиях и после антропогенных воздействий: опыт исследований и обобщения
text: The spontaneous development of primary forests also occurred through the periodic formation of windfall clearings or "windows" of varying sizes (from a few square meters to several thousand hectares). This process is typical in landscapes with spruce stands. Regardless of the terrain, soil cover, and other conditions, individual spruce trees, groups of spruce trees, or entire sections of spruce stands fall. The reasons for this pattern are quite obvious and simple. Spruce, with its dense, low-hanging crown and shallow root system, is highly susceptible to wind damage. It can be argued that dark coniferous taiga is a windfall in various stages of recovery. In landscapes with pine stands, such phenomena typically do not occur. Pine, with its open, high crown and powerful taproot system, can easily withstand even strong winds. Its resilience is evidenced by the frequently observed "wind-blown" pines or even groups of them. In other words, wind can break a pine trunk, but it cannot topple it. Thus, forests in different landscape types have varying degrees of wind resistance and, accordingly, develop different "wind-driven" successional systems.

title: Inicia caminata ambientalista en Costa Rica por más de 120 km
text:
July 11, 2011 San José, Costa Rica — An environmental march began today in Costa Rica, covering more than 120 kilometers over six days. The protesters are demanding the renegotiation of a contract with a concessionary company, the passage of a bill for coastal communities, and the cancellation of a contract with a mining company.

The main group of marchers consists of 12 people, but they have since been joined by others, bringing the total to nearly 100 protesters. They departed from the recently inaugurated National Stadium of Costa Rica, heading towards Ciudad Colón.

During the march, they were escorted by several police officers and interviewed by various media outlets. They were also accompanied by Congressman José María Villata Flores-Estrada of the Broad Front party.

The Coastal Territories Law aims to provide more than 50 communities with a legal framework that prevents the eviction of families living in these territories, while also restricting economic activities to practices consistent with the protection of the maritime-terrestrial zone.

The walkers will stop in Ciudad Colón, Atenas, Orotina, Caldera, and Puntarenas, where they will spend the nights with lodging and meals provided by the communities themselves.

Groups from each town will welcome the walkers upon their arrival and accompany them on their departure the following morning until they complete the day's route.

The activity is organized by the Environmental Commission of the Broad Front, the National Front of Coastal Territories, and the Citizen Action Party. Activists from various youth, community, environmental, and human rights organizations will also join the walk.

title: La capa de ozono llega a su peor deterioro en la historia de la humanidad
text:
April 9, 2011 San José, Costa Rica — Recent studies show the ozone layer is more depleted than ever before in human history. The "blanket" that protects us from the sun's harmful ultraviolet rays deteriorated by 40% between December and March.

The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) predicted a 30% depletion for the same period; however, industrial chemical reactions damaged the ozone layer more than anticipated.

As a consequence, global weather patterns have been altered. A warmer winter was reported on the Antarctic ice, while several kilometers above the ground, temperatures plummeted to unprecedented levels. These data were captured, stored, and reported by satellites and weather balloons.

An intense rainy season is expected this year in Central America, where some countries are already reporting cloudy skies and low temperatures. Meteorologists in Costa Rica reported that this will be one of the rainiest seasons ever seen in the country. One symptom of the damage caused to the ozone layer is the arrival of the rainy season three months earlier than expected.

The Montreal Protocol, signed by the UN in 1987, completely banned the use of dozens of chemicals that cause serious damage to the ozone layer; however, scientists say it will take decades for these chemicals to disappear from the atmosphere.

title: Ujitokezaji wa Maudhui ya Utunzaji wa Mazingira katika Hadithi Teule za Watoto: Mifano kutoka Fasihi ya Kiswahili
text: Etymologically, the concept of ecology is derived from two Greek roots: oikos (house) and logy (science or discipline of) (Odum, 1975). Therefore, ecology is a discipline that studies the relationship between organisms and their environment. There is a strong relationship between humans, plants, animals and the natural environment. The state of the environment at a given time reflects the type and level of life status of living organisms. In addition, the level of quality of life of living organisms reflects the state of the natural environment at a given time. This is the ecological relationship. Ecological relationships appear in various forms. For example, human life depends on plants because they are the ones that produce oxygen gas which is essential in the respiratory system. Plants are the source of rain which is a basic requirement for agricultural, fishing and livestock activities. Plants also depend largely on the manure produced by animals like humans which produce large amounts of carbon dioxide which is an important raw material for plants in the process of synthesizing their food.

title: Dhima ya Kiswahili katika Uimarishaji wa Utamaduni na Mazingira kwa Mujibu wa Katiba ya Kenya
text:
This article also emphasizes the responsibility of everyone to cooperate with government departments and other people in protecting and preserving the environment and ensuring ecological development and resource utilization.

These recommendations will only be meaningful and useful to the average citizen if their translation is provided in an African language that can give him a complete picture of what is being discussed. This is because environmental issues are often explained in foreign languages, especially English, through the use of complex scientific terms that are difficult to decipher for people who do not have a high level of knowledge of these issues.

The Swahili language can be a strong tool for educating the public about the importance of preserving the environment, the benefits we get from it and the losses resulting from environmental degradation. If this is fully implemented, the situation of ignorance such as that which arose regarding the invasion of various forests in this country may not occur again. The efforts of environmentalists such as the late Wangari Maathai can be more successful if methods such as those we have discussed regarding cultural preservation are used to spread the message regarding environmental conservation.

Advertisements on various environmental issues can also be made in Kiswahili through writings and drawings on clothing such as handkerchiefs, scarves, shirts, sheets and even blankets. Book publishers can also be encouraged to put such messages on the covers of books used at various levels to emphasize this issue. In addition, translations of various environmental works written in foreign languages can be done in Kiswahili and contribute significantly to environmental conservation efforts. This will ensure that Kenyans have a better chance of being educated about the environment and thus avoid the damage caused by ignorance.

This language will also sensitize citizens on their rights regarding the use of environmental resources as enshrined in Article 70 of Chapter Five.

title: Attention and Augmented Recurrent Neural Networks
text:
When I’m translating a sentence, I pay special attention to the word I’m presently translating. When I’m transcribing an audio recording, I listen carefully to the segment I’m actively writing down. And if you ask me to describe the room I’m sitting in, I’ll glance around at the objects I’m describing as I do so.

Neural networks can achieve this same behavior using attention, focusing on part of a subset of the information they’re given. For example, an RNN can attend over the output of another RNN. At every time step, it focuses on different positions in the other RNN.

We’d like attention to be differentiable, so that we can learn where to focus. To do this, we use the same trick Neural Turing Machines use: we focus everywhere, just to different extents.

The attention distribution is usually generated with content-based attention. The attending RNN generates a query describing what it wants to focus on. Each item is dot-producted with the query to produce a score, describing how well it matches the query. The scores are fed into a softmax to create the attention distribution.

title: How to Use t-SNE Effectively
text:
A popular method for exploring high-dimensional data is something called t-SNE, introduced by van der Maaten and Hinton in 2008 . The technique has become widespread in the field of machine learning, since it has an almost magical ability to create compelling two-dimensonal “maps” from data with hundreds or even thousands of dimensions. Although impressive, these images can be tempting to misread. The purpose of this note is to prevent some common misreadings.

We’ll walk through a series of simple examples to illustrate what t-SNE diagrams can and cannot show. The t-SNE technique really is useful—but only if you know how to interpret it.

Before diving in: if you haven’t encountered t-SNE before, here’s what you need to know about the math behind it. The goal is to take a set of points in a high-dimensional space and find a faithful representation of those points in a lower-dimensional space, typically the 2D plane. The algorithm is non-linear and adapts to the underlying data, performing different transformations on different regions. Those differences can be a major source of confusion.

title: هل علينا الوثوق في شركات الاتصالات والإنترنت؟
text:
The relationship between a citizen and a service provider—whether a telecommunications company, government agency, grocery store, or hospital—often begins with a set of personal questions posed by the provider before addressing the service itself. These questions typically include the individual's name, address, phone number, and possibly a copy of their national ID card with all its data. Before proceeding with the service, the provider may ask you to sign a document to initiate the process. In the technology and internet sectors, this document often takes the form of a form with a "yes" box at the end.

We use search engines daily to explore topics of interest, whether sports, arts, religion, politics, or health, all contributing to our general knowledge and our ability to think critically and make decisions. We also communicate daily through various communication tools and methods for social and professional purposes. We regularly watch entertaining and educational videos. Furthermore, most of us jot down notes and ideas in drafts, emails, computer files, or notebooks.

A few years ago, I was deeply shocked to discover that a record of all my search queries on Google over the years was accessible. Part of the shock came from seeing the evolution of my interests, my reading, and my thoughts over time. A greater shock, however, was the very existence of this record, which revealed so much about me. I decided to investigate other records I was unaware of, which were held by other companies. I discovered a record of all the videos I had watched on YouTube over the years and another containing every search term I had typed on Facebook. I felt a surge of anger and a profound sense of the collapse of the privacy I had assumed existed—a truly disturbing reality.

I realized that internet and telecommunications companies possess an almost unbridled ability to deduce our behaviors, preferences, and social networks, sometimes even better than our closest confidants or ourselves. Meanwhile, companies within our own countries either shirk their responsibility to hand over our personal data to those in power, citing "binding orders," or actively facilitate public surveillance based on "mutual interests" with those in power.

title: معاداة التقنية
text:
The issue of internet regulation worldwide raises primarily procedural questions. As a global and self-regulating medium, the internet poses several regulatory questions, chief among them the question of geographical jurisdiction: where are cybercrimes committed? The nature of the internet often allows for the perpetrator to be in one country and the victim in another, or for both to be in the same location while the crime is committed on an information system in a different country. This is often what is known as publishing offenses, as in Egypt, for example, where most websites operate through information systems located in other countries. Another question, which has become increasingly important after the discovery of the extent of surveillance carried out by governments and other entities against internet users, is the question of judicial warrants for surveillance. Mass internet surveillance requires authorities to intercept and examine all communications to find the message they seek. This renders a specific, limited judicial search warrant entirely incompatible with this type of internet surveillance. Such practices violate the Egyptian Constitution and Egyptian legislation, including the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights, which is part of national law and applicable according to Article 93 of the Constitution, and the Criminal Procedure Code No. 150 of 1950.

The draft "Combating Cybercrime" law is not intended to address this type of question, which has arisen as a result of the internet's widespread adoption as the primary communication medium, the largest source of information, and the most important arena for organization and assembly, particularly in countries lacking freedom of expression, association, and peaceful assembly. The legislature has not attempted to address the problems of jurisdiction and territorial authority. Judges issue convictions in most cases involving information technology, particularly in publishing cases, exceeding their territorial jurisdiction. Individuals are punished for actions that occurred on computer systems outside the court's territorial jurisdiction, perhaps due to a lack of knowledge of information technology. To date, the authors of this report have not encountered any Egyptian court rulings that address the jurisdiction and territorial authority of these courts, nor any requests for legal opinions from the Supreme Court on these matters.

Instead of attempting to address these procedural dilemmas, most of the law's provisions are penal, punishing crimes described in the explanatory memorandum to the government's 2015 draft law as "a new type of crime previously unknown." This is the primary focus of this policy analysis.

The draft cybercrime law creates a new situation in Egyptian criminal law, establishing new penalties based on the method of committing the crimes, rather than the crimes themselves. For example, impersonation or incitement to commit violent crimes will be punished differently if committed online than if the same crimes, causing the same level of harm to the same people, were committed by other means. This is akin to attempting to legislate a different punishment for murder committed with a firearm than for murder committed with a sword, claiming that technological advancements, such as the invention of gunpowder, led to the creation of new crimes. However, the crime remains the same: the violation of the right to life through murder, regardless of the method used.

The proposed law and its supporting propaganda attempt to argue that "electronic forgery" differs from forgery, and that "cyber hacking"—that is, unauthorized access to information systems—differs from property infringement, whether through unauthorized entry, damage, or theft, and so on for other types of crimes. This undermines the principle of justice and equality before the law and increases the likelihood of the law being deemed unconstitutional.

Issuing penal provisions specific to the digital domain with harsher penalties results in the law moving from punishing attacks on the rights and freedoms of others and causing harm to themselves or their property to punishing the use of specific tools in committing criminal acts. This negates the principle of equality before the law and transforms the law from punishing acts to punishing people for using information technologies.

title: 【物理世界】量子霍爾效應（一）：塵埃中洗滌出的整數
text:
Even today, we cannot be certain that semiconductor materials are free of impurities, let alone 30 years ago. Therefore, when scientists discover such precise integers, they have most likely struck gold.

The story unfolding within the material can be imagined as follows: First, when the initial velocity of a charge is perpendicular to the magnetic field and there is no electric field, its motion is a circular motion. We can further imagine a flat plate of material with a magnetic field applied perpendicularly; the charges within it begin to rotate. At the quantum mechanical level, the entire material seems like an apartment building, with each circle representing a room inhabited by a charge. Nowadays, no apartment building has only one floor, and the same applies to materials in a magnetic field. L. D. Landau points out that these apartments also have many floors, called Landau levels. Charges on the same floor have the same energy; the higher the floor, the higher the energy (rent). The integers in the Hall measurement correspond to the number of Landau levels that are fully occupied.

At the level of abstract mathematics, the number of occupied Landau levels corresponds to the so-called "Chern Number." The numbers I mentioned at the beginning of the article are Chern numbers for a certain model. (This is why I felt relieved and went to sleep after seeing -1.000000000.) Although the origin of Chern numbers is not a simple mathematical concept, there is a simple image to understand why it is an integer: Imagine a fountain with a radius of 1 meter in the center of a courtyard. A passerby, let's call him Person A, starts from a certain point in the fountain, walks around the fountain an unknown number of times, and returns to the same point. He wants to know:

How many times did he walk around the fountain in total? This question obviously has many ways to answer (for example, by replaying the process on a monitor). One rather roundabout way is to have someone calculate the path Person A walked and then divide it by 2π. To the person being asked to calculate this, it's a complex integral calculation, but we, the observers, know it has a clear meaning: the answer is the number of laps, an integer! Chern numbers can be understood as a "number of laps" calculated in a relatively abstract space. This analogy also helps us understand that Chen Shu is a number related to "topology," which is absolutely related to whether there is a fountain in your yard, but has little to do with the details of your movements.

title: 半導體：原理與發展（一）歷史、物理原理與二極體
text:
We now know this is because silver sulfide is a semiconductor, and a characteristic of semiconductors is that their resistance decreases as temperature increases.

Before World War II, research into semiconductors had begun, but a breakthrough in semiconductor technology didn't occur until 1948 when three scientists at Bell Labs—William Shockley (1910-1989), John Bardeen (1908-1991), and Walter Houser Brattain (1902-1987)—invented the bipolar transistor. The semiconductor industry then began to flourish, and the three scientists were awarded the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physics. Today, semiconductors are found in home appliances, consumer electronics, automobiles, and electrical appliances.

In solid-state physics, a hole refers to the phenomenon where an electron loses an electron from a covalent bond, leaving a vacancy. Figure (a) above shows a silicon crystal structure doped with boron. We know that silicon is tetravalent, while boron is trivalent. Originally, all atoms are electrically neutral. Due to the small band gap in semiconductors, the energy required for electrons to be excited from the valence band to the conduction band is not high. When an electron is excited to the conduction band, it leaves a hole in the valence band. We can consider the movement of this hole as the movement of a positively charged particle. We call this type of semiconductor a p-type semiconductor, and the carrier (i.e., a freely moving charged particle) is called a hole.

Conversely, we can also dope silicon with pentavalent atoms, such as phosphorus. Since phosphorus has one more electron than electrically neutral silicon, the carrier is a negatively charged electron.

The simplest semiconductor application is the diode, which consists of an n-type semiconductor and a p-type semiconductor joined together. Because the n-type semiconductor has more electrons, some electrons at the junction migrate to fill holes in the p-type semiconductor, becoming positively charged at the n-type junction and negatively charged at the p-type junction (this can also be explained by diffusion: the n-type semiconductor has more electrons, and the p-type semiconductor has more holes, thus diffusing in opposite directions), as shown in the diagram below.

Due to this factor, according to Gauss's law (i.e., the net electric flux through any closed surface is equal to the net charge within that closed surface divided by the permittivity), an electric field is generated at this junction. This causes only immobile charged ions to remain near the pn junction, losing their electrical neutrality and becoming charged, forming a depletion layer. The depletion region has a built-in potential of approximately 0.7 V.

title: Tübinger Universität ausgezeichnet – Wie groß sind Computer in Zukunft?
text:
Tübingen (Germany), November 28, 2007 – On Tuesday, November 26, 2007, the University of Tübingen was awarded this year's IBM Shared University Research Grant in a ceremony, having been selected from among 50 research institutions worldwide.

Julian Würtenberger, Ministerial Director at the Ministry of Science, Research and the Arts, expressed his delight and pride on behalf of the state of Baden-Württemberg, noting that it demonstrated the excellence of research in Tübingen, as these so-called SUR grants had been awarded in the state before, but never at the level now granted to Tübingen. However, he stated that he was unable to provide a comparable state subsidy, which is not uncommon when acquiring third-party funding.

Martin Jetter, Chairman of the Management Board of IBM Germany GmbH, specifically recognized the Chair of Computer Engineering, headed by Professor Wolfgang Rosenstiel (pictured left), for its research on automated workload management. The Wilhelm Schickard Institute at the University of Tübingen received a new z9 series mainframe computer, costing nearly two million euros. The "z" stands for "zero downtime," ensuring continuous availability.

Herbert Kircher, Managing Director of IBM Germany Development GmbH and Head of the IBM Research Laboratory in Böblingen, then addressed the future of computing, explaining that the once-presumed-dead mainframes are experiencing a renaissance. This is due, in part, to savings of 80 to 90 percent in both space and energy consumption compared to the clusters of smaller computers that were considered the only viable option just ten years ago. He stated that 3,900 conventional servers could now be replaced by just 30 z-series computers. Given the high energy and maintenance costs, acquisition costs are now a secondary consideration when demand is high. Rosenstiel, who plans to establish a mainframe competence center with this new computer, was very impressed. “The mainframe computer donated by IBM not only creates ideal conditions for conducting hardware-related research in conjunction with System z systems, but also enables us to provide students with practical, application-oriented training on leading IBM mainframe technology,” said Professor Rosenstiel.

Kircher brought along another example of the development of computer technology: Just thirty years ago, the Cray-1, a so-called supercomputer, was the fastest and most powerful computer in the world – costing around $8.8 million at the time and requiring a large amount of space. Today's PlayStation 3 from Sony, with the Cell chip developed by IBM, has more than 10,000 times the performance for only about €500. How these small devices and processors can support the large computers in demanding tasks, such as controlling virtual worlds like Second Life, where, according to Kircher, everyone interested in computers should be represented, is currently being investigated – the future belongs to the combination of both, the “gameframe.”

title: Warnung vor Trojanischem Pferd im Internet
text:
Berlin (Germany), May 9, 2007 – Frank Ziemann, a former employee of the Technical University of Berlin, is warning on a website hosted by TU Berlin about an email threatening legal action against the recipient. The alleged sender is listed as the Rhineland-Palatinate State Criminal Police Office (LKA Rheinland-Pfalz). Several emails with varying wording are circulating. The email attached (see source link) is just one example.

Wikinews user JARU received an email in which the sender impersonates a lawyer and threatens legal action. A Trojan horse is attached to the email. When the attachment is run on a Microsoft Windows operating system, spyware is downloaded and installed on the computer. This happens in the background without the user's knowledge. Further information can be found in the source. It is strongly recommended to delete such emails without opening them. Operating systems other than Windows are not affected.

title: स्वच्छ भारत के लिये अपशिष्ट प्रबन्धन की नई तकनीक और प्रौद्योगिकी
text:
Under the Smart Cities and Swachh Bharat Mission, NITI Aayog recently formulated a three-year agenda to address the massive problem of municipal solid waste, setting a seven-year strategy and a fifteen-year vision. This initiative proposes waste-to-energy generation in metropolitan cities and composting in suburban and semi-urban areas. NITI Aayog has suggested establishing a Waste to Energy Corporation, which will establish waste-to-energy plants in 100 smart cities by 2019.

The Subgroup of Chief Ministers on the Swachh Bharat Mission recommended waste-to-energy plants in its 2015 report. With technological advancements, it is possible to generate 330 MW of electricity by 2018 and 511 MW by 2019. Currently, scientists and policymakers in the country are receiving mixed reactions to waste-to-energy generation. The waste problem is so profound that its combustion can lead to the release of toxic gases. These include rotten food, plastic, metal waste, and electronic waste, all of which pose numerous problems when burned in a plant.

Today, several waste-to-energy technologies have been developed that process waste to produce cleaner and more cost-effective energy, including landfill gas absorption, thermal pyrolysis, and plasma gasification. Older waste incineration plants emitted high-level pollutants, while new technologies like thermal pyrolysis and plasma gasification have significantly reduced the pollution concerns from combustion. NITI Aayog has also conducted a cost-benefit assessment of thermal pyrolysis and plasma gasification technologies. These are high-budget technologies that require state support. Producing compost and biogas from waste requires land, which can only be acquired with state support. There are also strong possibilities of employment generation in waste to energy production, in which National Skill Development Corporation can play an important role.

title: लिनेक्स की कहानी
text:
Linux is the most successful and popular open-source software. It is GPL-based and derived from Unix. Unix was developed in the 1960s by AT&T's Bell Labs. At that time, AT&T was a regulated monopoly, so it could not sell computer software. It gave it, along with the source code, unconditionally to governments and universities, allowing them to modify it if they wished. By the 1980s, Unix had become the most popular, powerful, and stable operating system, although by then many variations had already been produced.

One drawback of Unix was that it was difficult to understand and operate. Andy Tanenbaum, a professor of computer science at Amsterdam, wrote a program called Minix to support it. This also had some drawbacks. Linus Torvalds was a computer science student at the University of Helsinki, Finland. To overcome the shortcomings of Minix, he wrote a program that later became known as "Linus's Unix," or Linux for short. He posted its first kernel on the Internet in 1991. By then, Richard Stallman's GNU project had already begun. Linus Torvalds incorporated many of its programs into his Linux. Therefore, Richard Stallman suggested calling it GNU-Linux. However, this name, perhaps due to its length, failed to catch on. However, this does not mean that the GNU project did not play a role in Linux's success. Linux would not have been possible without the GNU project.

title: Da Loiano alle osservazioni spaziali
text:
Today, Loiano celebrates the thirtieth anniversary of the "G.D. Cassini" telescope, installed in 1975 at the university's astronomical observatory in the Apennine town. This telescope has a 152-cm diameter mirror.

The celebrations are part of the Cassinian Year celebrations, dedicated to the 17th-century astronomer Giovanni Domenico Cassini, after whom the Loiano telescope is named. In 2005, three events were linked to Cassini: the 350th anniversary of the San Petronio sundial he built, the 30th anniversary of the telescope named after him, and the Cassini-Huygens space mission.

Italian astronaut Umberto Guidoni, now a Member of the European Parliament, was invited as guest of honor. It was a welcome return, since, as he himself recounted, Guidoni spent a period of observations at the Loiano facility in 1978 while preparing his thesis. From there, his scientific and professional career began, leading him, in 1996, to participate in the Shuttle space mission. The title of the event, "From Loiano to Space Observations," was therefore apt.

Together with Flavio Fusi Pecci, director of the Bologna Astronomical Observatory, Guidoni gave a two-hour lecture to a young audience of several hundred middle and high school students, gathered in the Loiano sports hall. He showed and commented on the video of the mission, then answered numerous questions from the students, who were also interested in learning about the less scientific aspects of the mission, such as how astronauts wash themselves or what happens if the station toilet clogs.

Mayor Giovanni Maestrami presented Guidoni with a plaque commemorating today's event and Loiano's "observations under the stars" nearly thirty years ago. The celebrations continued with refreshments to toast the telescope's "first light." This afternoon and this evening, the facility will be open to the public for tours and astronomical observations.

title: Un’Analisi Multidimensionale della Ricerca Italiana nel Campo delle Digital Humanities e della Linguistica Computazionale
text: Digital Humanities and Computational Linguistics have common sources. We prefer to speak of sources rather than roots, because the multiple relationships these disciplines have woven over time are more reminiscent of a karst river than a tree. Indeed, there appears to have been no initial division into areas of expertise and subsequent branching into specific fields. Rather, like a karst river, the lines of inquiry have diverged several times and reconverged several times, perhaps after following underground paths based on humble laboratory work toward pilot projects or simple private communication around sketchy ideas, before regaining visibility in large-scale funded projects or in authoritative journals and conferences. If we accept Gibbon's framework, Computer Science and Humanities form the basis of Computational Linguistics, which over the years has been subdivided into Mathematical Computational Linguistics, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Computational Corpus Linguistics (CL), and, once again hybridizing with traditional Humanities, into Humanities Computing (HC). According to this framework, Digital Humanities (DH) would arise from the confluence of some NLP and CL fields with HC. But, beyond the birth certificates of monographs, journals, and international conferences that have established one or the other title, there is no doubt that topics in computational linguistics and topics in digital humanities have been addressed by the same authors, through the same publications, and at the same conferences since their inception. It is in this context that the idea arose to compare the performance of the annual conferences of the Association of Humanities and Digital Cultures (AIUCD) and the Italian Association of Computational Linguistics (AILC, which organizes the Italian Conference on Computational Linguistics, CLiC-it), over the four years (2014-2017) of their coexistence, for which contributions are available. Both are young associations, born at a time when Italian scholars with hybrid expertise in the humanities and sciences felt the need to assert their identity and disciplinary autonomy and to actively participate in their respective scientific communities, not only through their regular academic teaching and publishing activities, but also through organizing community events and participating in groups that find expression on social media. We believe this comparative study, which begins monitoring the conferences, can be useful for highlighting resources and practices shared by the two associations, thus strengthening synergy and resource sharing between the two communities or identifying discrepancies that could be addressed. After an overview of the state of the art in analyzing scientific communities from various perspectives, the methods and tools adopted to compare the information from the two four-yearly conference series are illustrated. The analyses conducted are then described in detail: these analyses focus on the communities (authors, genre, affiliation, joint participation in both conferences), the textual content of the articles (diachronic terminology extraction), and the citation entries (measurement of document categories, census of associations involved in the publication). The conclusions then formulate interpretative hypotheses that leave room for future research.

title: 病名アノテーションが付与された医療テキスト・コーパスの構築
text: The majority of the diverse data generated in medical settings (hereinafter referred to as medical data) is in natural language, and this situation is unlikely to change anytime soon. While the utilization of medical data can be applied to clinical practice or to academic research and policy, the latter—secondary use—is currently receiving much attention (Japan Science and Technology Agency Research and Development Strategy Center, 2017). Examples of medical data expected to be used for secondary purposes include health checkup data and medical fee data. Health checkup data is created during health examinations and consists of test names and test values. Because health checkup data involves a large number of participants and is collected centrally by organizations, it is often used as large-scale medical data. On the other hand, medical fee data is used to calculate medical expenses and is a coded representation of medical procedures. Because this data is collected and managed by the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare, it is also often used as large-scale medical data. Both types of data are structured data composed of numbers and codes, making them easy to handle by computers, but the lack of detailed information has limited their analysis. Therefore, attention is being drawn to the use of text-based medical data such as medical records, discharge summaries, and case reports, which contain more detailed information. Medical records are text documents written in hospitals when patients visit or during rounds upon admission, and they contain detailed patient information. Discharge summaries are information written at the time of discharge and are a summary of the medical records during hospitalization. Case reports are also summaries of admission, similar to discharge summaries, but are reported to academic societies. In addition, there is other text-based medical data within hospitals, and in this article, all of this text-based medical data will be referred to as electronic medical records.

title: 表層類似度に基づくセンター試験『国語』現代文傍線部問題ソルバー
text: In Japan, university entrance examinations are established as questions that test academic ability (intellectual ability and knowledge). An attempt to have a computer solve these university entrance examination questions was launched in 2011 as the National Institute of Informatics' Grand Challenge project, "Can a Robot Get into the University of Tokyo?" (Arai, Matsuzaki 2012). The interim goal of this project is to achieve a high score on the National Center Test for University Admissions by 2016, which would allow a student to advance to the second stage of the University of Tokyo's entrance examination. We are participating in this project and, since 2013, have been working on developing a system to solve the modern Japanese language questions in the National Center Test for University Admissions. As will be discussed in the next chapter, the majority of the questions in the modern Japanese language section of the National Center Test are what are called underlined section questions. As Funaguchi (Funaguchi 1997) implicitly points out, the key to "conquering" the modern Japanese language section of the National Center Test lies in "conquering" the underlined section questions. To our knowledge, there have been no previous attempts to use computers to solve underlined section problems in the Japanese language section of university entrance examinations. Therefore, it is unclear how difficult these types of problems are for computers. In such a situation, before trying various methods, it is important to first clarify what kind of accuracy can be obtained with a relatively simple method. This paper reports on the formulation, implementation, and evaluation of a solution method based on superficial clues, which was carried out based on this background. The performance of the system we implemented far exceeded our initial expectations, and was able to correctly solve about half of the underlined section problems in the "critical essays."

title: Зарождение и развитие искусственного интеллекта: характеристика исследовательских направлений
text:
AI research, as well as the understanding and application of intelligent machine theory, are being commercialized. AI is entering the global marketplace not only as a high-performance computer information system, but also as a global cultural idea, generating both new hopes and new fears.

By now, every specialist involved in computer technology has heard of AI. For the past 70 years, the world has been trying to use computer technology to solve problems that have persisted throughout human history—understanding and re-creating life, intelligence, and the ability to perceive, understand, and explain the world around us.

Perhaps this problem will be solved through the creation of AI, or perhaps AI, once it emerges, will solve this problem. However, it is safe to say that AI, like any scientific field, will only achieve productive development through the active, collaborative efforts of the global scientific community.

The AI ideas highlighted in this paper are important because they are fundamental. These are the first attempts to embody the capabilities of reason, recreated by individual technical systems, to be later integrated into a fully-fledged intelligent environment. On the other hand, these research areas were chosen for consideration primarily because they embody the most general ways of knowing and understanding the surrounding world – from the perception of reality (pattern recognition) to attempts to describe and adapt to the environment (translation, labyrinth search, play).

Thus, the concepts of learning, play, the search for something new, and its adaptation to improve human existence, defined during the cultural and historical development of society, have found their reflection in the theory and practice of AI. The components of the complex idea (artificial intelligence), implemented using computer tools and described in this article, have ushered in a new era of computer culture, which has completely encompassed most of our planet, defining the characteristics of today's historical era.

title: Стандартизация Умных городов, Интернета Вещей и Больших Данных. Соображения по практическому использованию в России
text: We think that standards and standardization have always existed. However, this is not the case. The history of this phenomenon is quite recent. In fact, organized standardization is just over 100 years old. In fact, the oldest institution of this kind in the world is the British Standards Institution (BSI), founded in 1901. However, the first national standard appeared at BSI only in 1903, or more accurately, was officially published [1]. The birth of a global standardization system is quite recent history – in 1946, the International Organization for Standardization, or ISO, was created. International technology committees such as IEEE are even younger. However, despite their relative youth, today standards and the standardization process itself have become one of the main factors contributing to global development and the globalization of markets and industries, largely determining the success of various endeavors in business and even politics. Much can be said about standards themselves, but we will try to limit ourselves to brief conceptual questions. What is standardized is what will be applied on a mass and collective basis, so that all participants in the process have the same concepts and values for characteristics on a given subject. How did this typically happen in the past? Initially, company or association standards emerged; then, with overwhelming commercial success, they became national standards, and then, with the participation of representatives from various countries participating in international standardization organizations, they became international standards. Of course, there are other ways to disseminate standards—for example, localizing one country's standards for another or including one country in another country's roadmap for developing these documents. And in the 21st century, when the need to adopt new technical regulations or standards often determines the success of certain economic decisions, such alternative methods of standard adoption are increasingly being used. Typically, in both cases, the success of a given standard's application or its "popularity" determines everything. Adopted international standards are then localized in each country, referencing international numbering. This, in principle, facilitates the transfer of proven solutions and creates the conditions for an international division of labor.

title: Diagnóstico de fallas con redes neuronales. Parte 1: Reconocimiento de trayectorias
text: The research aimed to formulate a method for designing a fault diagnosis system for chemical plants using artificial neural networks. Fault diagnosis aims to identify the fault affecting a given process by analyzing the signals provided by the process sensors. Neural networks are mathematical models that attempt to replicate the cognitive activity of the human brain. They are characterized by their structure and the learning method used. The fault diagnosis problem is approached from the perspective of identifying the trajectories (temporal sequences of data) that describe the process variables when affected by a fault. Once these trajectories are recognized, the associated fault will be identified. The theoretical framework recommends an optimized structure and training method for the neural networks to be used. Both the proposed structure and training method were evaluated by conducting comparative studies with traditional structures and training methods. The results obtained demonstrated the superiority of the neural networks designed and trained using the method proposed in this work. Except in simple processes, fault diagnosis is more complex than path recognition because each fault can generate an infinite set of paths (flows). For this reason, the principles established in this work are used in Part II, where the analysis is extended to flow recognition.

title: Desarrollo de un modelo de redes neuronales artificiales para predecir la resistencia a la compresión y la resistividad eléctrica del concreto
text: Throughout history, and parallel to the development of civilization, humankind has been able to conceptualize nature, abstracting it through models that have allowed us to understand and control it. In this sense, the modeling of concrete in its fresh and hardened states using theoretical and mathematical tools is an area that has been growing in recent years. Currently, the computing power offered by personal computers has made it possible to perform tasks that were unthinkable not long ago. Among the artificial intelligence techniques that have become most widespread and applied in the field of materials science is that known as artificial neural networks. Their academic, research, and industrial relevance can be demonstrated by the large number of publications in the last ten years. During this time, artificial neural networks have been applied to the modeling of a significant number of civil engineering problems with a reasonable degree of success. The most important applications have been in the fields of structural damage detection, identification of structural systems, modeling of material behavior, structural optimization, structural control, groundwater monitoring, prediction of foundation settlements, and concrete mix design (Graham et al., 2005). A neuron within a living organism has the function of controlling some of the basic biological functions, as well as the organism's state and behavior with respect to its environment. The basic operation of biological neural networks is an analogous transformation of their input signals. They generally correspond to systems of simple, highly interconnected elements. The ability of neurons to develop complex processes results from abundant feedback loops along with nonlinearities in the process elements. A neuron consists of a more or less spherical cell body from which a main branch, known as the axon, and several shorter branches called dendrites emerge. Neurons differ from other living cells in their ability to communicate. They receive input signals that are combined, analyzed, and integrated by the cell body, from which output signals are emitted and transmitted to other neurons as information. An artificial neural network is a computational model that, due to its architecture, attempts to mimic the behavioral relationships of the brain. It consists of a limited number of interconnected elements (neurons) distributed across an input layer, one or more hidden layers, and an output layer. The layers and neurons are interconnected, as shown in Figure 3.

title: Kiswahili katika Kufundishia TEHAMA katika Shule za Msingi nchini Tanzania: Umuhimu na Changamoto zake
text:
Lack of teaching aids and materials for learning and teaching ICT is another obstacle. Lack of laboratories and equipment such as computers is a chronic problem that plagues many primary schools in Africa, especially in rural areas. This situation hinders the practical teaching of the subject. Teachers end up giving long, boring explanations and using incomprehensible drawings on the board. However, in order to teach ICT effectively, there is a need to fully involve students in various practical training using computers installed with appropriate software in the Kiswahili language. This will only be possible when deliberate steps are taken to build computer laboratories in all schools in the country.

Lack of textbooks and supplementary books written in Kiswahili is another obstacle to the use of Kiswahili for teaching. Although the books available in schools are few or non-existent, these books do not meet the needs of the subject of ICT. In general, many science and technology books are written in foreign languages that are not familiar to many people, especially those specializing in information and communication technology. In addition, there are few articles, blogs and websites written in Swahili. In this situation, many students and people who want to learn computers in Swahili are denied this opportunity.

Despite the importance of the subject of ICT in today’s world, many teachers in rural areas find it difficult to teach ICT subjects such as computers due to the fact that teachers themselves have either never used computers or have very limited knowledge. In the summary of the subject of ICT for grade seven, topics such as ‘computer local area network’, ‘internet network’, ‘using websites’ and ‘meaning of e-mail’ are listed (Ministry of Education and Vocational Training, 2005). Many teachers in rural areas do not understand e-mail, they only hear about it in the media. Expecting such teachers to teach ICT to students is unrealistic.

title: Makala za Kuchochea Utafiti: Kiswahili na Teknolojia ya Habari
text:
The work of compiling computer terminology and related fields is still very much needed. This is because the work that has been done is very little. For example, Chuwa (1991:47) in his work on computers has only one page with 21 terms for “Word Perfect (WP) 5” and “DOS”. This means that even if these terms have spread and been accepted, they are still too few for this field. In addition, many other people are still creating terms that perhaps also need to be examined for their suitability. But the question can still be asked by some people as to whether there is a need for these terms, especially considering that the use of computers is taught to the participants in the English language system. Regarding such a question, our opinion is that we also still have a responsibility to give Kiswahili the opportunity to take any steps forward.

In many parts of the world, especially where the English language is spoken, computers have an operating system that provides instructions and commands as well as the results (and/or responses) of these instructions and commands in the English language. But usually these computers also have operating systems that do the same things in some of the other major languages in the world. Until now, the operating system in a computer that provides instructions and commands in the Swahili language has not been very well developed.

title: Progress in Play: Board Games and the Meaning of History
text:
Ten thousand years ago, in the Neolithic period, before human beings began making pottery, we were playing games on flat stone boards drilled with two or more rows of holes. By the Early Dynastic Period in Ancient Egypt, three millennia later, board games were already represented in hieroglyphs. And on the wall of Nefertari’s tomb, built in the twelfth or thirteenth century BCE, someone painted the queen playing Senet, one of three Ancient Egyptian board games whose pieces have come down to us, along with Mehen and Hounds and Jackals.

The ancient Greeks, for their part, had Tabula, an ancestor of backgammon; the Romans added Latrones, an ancestor of chess. All across the ancient Near East, people played the Game of Twenty Squares, while in ancient China they played Liubo and in ancient India Moksha Patam, which was rechristened Snakes and Ladders when colonials imported it to Britain in the Victorian era. Wherever there has been civilization, strange to say, there have been games played on boards.

Until about the seventeenth century, these games tended to be traditional folk inventions that could not be traced back to a maker. Their boards were also relatively abstract, consisting of squares, triangles, spirals, or holes. With the advent of the Enlightenment and the rise of capitalism, however, the board games of Europe — like so much else on the continent — began to change. By the end of the eighteenth century, games were being produced for the marketplace promoting everything from ferry rides to colonial conquest. To appeal to consumers (a category of persons that had not previously existed), these games were made to be played on boards printed with pictures that represented specific places, people, and things.

title: Music Manuscripts from the 17th and 18th Centuries in the British Library
text:
Ever since the earliest methods of notating music were devised, composers and scribes have written out music by hand — on vellum in the medieval period and subsequently on paper. (Only now is this beginning to change, with the advent of computer programs for music notation.) Even after the perfecting of music printing techniques in the 16th century, when music was printed using moveable type and later by engraving, and the burgeoning of a trade in music publishing, much music continued to be written out by hand and circulated in manuscript. Printing music was expensive, time-consuming and complex; copying out music by hand could be done relatively cheaply and quickly, especially when a few copies only of a particular composition were needed.

In the 17th and 18th centuries, music was written out in manuscript for several purposes. These included the creation of ‘master copies’ from which further handwritten copies could be made when required, the provision of musicians’ parts for use in performance and the commercial and non-commercial dissemination of musical works. Many publishers of printed music also sold manuscript music. With musical genres for which the market in scores was likely to be small (opera, for example), producing manuscripts in small quantities was more cost-effective than setting up a print run.
